Portal 2 draws from the award-winning formula of innovative gameplay, story, and music that earned the original Portal over 70 industry accolades and created a cult following.
The single-player portion of Portal 2 introduces a cast of dynamic new characters, a host of fresh puzzle elements, and a much larger set of devious test chambers. Players will explore never-before-seen areas of the Aperture Science Labs and be reunited with GLaDOS, the occasionally murderous computer companion who guided them through the original game.
The game’s two-player cooperative mode features its own entirely separate campaign with a unique story, test chambers, and two new player characters. This new mode forces players to reconsider everything they thought they knew about portals. Success will require them to not just act cooperatively, but to think cooperatively.

TLDR at the end, for those that are just skimming through reviews.
Having played since before TX-1 (mk 11) came out, I can definitely say I had a good time playing Robocraft. I've endured all the new updates, and I say endured because some of them have been terrible. I can't find myself to play anymore after my robots took some nerfs. An example of this is the release of 'mech' legs, which are more durable than the older 'walker' legs. Essentially, walker legs have been made almost obsolete, but I know other designs are availble for me to use. Tank tracks took another hit too. Steering became a whole lot less responsive, and I know and have confirmed lag isn't the issue. Tanks have simply been made terrible. The recent updates aren't the only reason I stopped playing.
The community. My God. In almost every game I look at my teammates and shake my head in dissapointment. Medics healing rail snipers in the middle of a fight. Gunner tanks so busy trying to shoot down a plane that they don't realise another gunner is tearing them apart. Some of them are toxic too. I remember in multiple matches I asked the medics to focus their healing on the tanks, (The scoreboard clearly showed the tanks were not only taking but also dealing all the damage), only to cop some verbal abuse from my team members who fail to acknowledge who is contributing the most to the team. Initially I wanted to climb to the higher ranks in hopes of playing with people that knew how to play. The only difference I found is that Robocraft veterans are more toxic than the newer players. Those that aren't toxic agree that Robocraft is becoming a lot worse than what is used to be.
TLDR
If you're planning on picking up the game, just know:
Freejam, the game developers of Robocraft, is changing the game too much in negative ways.

Building, improving, and driving your vehicle is a load of fun. Unfortunately, the fun is hindered by a leveling system which determines the quality and quantity of your vehicle's parts. Balance isn't just an afterthought as a consequence of open-ended construction, it's discarded as a concept entirely.
This might work in a small PvP deathmatch-type game, or even a PvE MMO. Unfortunately, this is a team-based shooter. Which team wins depends entirely on which has the highest level players.
The fun of designing a vehicle quickly degrades into grinding for more and better parts, with the matches serving more as a way to earn levels and points than their own form of entertainment.

Just take a quick look at the overall rating. Not only is it 98%, but that makes it one of the highest rated games on Steam, above Half Life 2 and many others. If you don't like puzzle games, you might still enjoy Portal 2. The humor makes you want to keep playing. Also, this game is like Easter in terms of easter eggs. There's so many that it's kind of scary. There are even easter eggs inside of easter eggs. If you haven't played the first Portal, I recommend that you play that first. Also, if you have, and didn't enjoy it, you might want to wait for a sale to buy this game if you plan on buying it.
Portal 2 is well written, and features the voice talent of J.K. Simmons (Peter Parker's boss, and now Comissioner Gordon!) as Cave Johnson. The addition of gels was a great idea, because it adds more variety to the gameplay. Also, Custom Levels are extremely easy to make, and are fun to play. Co-op levels really do require full cooperation and a headset. It's nearly impossible to communicate without one.
With all this being said, Portal 2 is a great puzzle game. This may surprise you, but if you dig deep into the lore of this game and pay really close attention to every detail, Portal 2 is a really creepy game. I don't want to spoil it for anyone, so I'll just say that it's all very subtle and ambiguous. If you do plan on getting into the lore of Aperture Science, I recommend you read the comic (I forgot the name) and watch a lot of YouTube videos.
In conclusion, Portal 2 is one of the greatest modern games, no, one of the greatest games ever, and can be enjoyed by a wide variety of people. I hope that if you buy Portal 2 you enjoy it as much as I did. (I played and beat it on Xbox 360 and here on Steam)
P.S. If you're interested in the darker side of Portal 2, there are quite a few videos discussing it, but here are the two best ones:
RustyMolboxer- Darker Side of the Disc
TheStickyPaddle-Creepy Gaming

So where do I start? Well I"ve been playing for over 2000 hours, I'm a pilot seat and Mega bot Veteran (more on that later)
This game at it's core is pretty simple. You build a bot from block just like in Space Engineers or From the Dephts and you take to battle, to build you have a CPU limit (each block uses 1 CPU, and weapons and such have different values. Some years ago the limit for regular bots was 1515, noawaday is 2000. A good upgrade.
2 years ago the game was great because we had:
1- A pilot seat, the center of the bot, you would build your bot around and you had to protect it. If the pilot seat was hit you were dead.
2- Megabots - Huge bots that could use up to 7500 CPU, they were the end game. You went from Tier 1 to Tier 10 hoping to build the best mega bot and take it to the pit (a Free for All game mode, where megabots would fight megabots ) although this game mode was pure cancer, (weak megas would team up to kill the strong one or people would abuse the pit to make money at your expense, there should have been a Team Deathmatch mode for Megabots, 5x5 for example).
3- Tiers and a Tech Tree.
4- RP, the in game currency, you would win it after a match, and each robot would get a first win bonus.
All those 4 things were removed from the game, after hours building megas and unlocking itens Freejam (the developer) just removed then saying the game was still in alpha (although people were paying for custom itens, garage slots and such ) and After a match you don't get RP (money) anymore you get crates with parts you have to sell to get another, but the sell value is less than 50% of the part value if you don't have premium.
That means eternal grinding to build anything.
Ohh and the maps! The maps were quite big, but Freejam decided (despite the player base saying no) to make the maps really small, we also only have 4 or 6 maps, dont quite remember cause they all look the same. After almost 4 years, They can't even make good new content for the game.
They also added an energy system that's simply put crazy. You would think that the more blocks you have, the more energy you can store. Well with Robocraft it's just the opposite. Now if you build using the 2000 CPU limit, you may have 3 or 5 seconds of energy to fire.
That means the game is now about building tiny bots (1000 CPU or less) and jumping people. Real Building is gone from the game, you can just build a BORG cube and it's all the same, because you have no pilot seat to protect.
Megabots are now back into the game, with 10000 CPU, but they can only be used in a custom game mode set up by the player who has to invite people to it, but you earn no points whatsoever and there
And now they finally screwed the game for good.
After the awful Return of The Megabot Update (which gave a 10000 useless CPU monster) they gave us the aerofoils update, where
1- Wings now have VTOL but you can't do a loop or rolls, planes are now basically on rails.
2- All movement parts were affected and don't work as they should anymore.
The game is just becoming more and more like Gear Up, even Crossout has more depth to build now than Robocraft.
Ohh and let me just warning you about the mega toxic community (not all of then, but the forum trolls are terrible, and in game it's even worst.). People just abuse and use the same designs over and over again just to win. There's no fun at all.
if you are curious give it a go, but don't get your hopes up, Robocraft is dead, the player base went from 20k people daily to 4k.
TO sum it up the problems with the game
1- Building its pointless
2- Planes are like cars drifting in the sky. Basically on rails
3- After a match you don't get RP (money) you get crates with parts you have to sell to get another, but the sell value is less than 50% of the part value if you don't have premium
4- Maps are small, boring and just the same for the last 3-4 years.
5- Toxic community.
6- No rewards, no tech tree. No tiers or ranks (there's a level that means nothing).
7- After 3 years the game has no useful in-game chat, you can't click a players name, you can't batch remove or add. There's no chatroom browser or anything like it. Games from 10 years ago had more resources than robocraft.
8 - No game browser(like battlefield) just Quick match were teams are poorly balanced.
9 - THe game feels like is just bad programmed, all functions barely work and are poorly done. Feels like the team at Freejam has no experience at all.
10- No reconnect function, and if a player disconnects during the loading screen of a match you need to alt+F4 to leave the game.
11- No point in building since flying boxes and drones are the thing in the game (drones are flyers with no wings just thrusters ).
Take a look cause it's free, but dont get too much into the game, at least no until they restore all they screw up.

Robocraft is an online third-person vehicle shooter game set on fictional areas of different planets where players construct machines that are used to fight with others in battles. It is currently an open-alpha game, and is being developed and published by the indie video game developer Freejam Games based in the United Kingdom. The game features contained garages in which players can build various functional vehicles with basic block-based parts (such as cubes and wheels) along with weapons that can be used for combat. The initial alpha build was released in March 2013, featuring a single-player building and test mode. In April 2013, Freejam Games released multiplayer combat, which is now the core content of the game. Content updates and bug fixes for the game are released a few times each month. On April 14, 2014, the company revealed that Robocraft had gained over 300,000 players in a few months; the game continues to attract many players, notably, international players from non-English speaking countries.

This review is quite long (it turned into a rant), but feel free to skim it over.
Just... why? Why would you make it so you need 30 MILLION (That's right: 30,000,000) robot ranking to even enter other game modes? It makes zero sense, the tier system was fine.
If the point of the game is to build cool robots, why is there an option to buy them? This completely kill the whole 'build insane robots' and creativity part of the game.
The controls for this game, as well as the various options for the movement of your vehicle, used to be quite tight. Now they all mostly control like wet noodles.
Wheels used to control great, now they suck. They can barely handle speed, they have horrible handling, and control like wet noodles. You'll probably even flip over sometimes... on a flat surface. Even more pathetic when your vehicle has rockets.
Aerofoils and Hovers are also incredibly sluggish and control like wet noodles.
Rotors are pathetic. Not only are they sluggish and wet noodle-esque, but they also lack roll.  The rotors have pitch and yaw, but no roll. How do you expect me to control a helicopter when it's missing a primary method of control?
Rockets are a joke now. The momentum they now gave is hilariously bad, which is a huge detriment for flying and fast moving vehicles.
If you want to go anywhere, you're best off using Tank Treads or Walker Legs, which both have great handling, tight controls, and decent speed. Even Skis are better than half of the other movement options.
These changes blow.  The overclocking system is terrible and should've never been implemented. It makes already hard to control vehicles even more wet noodle like.
The new game modes are nice, but what it ruins it is the prevalent amount of over-tiered vehicles and the new, horrible, ranking system.  As far as I'm concerned, before your rank was determined via your profile level and Tier placement. Now it's a tier placement based on how good your vehicle is in terms of 1,000's of point.
I feel like I'm not the only one who'd prefer the old ranking system back.
The balancing in this game is a huge joke. Plasma and Rail guns are okay, melee is a joke, but they are essentially useless against SMG's. SMG's are still stupidly overpowered, can still snipe, damage travel, etc.
There's practically no point in choosing anything else, because SMG's are just that good.  What the balancing should be is a system like 'Rock, Paper, Scissors', where each weapon type is effective against one another, but is also ineffective against one another.
---> SMG: Good against Melee, Bad against Plasma.
---> Plasma: Good against SMG, Bad against Rail.
---> Rail: Good against SMG and Plasma, but bad against Rail and Melee.
---> Melee: Good against Rail and Melee, Bad against SMG and Plasma.
But in reality, it isn't like this at all.
For a game that wants to promote 'building insane robots', there is a huge lack of it ingame. Most of the robo's you'll find in your matches are either gunbeds or store bought, but it's mostly going to be gunbeds.
The biggest problem with gunbeds, is that they are purely uncreative. Like net-decking in Hearthstone (especially when people just net-deck for the meta and don't know how to play the deck they've chosen), everyone copies or has similair gunbed designs.  They're all square or flat. They all have a bllion guns on them.
It's a shame, because this game does have a lot of creative player potential, but its sadly thwarted by both the store, shameless copying of gunbed designs, and a lack of re-enforcement from the DEV's.
I may be looking at this with rose-tinted glasses, but the game was truly that much better back then. The DEV's seemingly don't care about half the issues in this game, especially balancing, ranking, and bugs, and I've only heard about the DEV's being non-community orientated either.
With the direction the game is taking, I wouldn't be suprised to see it dead in a few years.

A somewhat half hearted attempt by valve to capture the Candy Crush crowd, Portal 2 exemplifies the desperation to capture this growing mobile phone audience. In exchange for Candy Crush's brilliant and vibrant color, the laboratories of Aperture Science are a lugubrious, drab greyish white. The charm that King's mobile title exudes at every corner is lacking in Valve's poor imitation. The illustrious guide, Mr. Toffee, whose physiognomy personifies joy is discarded in exchange for a heartless, inhuman machine. The delightful player character, Tiffi, is replaced by a voiceless, utterly uninteresting test subject. With no character development whatsoever, Portal 2 fails to make the player become invested in the outcome of the characters, one of the main reasons Candy Crush was so well received. The game mechanics of Portal 2 have been watered down in order to appeal to toddlers. The once mentally intensive act of matching varieties of candy has been replaced with generating portals to the end of the levels. No skill is required as one may just create a portal at any moment to the end of the game. Overall Valve's attempt to cash in on the success of puzzle games lacks all that made Candy Crush so fantastic, including the ability to play on the go. Why a puzzle game such as this lacks mobile phone functionality is an enigma to me.
Overall I give this game a 2/10.
As others have suggested, play Candy Crush instead.

A somewhat half hearted attempt by valve to capture the Candy Crush crowd, Portal 2 exemplifies the desperation to capture this growing mobile phone audience. In exchange for Candy Crush's brilliant and vibrant color, the laboratories of Aperture Science are a lugubrious, drab greyish white. The charm that King's mobile title exudes at every corner is lacking in Valve's poor imitation. The illustrious guide, Mr. Toffee, whose physiognomy personifies joy is discarded in exchange for a heartless, inhuman machine. The delightful player character, Tiffi, is replaced by a voiceless, utterly uninteresting test subject. With no character development whatsoever, Portal 2 fails to make the player become invested in the outcome of the characters, one of the main reasons Candy Crush was so well received. The game mechanics of Portal 2 have been watered down in order to appeal to toddlers. The once mentally intensive act of matching varieties of candy has been replaced with generating portals to the end of the levels. No skill is required as one may just create a portal at any moment to the end of the game. Overall Valve's attempt to cash in on the success of puzzle games lacks all that made Candy Crush so fantastic, including the ability to play on the go. Why a puzzle game such as this lacks mobile phone functionality is an enigma to me.
Overall I give this game a 2/10.
As others have suggested, play Candy Crush instead.

This game is fun, don't get me wrong here, but it needs improvment. I was what used to be tier 7 when Robocraft Unleashed came out. I was level 74, which is high for a tier 7 or even 8. Then I saw there was a new update. I got it expecting something cool and new, only to find the tiers which I loved -because it made the game fairly matched in battles, and gave me a goal to achive in ranking up- were gone. Along with the tiers were the Tech Tokens, which I thought was a good idea and enjoyed having to earn. Since there were no more Tech Tokens, I saw that you had to level up to unlock new items. This made me mad because I had tier 8 items (or as the game now calls them Mark 8 items). Then after 3 days of the new update, I logged on and saw a level up screen, confused I clicked ok and saw i was level 99.  When i saw i was level 99 I was ticked and hoped it was a glitch that would go away if i rebooted, then the game crashed ,-level 99 unlocking all but 2 items-. Then wheni logged back on, I was level 100 and angrier then any hornet you have ever seen, so I played for a week or 2 then quit because it was no fun anymore. I had put Mark 10 SMG's ( the machine guns of the game ) on my Mark 7 bot, just for laughs. I logged back a week or so ago (after months of inactivity) and saw I couldn't play Battle Arena mode, which was my favorite. I was ticked, because it required a bot of 30 million Robo Ranking ( which comes form the items on your bot ), and my highest was 14 million. I then noticed Mech Legs, and insatly was distraced form my anger, only to find out that they cost so much that getting 2 for a basic mech, cost as much as about 3 or 4 of the same mark wheels. I saved and on a small budget made a mark 4 mech, and it was fun as heck. I continued to upgrade it to mark 5, and now I'm working on a mark 7 mech. I made a Medic Helicopter, because used too that was the best way to make money on this game. I joined a match and realized my 800+ thousand Robo Cash ( which is a lot to build a mark 8 bot) was pretty much obselite, because everyone was a medic with 1 or 2 SMG's a game, and one most the time being a plane. I still use it, because when I win I can get anywhere from 45k to 75k Robo Cash. When I said everyone wanted to be a medic I didn't mean they were good medics, because in most mark7-8 matches the medic are small with 1 or 2 guns that are mark 6 (which are the lowest you can buy) and don't heal jack squat. The meaning of this whole review is to say that old is never obselite, when it worked amazingly in the past. This game has maby 1 half of what it had when there were still tiers and Tech Tokens, so bring them back, its way more fun, challenging, and evenly matched then. If this game doesn't improve my January 1st 2016, I might quit. It's not definate but a probablity, however if tiers and Tech Tokens come back ther is a 99% chance I will stay and play on this one great, now decent game.

Good: Inspires creativity with builds, allowing you to virtually build anything you want (with a block limit of course).
Level system allows users a gentle introduction to the game whilst gradually bringing new pieces into the creator's hands later on.
Game is balanced for the most part, with all three weapon types having their own playstyles that fit well with multiple movement types.
Bad: Only three types of weapons available, and the game doesn't allow them to be mix matched together.
For people who are experienced or good at the game, the leveling up still feels extremely slow, even with getting three to five kills on average per game.
The ability to make some builds with overpowered parts and still place the player in lower tiers is still present.
The game lags in general, usually during the most opportune times as well. (I run the system on fastest and highest graphic settings and there is no difference in the lag).
Overall: Since it's a free game, yes I do reccomend it. Give it a try and see if you like it. There are some builds that are just stupid overpowered, but it seems like there are still a good amount of people who enjoy just making neat looking builds over something that performs well. Robocraft. It was once a great game for me and my friends.
Here's the story:
I was board one day and was searching youtube for free-to-play games. I found some vids about "Robocraft" some new MMO that was said to be a combination of "World of Tanks" and "Minecraft", two of my favorite games. I download it. And the begining battles were fun, you could build whatever you want, and seemingly do fairly well.
However, as the tiers progress, me and my friends reailzied that it became extremly grindy. Cash for new weapons could be upwords of 34,000 RP (which is the name of the in-game cash system). When you earn a fair 10,000 RP a game, even if you do poorly, that's good. However, that is far from true (you'll earn about 10,000 RP if you buy a premium account) . You can only earn about maybe 5k if you do "ok" in a match. But if you do poorly, then you're looking at about 1-2k - sometimes less, and that 34,000 (or so) RP is only for a single weapon, not a cluster. Also, if you want to build a good robot, expect to poor in at least 500,000 RP or more. If the weapons weren't bad enough, a single high tiered armor cube (a single one!) could cost upwords of 1000-2500 RP. If I wanted to build a robot that had 200 cubes total (which isn't that big) at 1,700 RP a block, I'm going to have to fork out 340,000 RP. 200 armor cubes by-the-way will not do you much in the higher tiers. And if you're not that good with vehicular combat  games, then you're grinding for at least a few weeks. Even worse, if I wanted to build a bot with only 200 armor cubes at tier 8 (which I think cost about 2515 RP, could be wrong though so forgive me if I am) I am going to have to grind a staggering 503,000, which is quite ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for just 200 cubes.
Perhaps another very stupid problem that I have found in this game that the SMG guns are way too overpowered. You can build a heavily armored bot, plazma sheilds, etc. only to watch it get mauled to bits by another player with SMGs. They need a heavy nerfing if they want the game to be fun.  The next issue, after me and my friends left the game for a few months, we desiced to return to it only to find everything has drastically changed. The new tiering system is a joke compaired to the older one. The leveling system is strange. All in all, I think this game is heading south when it comes to playability. But hey, give it a shot. I'll bet that you will rage quit in 2-3 games when you reach tier 4-6 watching your beautiful built realistic robot, get mauled to death by a blob with SMGs. Afterall, they nerfed the Plasma and Railguns by adding the Plazma sheilds (which block some damage), and contrary to player opinion, I have found that they are useless against SMGs due to the rappid fire of the SMGs.
Message to the Devs (if they are reading this). These are only my opinions, but I am sure many other players agree. You need to buff the cash making so even a player who does very poorly in a game can earn at least 5-7,000 RP, in order to build a decent bot. The SMGs need to be nerfed as they are way to overpowered. And if you don't want to nerf (downgrade) the SMGs, then make the angled/triangular armor cubes bounce SMG shells like it would in real life.
Sidenote: I am not going to bother putting my rant and review in spell-checker, so ignor any mispellings. I have better things to do then to cater to the grammer police (lol).

Robocraft is an online MMO where you battle in 10v10 arenas. But the one difference to the game is the fact that YOU make the robots you fight with. Anything from flying bombers, to walking snipers, to hovering battle cruisers, what you can build is up to you. Another thing I like about the game, and others may not, is the fact that you have to buy all the weapons you use. It gives the game a more real feeling instead of just unlocking new weapons, you have to actually buy them like you would in real life. But don't worry, acquiring funds is as easy as shooting down someone in a online battle. With the recent gamemode releases, the playing experience has gotten better then ever. These include: Deathmatch, team vs. team, Arena mode, a sort of strong vs. weak, and even a practice mode to test your newfangled creation. Now, even though there is a lot of amazing aspects to this game, there are a few negative ones. Firstly, the shortage of different maps has given the game a repetitive feel that kind of drags it out, though this can be remedied by some new maps. Secondly, the physics engine is a little bit off in the fact that my sniper tank is able to climb shear cliffs (and proceed to snipe people from there). A little attention to detail here may smooth out a few of those glitches. Other then that, this game is a joy to play. I can totally say that this game is worth every dollar I didn't pay for it.

This game is actually pretty enjoyable, I like how creative you can get with the vehicles and how that reflects on the play style. I like games generally where you roll around and blast♥♥♥♥♥♥with cannons or whatever. I was a big fan of the game Bandits : Phoenix Rising which was a vehicle combat game with a lot of customization when it came to weapons. Robocraft brought back memories of playing this game but in a completely different game style, and altered gameplay.
In Robocraft you are in space and you are battling other robots on alien planets in custom built vehicles. It's pretty awesome.
Lots of walkers and tanks moving about. for instance earlier today I saw what looked like an AT-AT albeit nowhere near as imposing, fighting on my team. I believe in the same game there was someone in a dino-bot.
Robocraft is truly the next generation of games, with its Minecraft-style block building demonstrating primitive emergent gameplay common across many titles today eg Fallout 4. This game evolved from a whole genere of games where often you build buildings and modify worlds as you like into a distilled application of this way of playing into a combat game where man-made machines evolve and destroy each other ad infinitum.
There are many tactical possibilities and this seems like a game where it pays to play as a team. The combat is quite fun, I particularly like the plasma cannon and look forward to using the railgun on my Panzer. I do wish there were more guns though like rockets (katyusha anyone?) or mortars or howitzers, miniguns and flame or plasna throwers, lasers, with turret versions. That would own.
The freemium system is pretty fair but the unlock tree could use a research mechanic where you spend money or points on unlocking new parts as well, could lead to more specialization in vehicles determining gameplay.
There is a lot that could be done with this kind of game. More players per battle would be a start. More different levels of players playing together en masse.
Overall I dig it, I'll probably sink a few hours in in the future.

This is one of those games that I keep going back and forth as to whether or not I like it. It has lots of things I really like, but it has a few things that are absolutely annoying. I like being able to build a unique robot, throw it in battle, improve the weaknesses, and so forth. Great. The parts I don't like, is the game modes and ranking system. Both of which used to be much much better.
To give you and idea as to how it used to be, robots were divided by "Tiers" ranging 1-10 and Mega. You had a certain ranking to stay within in order to compete in a tier. The better the parts you add, the higher your ranking. There were also levels, which like other games was based off of "experience". Cpu is another thing you had to watch. The higher your level the more cpu your bot could have. Which means bigger, better bots. It was pretty hard to hit that limit due to the fact that you would cross the ranking line before you ran out of cpu.
Game modes consisted of team deathmatch, a "mega bot battle", and one that resembled Battlefield. The last mode being the most fun and profitable. I also want to mention that they have upgrades that you could get to make your bot better, such as wheels, guns, and armor.  You unlocked the tech with points that you would get from battles in order to purchase them.
I really liked this system, I felt like I was earning my way to the top. But after a few updates the game has completly changed, and in my opinion, not for the better. They basically eliminated tiers. You can purchase different Tier parts, but there isn't any incentive to rise up traditionally. Now it's save up for the biggest guns you can have and power your way to the top. Which is easier to do now that the tech tree auto unlocks tech depending on your level. Another part of the game that I felt was fulfilling. To make matters worse, they now only allow robots with at least 30million ranking to play the "battlefield" match. A level 1 bot was ranked at about 200, to give you an idea as to how crazy that is. Team deathmatch. You have your bot ready, select the game mode, wait 30 seconds or so to get in a match, 30-40 seconds for the game to load and have it count from 10 to 0, drive another 30 seconds till you hit conflict, end up dying... wait... thats it? One life. No respawn? Where is the fun in that. So what is the objective? Eliminate the other team or sit on their spawn point trying to figure out which bar at the top of the screen corresponds to what you are doing. If you are going to have only one life, at least make it like Counter-Strike where there are at least multiple rounds. It seems rather lame to just quit because you died.
Moral of the story, it was really fun before, now its just simply fun. Would I recommend it? Yes, because it is free. Would I recommend it if it cost more than $5? No. Not unless they changed their system back to the way they had it.

At the time of writing, Robocraft is in the middle of a long, slow death.
This game had a lot of potential, and still might be great game in the future. I might check back in 2020 when the devs put a bit more thought and care into what they do. Here we have an "early access game" that probably already has a pretty steady revenue stream. So, let's all stop calling it "alpha" or "early access" or whatever else and just admit that it is in a strange game limbo.
The gamelpay is fun enough, but doesn't hold the attention for the casual player for too long. This has partly to do with the lack of great content one would expect on a regular basis from an alpha game. The other major factor is the terrible playerbase. Due to the game having no tutorial whatsoever, it can be incredibly punishing to new players. The high skill ceiling and steep learning curve make this a perfect gave for min/max tryhards who have put 2000+ hours into the game. They are currently working on matchmaking, but the poor in-game commincation makes dedicated teams called "platoons" far more powerful than they should be.
Constant disconnects, glitches, and poorly made matches have inevitably ruined this one for me. I might check back next year to see how things are going, but I don't know if it will be around that long.
It isn't pay-to-win, by any means, but it will take you a long time to get to any sense of completion with what you have.

Portal 2 is a first person puzzle game developed by Valve on a modified Source Engine. Set in an old and destroyed science facility, former test subject Chell must escape back to the surface, using her trusty Portal Gun.
Portal 2 is beyond impressive, creating a player-narrative experience that never forgets to be a video game. It's filled to the brim with portal-centric tests, but with various new mechanics added to the mix, such as catapults, tractor beams, lasers, and a variety of paints you can use to change the physical structure of walls and floors. All of these new mechanics however always tie back into the portal gun, giving the game focus, and leaving it uncluttered feeling.
The writing is also spot-on in terms of brilliance. With delightful tangents and jabs, given out by your mechanical warden Glados. Alongside some charming improv by british comedian Steven Merchant, in his role as Wheatley. JK Simmons even makes an appearance as a billionare who's almost patriotic for science.
When you finish the main campaign, there's also some other goodies left to have fun with. Most interesting is a co-operative campaign, with it's own seperate plot and gameplay structure. And a level editor allowing the player to try their hand at puzzle creating. And also an interactive teaser for JJ Abrams' Super 8, for some reason..
The point is, Portal 2 is a great game. With endless wit and addictive puzzle solving, it creates a world worthy of being a part of Half-Life, and especially of part of your steam Library.

I used to love this game so much...it hurts me to write a negative review. Well, as you see with many other reviews I have to say this game isn't worth the time. Until the developers decide enough is enough and put down something concrete, you will have to endlessly wander the internet looking for the answer to the question "What the hell did this update do?" Updates come at decent intervals, but usually bring more harm than good. In past updates, they made robot rankings more obscure yet still keep the same tiered matchmaking system, even though they made it sound like they took it out.
As of right now, the game is terrible for new players. For anybody without a rank 6 robot, you can only play single player (which gives you absolutely nothing) and Team Deathmatch, where grinding levels is tough because there are no respawns and there are major inbalances. That means that you have to buy your way there, with rentals or company builds. This leads to complaints by high level players about noobs. For instance, in a tier 3 game, you can see tiny robots with railguns just oneshotting robots from the tops of hills. New players can't fight back, because rails haven't been unlocked for them yet. Plus, new weapons are expensive. I tried helping a friend into the game, and while I had near infinite reserves of cash to buy low level weapons and blocks, he had issues buying much of anything, guns or blocks.
The game has been in "alpha" for 2 years, but they won't finalise anything and go into beta. Until it reaches beta, and maybe not even then, I would not reccomend this game to anyone not planning to spend quite a bit of money on in game items.

PRELUDE
I played this game for nearly 1.5 years I think. It's good for a quick fight after you have build your bots. Building them takes time... or you rent / buy them.
The game let's you build your own bot with different kind of blocks (like Minecraft). Besides the classical Team-Deathmatch the other main mode is a more strategically battle where you fight against each others and have to capture towers for advantages.
PRO
- It makes fun to build different styled bots which need different playstyles to be good.
- Still make some fun
CONTRA
- The developer implements new stuff while not fixing some old stuff. There are some bugs and gamecrashes that are there for a long time now.
- The matchmaking system seems strange. Many matches are more or less decided by classes the teams have. E.g. if your team have none but the opponent team multiple healers... or if your team has many flying bots and the opponent many railguns... could be better
- The point/ranking system... at some point a system was introduced which showed at the end of the fight how good everybody was. Kills/damage/tower capping/healing everything will get you points and the hidden algorithm calculates your points out of it... I always felt bad for some teammates who played very teamfriendly but got only a few points... this point system seems not well balanced, in addition I noticed the decling of creative bots... when you got rated, you rather build a functional bot than a fun bot. The new ranking system will also lead to this behaviour... you can't have a second fun bot now without decreasing your rank... there are so many bots you could build theoretically, practically there are only some few models with some variation because from a functional point there aren't that many builds... this took fun out of the game
- The bot designing mode is not very helpful. It can take hours at the highest level to build your bot when you want it to bet very tough. The design mode is not helping me much with the right placement/rotation of blocks and has bugs sometimes
- The rental/buying system... I don't like it. I think it will reduce the variety of bots because you rather rent or buy a bot than take the painful experience to build a good bot by your own. This isn't wrong, I would do it too if I were starting now... but I liked the veriety of the bots in the past.
NEUTRAL
The game is still in Early-Access. Therefore there are big chances from time to time where things will get balanced different or new features are implemented. You have to check reguarly what's new, could happen that your bot will be worse than before because somethings changed...
CONCLUSION
I like the basic idea of the game very much and ignored all the bugs in the past, hoping it will get better... had many fun with it. The recent changes in the game took many fun out of the game for me. I will take a break and see what happened in a few month I guess. So I would recommend to have an eye on the game, bt rather wait until the developers have found back to the roots of the game

What exactly is Robocraft?
with the mass amounts of "Craft" games being spewed out, it may just look like another blocky copy of some other beloved game, but oohh boy, are you wrong. Robocraft is a beautiful  experience, letting you build and pilot your own vehicle, while letting you customize its weaponry, armor, design, and pretty much everything? want a swastica on wheels? go right ahead (We actually don't recommend doing that) How about a massive attack chopper? a floating cube with a superweapon? they're all choices. and you can build them.
What's good about the game?
The customization, of course, there's hundreds of parts to choose from, so you never feel "fresh out of ideas"
The nicely paced updates! Even when  things start to feel a wee bit stale, the Robocraft team releases a new update to give the game a well deserved lift. (and be prepared to see everyone using the update parts, I mean EVERYBODY)
And lastly, the controls. Robocraft has some of the smoothest and similest controls i've ever seen, (besides the legs, the legs are weird)
What's not so good?
the community. WHile it isn't perfect, (no community is) Robocraft seems to be a bit too full of small children willing to make "YOUR MOM" jokes when you look for advice in chat.
Gun walls. Ever faced a literal moving wall of guns? I have. and it's not fun.
Legs. yep. legs. I just don't like 'em. they clash with the design of the rest of the game.
While most of the "Bad" things about the game were nitpicking, I can honestly say that while the game is free to play, there is still a shop, where you can buy pre-built machines if you have no creativity, or just use them as massive part outputs, but all in all, Robocraft is fantastic, and i highly suggest you take a look at it.
8.5/10

Portal and Portal 2 are amazing games! They should be a must-play for all gamers. It introduces lots of science in a video game which fits well with its perfect storyline. When I say 'science in a video game,' I mean literally use some scientific equations. I cannot confirm this, but I remember hearing somewhere that they used a real life equation for velocity in the games objects. The puzzles get harder to solve as you go along, and at some point, you may not even be able to solve it yourself! Grab a buddy and go through these puzzles (if you dont have a buddy, Wikipedia is there...). Its mysterious background fits well for this, and why (as well as fits in another VALVe title...). The Portal franchise itself is fantastic and I still think it has the best storyline of any game ever! I first played this game in 2011, and I've played many Triple A (AAA) titles. This game, right here, can single-handedly change your view on many good game stories, concepts, and maybe even (if you don't like shooter games) change your opinion on disliking some other games. I always, to this day, and always will, compare a games quality to Portal.

The last updates have completely ruined this game an I have no interest in playing nor promoting this terrible failure of what was once great. Sorry devs you really did us all an injustice. Don't waste your time.
****Update*****
ROBOCRAFT STILL SUCKS!
After attempting to get back into the game so many times, having read all the promises from the dev's about how fantastic they have made it, it still sucks hairy nuts. If they would rewind the clock back two years when this game was fun and enjoyable, if they would get with the program and listen to the community - out of touch devs have ruined a once awesome game. Not to mention the rorrible server wait times and being penalised for dropouts (leaving early when the server just loses contact) I just hate it now, and I am not alone.
****Another Update****
I have gone from hating it back to playing it... But not in love with it like I was before in BETA days.
Yeah yeah I know, I said it sucks, which in comparison to what it was originally - Yes it sucks.
But coming back into it with the perspective of, what else is there like it to play? Tell me please?
I want to build and fight, I want to refine my bots and make them better and more punishing, I still get rewarded for playing- not how I used to be rewarded, no sense of accomplishment now but I still get crate drops every round so there's that.
Small consolation to what used to be an "EPIC" or "LGENDARY" game. I put down another 250 Hours and am enjoying it, I would prefer the old OG Robocraft but that's never gonna happen, so I will continue to play regardless.
Other things to point out about my current standing on the game.
I have just recently at the 480 hour point decided to show my appreciation to the devs and buy Premium for life.
I am not one to buy into Pay To Win scenarios and I have never bought any P2W bots but the benefits of buying P4L was both appealing to me as a show of dev support (still not happy they changed the game so much from the original versions) I have an extensive library of bots now, all built by me.
There is a certain level of toxicity from the community, I see criticism against people with cool bots or if the team isn't cohesive and you try to voice yourself sometimes other players on your team will just diss you, even when you are actually ahead of them in points. There are a lot of idiots playing this game but all in all I have decided it it worth my time.
Is it worth your time too? I can't answer that but I think you need to give it a chance and decide for yourself.

I've been playing this game for a couple hundred hours now. So this review isn't some newbie review made by a person who hasm't  even invested enough time to know what t stick or a glass cannon is.
I have made it to tier 10, I ave been playing for 1.5 years now and i have seen this game in all of it's ups and downs,  and i have got to say, there will be haters, there will fanboys. This game was good when i started and it's still good now. The only problem is that the game now is that it is directed towards the casual gamer. The guy that invests ~20 hours and never plays again. That just about explains all the decisions that freejam has made in the past while.
Tiering
Cpu, tiering and Roboranking changes have all made the game a lot funner and better for the casual player. But it did take Freejam a couple week and a lot of attpets to get their stuff together for it to actually work. In the process, it destroyed many, many bots. All of my bots included. I scrapped some of the best bots i have ever made. (RIP Gladius MK2., Abomination 2.0 Mk 4) I was mad, unhappy like just about every one else. But i waited a week, ideas were spread around, solutions were concieved and now the tiering system is completly removed. And for the better in my opinion.
Match making
The MM is garbage. That is all i have to say.
Gamemode
Battle arena was a relatively new-ish gamemode where the goal is to the destroy the enemy protonium reactor and you can capture tower to give you buffs and stuff to help you destroy the enemy reactor. Each reactor is guarded be a shield which you can't shoot into but they can shoot out of. Yes there are people that abuse this and become campers. But which game dosn't have campers? Anyways, there arn't all that many of them in my opinion. But you seriosly have to give them praise. I tryed camping once. It was not fun. you just sat there. All day. hardly anyone got close enough for you to kill them. And if they did, they usually had 3-4 buddies with them and you just get trampled by them.
The pit, which is the newest gamemode, is a free for all, Who can steal  kill the best.
Team death match is the regular typical team death match is going to be what you will be playing until  you have a bot that has more than 35m+ RR
gamemode restrictions
Because of player count dropping, the devs are forced to lock gamemodes so that people can actually get into games within a semi reasonable time. IT SUCKS. I really like playing battle arena but since i can ony play it in teir 10,  so many options and ideas that i have are no longer possible because everything is just too damn big. I won't be ab;e to build super small sneaky bots that hide in crevices and then spring up behind people and massacre them.
Conclusion
i'm tryied to make this review as equel as possible and not biased in anyway.  Though still sounds like i sway to one side from time to time. Oh well.
This game isn't for everyone. Be prepared for huge changes, rebuilding bots and lots of negativity. great for the casual player but not if you decided to go long term on this. if you do then you will have to keep your wits and your sanity  about you.
try it, it's free. you got nothing to lose. I guarentee the first few hours will be a blast.

Epic Loot Update and ELO - Beta Updates
ELO - Beta
Ha ha ha ha, reinvented the core gameplay for the main mode to include smaller teams, redefined the mapsm and changed the mechanics. So your team has been dominating for the majority of the match? Well, here, in literally 30 seconds the enemy team can win. No, this is NOT a joke. Absolute nonsense with the mechanics that allow for that. ELO
I know, ELO ratings can be great. But remember, YOU'RE ELO is determined by the teams performance. You could literally singelhandly capture points, heal your entire team, and an astronomical kill death ratio, and STILL go down. This is becuase the winning teams score is doubled, so you can be kicking rear end the entire game and go down because your team sucks and the enemy won in the last 3 seconds. Then when in the lower ranks it only gets worse with even MOAR garbage bots becuase of your teams.
Epic Loot
This update had the economy changed from a perfectly functional you do well = money to RNG based economy, and which took much fun from the game. This is due to the fact you must sell everything to cash, and you get HALF the value from your items. Apperently the higher tier rewards give you better rewards? Cant tell. Free Jam won indie game of the year for this title in 2014. They had the right stuff.
But that was a year ago. This new game is well, by its very context, a new game. Much of the free-friendly content that it once had, is now gone. They have restricted the game modes to make it harder to grind and thus, easier to sell in-game robocraft gear. But as they always say, a good product will sell itself.. but when they have to force us to buy, what does that say about the quality of the product?
Do not get fooled. This game is unclean. Greed has dug its roots into its free system and pay to win has prospered. The game treats its free players like potential customers, not actual customers.
I have personally spent money on this game. I have spent a lot of hours, more than my count indicates. This game used to be great. It was a unique piece of steam that provided an experience of playing on equal grounds within the tier system. That unique experience is gone, now players who were once tier 10 can play with free to play players and that is wrong. It encourages you to invest into the system, when the previous people who were invested into the system were only rewarded by their progress alone, as well as another venue to purchase at. This is a huge slap in the face to the pre-existing community.
1/10. Will be uninstalling. Do not spend money on this product.

I remember when this game was very fun. That was when it had tiers, and rewards consisting of robopoints that you won from matches. You had to strategize where to put your pilot seat and what types of cubes to use (more armored, but heavier, or vice versa). There were 4 types of weapons: the SMG, the rail cannon, the plasma cannon, and the nanotech disruptor. There were 3 gamemodes that were each pretty fun.
But then the terrible updates came along. The first one removed tiers and tech points. At first, I was okay with that one. I thought it solved all my in-game problems at the time. Now i think it was evil.
After a year, the game is deteriorating thanks to bad devs. They are trying to pay off debts, but ruin the game by doing so. The lead dev is arrogant. They refuse to undo all the terrible changes like removing tiers and tech points. Another thing, sometimes they remove these features instead of fixing them. ("oh, lets remove tiers since people say we need to balance them")
Anyway, after the unleashed update, there was an update called Full Spectrum Combat. It removed two major strategic mechanics for bots, the pilot seat and different armor cubes. The pilot seat involves knowing where to place it, since if you were to destroy the blocks connected to it, you would automatically die. The armor cubes were important as well, since different tiered cubes could protect different areas of your bot.
Several months later, 3 new overpowered weapons were added to the game. One makes flying bots obsolete, one is auto-aim and involves homing projectiles, and one does a LOT of damage. They were basically behind a paywall since they costed so much robopoints. If you paid for premium or galaxy cash, you could get these weapons much easier. To top it all off, an update that allows more than one weapon on a bot came, making it possible to have all 3 of those weapons.
Then came along not-so-epic loot. It removed robopoints AND galaxy cash and replaced them with "Robits". You cannot earn robits from matches. The only way to get them is to scrap things you find in crates you get from those matches.
There are 6 grades of crates (you get them depending on how good you did): Rusted, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Protonium. The protonium crates have the highest chance of dropping good loot. But mostly, you get stuff you don't need and you scrap them for robits (The recycle value used to be 50%, but the money-desperate update made it less than 25%).
Now, for the money-grab easy way:
You pay for premium, which doubles the items you get from crates, or you buy crates themselves.
Until a few weeks ago, I found fun in this game. Now I have left FOR GOOD.

This game is incredible.
-Amazing mechanics and gameplay.

-Premium Furthermore doubles the already generous ammount of currency given from every game.
-CREATIVITY AND OPTIONS ARE LIMITLESS!! I do not exhadderate, it's amazing how many possibilities there are. ( I get stuck sometimes simply mixing and matching/playing the single player survival with all kinds of creations.)
-Huge playerbase. 10v10 matches typically take anywhere from 5-25 seconds to get into a match.
-Multiple game modes.
-Multiple types of transportation. ( Want a spider tank medic with wings, propellers, and thrusters? Yeah sure. Why not throw a couple of regenerative shields on that thing while youre at it too.)
-Community sharing and renting system.    Basically, to elaborate, you can get paid the real "$" only currency by sharing your creations. Other players will browse, pick your creation out, and if they like it enough to purchase.... You get paid a portion, which is also so unique amongst free to play games.  They are also able to rent it, in turn giving you in-game money.
Believe me when I say the only con of this game is the 25 second wait time.
Other than the wait time, the only cons are the ones derived from your own carelessness.
This game is balanced.. And though it's possible to be one shotted by a sniper if they're lucky or skilled enough, this game is about being tactical and doing what it takes to win. Which is a great feeling when your team works as a team.
Speaking of the matter.. It's crazy how the team sometimes doesn't even have to communicate, and will cooperate exclusively to the benefit of the team as a whole. What I mean by this is, you have spider snipers at 90* angles on mountains flanking, as bombers pick off tanks on the front lines, with medics healing said tanks, and helicopter SMG's providing air support.. Sometimes people create fighter jets. Sometimes people create satellites to camp over base and provide base defense while jamming enemy radar.. Everyone has your back. It's always a great game and I have yet to try the new game modes as well!
(Every game is extremely diverse.   Last game, someone created Barrack Obama holding a Plasma cannon.. the enemy team mostly just game up when they saw him xD Bomber took him out sadly... But I can still hear the 'Murica ringing in my ears..)

Also, another improvement from Portal 1 is that the game is much longer. Portal 1 took me under 3 hours to complete. Nothing was very hard in that game besides a couple levels. One of the best games you'll ever play, I guarantee it.
Portal 2 has two great different game modes: Singleplayer and Co-Op. Sadly, if you don't have any friends, you won't be able to play the co-op, but in my opinion, the singleplayer alone would be worth your money.
Your problem solving skills will come to a test while playing this, but the story alone in this game is something to love; Portal 2 is a perfect example of great narration and character interaction with the player. The characters are enjoyable and the gameplay is easy enough to master. You can explore and find easter eggs that tell you more about the plot and the world you're in.
The co-op is also entertaining. Puzzles that you have to solve with a friend? Nothing could be more fun! The commands help communication alot - you can watch your friend in a small window to see what he sees, and with the easy commands you can tell your friend what to do. You practically don't need voice chat at all, but it does help alot! The puzzles in the game are fun as well, as the small storyline that goes along with the co-op - nothing major, but still enjoyable. And the community maps are endless - you can always get more community made maps, that can be wonderful to play through!
TL;DR: 10/10, would play again. Must buy game if on sale in Steam!
You can also have a drinking game with a friend, if one of you fails, take a shot. You'll get hammered in no time, because mistakes are bound to happen.

JANUARY 4, 2018 UPDATE #7:
FreeJam is doing a great job with this game.  They are quick to get parts in balance for all types of weapons, movements, etc.  There is now motivation to build both small and large bots with things like Damage Boosts, Speed Boosts, and Health Boosts affecting the way different build operate.
The company also maintains the free-to-play nature - although some people who play for less than a week think it is pay-to-win, it is NOT - just play for a little bit and you will get more parts than years ago.  You can even get legendary parts very early on with a bit of skill and luck which used to take long periods of time to save up for with the old model of the game.
There are also many strategies for earning money in game if you are smart and don't knee-jerk sell every item you get the moment you get it.  Some people refuse to learn and continue to whine about pay-to-win, which is false.
On the topic of paying real money, lifetime premium looks to be worth the purchase if you want to support the developers and get some nice perks at the same time.  Essentially you get advanced progression via double the number of part drops and triple the rate of robits (game-money) when recycling.
The most lucrative aspect of premium for veterans though is probably the wider color wheel and being able to use four times as many cosmetic parts for free without needing to consume regular robot CPU, which allows you to make even cooler looking robots with only the slightest effect on combat (i.e. brighter colors make you more of a target and darker colors tend to have a more imposing look which does not affect game mechanics, but does affect the mind of your opponents which can have an impact on the flow of the game).
Overall, I do highly recommend Robocraft in its current state, there are likely to be more significant changes down the road as FreeJam continues to refine their game.

This game is a huge ammount of fun, but also extremely annoying. You can fully customize your own war machine, though you have a limited ammount of "CPU" to do so, and each part has a value. The value of all your parts cannot exceed your CPU. Since each vehicle is personalized, they each have their own individual weaknesses and strengths. However, there are some extremely annoying elements to this game. Namely, the level progression is pitifully slow, and there is a lack of a tutorial on many things, while the building tutorial seemingly only shows up when it wants to. For example, it took quite a while longer than it should have for the game to tell me how to rotate objects, and when it finally did, I had looked it up an hour ago and was halfway finished my vehicle. Also, when you are shot in this game, your vehicle loses pieces. This seems cool, until all your weapons are shot off, and you only have one wheel, and are destroyed by someone 2 levels higher than you. As well, you cannot have different types of weapons on your vehicle, so  you either have to choose between low damage but easier to use SMGs, or medium damage, low firing Plasma Cannons. As well, you cannot respawn in deathmatches, so once you are plowed down by someone in a hovercraft with level 7 plasma cannons, all you can do is watch other people or exit the game. I have not yet been able to experience the other two gamemodes, which is another complaint. The only two gamemodes other than 1: Useless Practice Map, 2: Real Practice Map Singleplayer, and 3: Repetitive Deathmatch are locked until you are significantly higher level and more powerful than you are at the start of the game, essentially locking new players into playing the boring, repetitive deathmatch mode, or the horrifically boring singleplayer. All in all, I enjoy robocraft, and would recommend it, though it has some amazingly glaring and irritating flaws.

Update [4-5-2017]:
Ah, it was so fun. It really was. And tonight, due to another "trolls and wanderers versus super-powered and coordinated enemy team" battle, I've just decided "screw it". This game is awful, in part to its user base and in part because ... well, frankly, I just can't win. All my epic crate prizes have been in the premium (locked) part, and I'm not earning enough to upgrade worth a flip. It takes ages to earn enough to buy one powerful part, and that only gets you so far.
... and this isn't even starting to discuss the recent "forced to quit when recycling" glitch, and the very, very frequent and random server disconnects that usually cause one to have to wait 5 minutes for "abandoning a battle" even though you had no choice in the matter.
No, I cannot recommend the game. The last 500 hours I spent in it were wasted. During the first 500, though, I would have given this game a much better review.
Update [3-18-2017]: Yep. Removing the game. Peace, out. (... it got one more chance anyways.)
Update [1-24-2017]: Alrighty, I didn't think anyone could take such an awesome idea and ruin it so badly. Every time I play the game, FJ have come up with some new way to make it worse. So here's my new take on it:
Pros:
- You get to build and pilot your own bot.
Cons:
- Matchmaking is broken even worse now than my 2016 review said.
- Now you have crates that give you random stuff, and this "robits" currency. While this would normally be an okay thing, you only get like 1/3 of the parts' worth in robits when you sell them, and the cost of new parts is insane.
- It's all about grinding, due to the above garbage.
- See also: Gripes (2016, below)
I've been on the receiving end of the RNG's wrath. Due to this, I haven't been able to make a bot that can join the ranks of the elite - level 114 with 935 hours on record, and I can't keep any of my bots together long enough to score a kill most of the time, and it's partly because of the drastic changes to the game. I can attribute some of that to my own skill level, but I still see weird stuff like people glitching through maps, and hitting me from across the stage with non-guided weapons as if I were standing still... and I know that isn't right. Especially considering the new weapon power level restrictions.
As far as I'm concerned, this is really all I have to say about the game now:
FreeJam: You OWE me. $45 spent supporting you. I'd like to retract that support now, you don't deserve it.
--------
Update [08-25-2016]: Yeah, I'm heading over to Scrap Mechanic, first chance. I just uninstalled again, probably permanantly. For all the problems and bugs in Minecraft modpacks that make it remotely like Robocraft, I think I'll also stick to Minecraft for blowing stuff up. Sorry, FJ - you did well the first several months of development. I just feel conned out of the $45 spent on the game, now, since it didn't even make a dent in how much fun I could have later. Fact is, too much change.
--------
Update [07-03-2016]: Just played the game again, giving it another chance... and I'm pretty much sticking to my opinion. Game's not really worth the effort. *shrug* I'd hoped after a year things would be better, but nope... still the same crappy one-sided battles, ignoramuses talking like trolls and idiots in chat and ... well, it still feels like one of those pay-to-win games that infest the smartphone market.
Well, I have to hand to to FreeJam. They've taken a really awesome idea, lured a bunch of people into playing it, and now they're changing things left and right. "Alpha" is no longer an excuse; perhaps it should simply be called "Robocraft: Forever" due to its purpetually incomplete state. I feel... trolled upon, and as much as I love the concept, I just can't stand this anymore.
The pros:
- You get to build giant robots like you'd build structures in Minecraft (Still)
- You can pit your creations against others' (Still)
- You can (sort of) show off your creations to others (Still)
The cons:
- The devs can't make up their minds (Still)
- They push more content than bug fixes (or so it seems) (Still)
- Several of the players can't play an honest game* (Still)
- It seems like the devs aren't paying too much attention to players' wants** (Still)
- The matchmaking system is very, very broken. (Still)
The Praises:
- They (being FJ) added the ability to paint your bot ... but... (see gripes)
- They added the ability to mount more than one weapon type at a time.
- They fixed a few exploits, which did make the game easier at least in that respect.
The Gripes:
- They took away Megabots, which is something I still hear people complaining about.
- They took away the Pilot's Seat, which was an integral part of strategic designing.
- They also took away the tech tree and completely changed the way parts are acquired.
- The ability to paint your bot is limited to white, grey, orange and some other color I never used, unless you have premium, which is given through promo codes or... you guessed it! Purchasing with real money.
There should be a button on the Web site for this game entitled "Let me know when the game's ready" - I may come back at that point. I'm likely going to uninstall the game to free up space for less ... daunting venues of entertainment.
* - See also "clipping exploits"
** - See also "large numbers of us can't actually play the way we wish due to absurd bot level restrictions"

Robocraft is far from a perfect game - it's not very polished, glitches happen, and building your robot is a bit unintuitive, which can make it a chore at times (no undos, you have to flip screens to change your building material).
Even so, I'm having good fun playing it so far. Most importantly many of the reasons for this are exactly the complaints in many of the reviews:
And to me that's a good thing. It's was and still is an Early Access game, so I don't care if I just unlocked parts in 1/10th of the time it took you way back when. I want to play a fun game, I don't plan on devoting my life to unlocking helicopter blades.
Duh. That's pretty much the point in playing Robocraft as opposed to a different multiplayer game. At this point the practical reasons for not letting your imagination run completely bananas is that useless parts weigh you down. But not by a lot. And that's also a good decision. If you're willing to sacrifice a little speed Robocraft can be a very creative experience.
The progression tree view for example is dumb. That's not even a tree. It's not how a progression tree works. I don't even think it's confusing, it's just unnecessary. You don't go directions, it's just a classic linear progression (you unlock this at level 1, and this at level 3. etc) but all the icons are kinda shuffled up a bit. People obviously don't think it's a cool idea, so just do a list of rows of icons for each level or something.
These are nitpicks. As I said - unpolished. The game is fun and I like building my robots, I get excited when new parts become available, and I like that I can mostly aford them with ingame money.
Balancing I have not played enough to talk about competently. Sounds bad in other reviews and hopefully Freejam will address that. I don't like the idea of unlocking awesome robot legs 100 hours in and finding out my free wheels from level 1 are actually far superior.

Since it's release on Steam, I've played Robocraft off and on.  At it's core, the game is about building a battle-machine, and matching it against opponents. I mostly enjoyed playing it.
The development of the game has become disappointing. It seems to be locked in a never-ending cycle of buffs and nerfs. Once a weapon is determined to be the best, cries of it being "OP" are common. These people aren't wrong. However, the changes always make way for another weapon to become OP. Rail guns get buffed, then they get nerfed, then they get buffed, then they get nerfed... Development seems to go in continous circles.
The core problem seems to be from the playerbase. Some players have a particular perspective on the game's development. Other players have a diametrically opposed viewpoint. The developers of this game, FreeJam, have tried their best to appease everyone. A noble ambition. The results, however, have been poor. Players have left by the thousands.
A secondary (but related) issue is the changes themselves. They seem to be quite haphazard. FreeJam has no fear of making major and sweeping changes to the game. Which means that your hovers might function completely differently after the next patch. The tech system might be completely different. The menus will change radically. Game modes will come and go. Your damage, range, and RoF will change with nearly every patch. This forces you to constantly modify your designs.
My biggest personal gripe is with the removal of the tiering system. The tiers created strict guidelines which every craft had to abide by. FreeJam decided this was too restrictive. They replaced tiers with a rating system. Instead of being matched by tier, you are matched by rating. Since ratings can vary wildly, you'll be matched against a wide scope of builds. Exploitative min/max builds are incredibly common. You'll find hovers with impenetrable shields. There will be rail cannons that will one-shot you, from across the map, in a spot you can't see, and cannot hit.
Another concern, is that of the forum moderator, "Drognin". This person shows extreme bias towards certain players. Have a negative opinion about the game? He'll let people troll and insult you. Disagree with someone that enjoys the game? Prepare for a temp ban, your thread to be locked, and/or your post to be deleted. When I claimed he was engaging in censorship, he trolled me with, "What are you talking about? I haven't censored anyone!" This he says just minutes after deleting my post, and ignoring all of my reports of people trolling me. (Because he is friends with the people that were trolling me!)
The last thing I want to mention is the penalty added for having "too many" guns. I prefer SMGs. (Rapid-fire lasers.) To be effective, you need around 10 SMGs. However, the game penalizes you (by exponetially increasing your rating!) for each gun you add over 6. My 10 SMG build would have been tier 6. After all the changes, it was rated the same as tier 9s and 10s. Removing the guns lowered the rating, but left my craft with a uselessly low DPS.
I check in with the game occassionally. Sometimes its better, sometimes it's worse. It isn't much fun any more though. I'm tired of spending hours perfecting a design only to find it's matched only against things way better than it can handle. Without tiers, there is no way of knowing what I will face. I'm also tired of being trapped at the base because half the players are sniping with rail cannons. (Thus eliminating any chance of approaching the enemy base!)
I've moved on to other games. This one is way too hard now. The competition is exceedingly high. Exploits are rampant.

For new players, the older version of this game was really cool, so cool it won awards.
Back in the earlier days, you could see what tier your robot was and the more parts you added, would show your progress to moving up a tier.
Players would sometimes build their bots as close to the next tier as possible without moving up a rank and players had full control of the ranking of their bots.
You would be put in battles with only bots your own tier, and because you had to use your own creativity coupled with using blocks you could afford, players witnessed a nice myriad of styles robots and amusing fails, and unusual creations as, each player learned how to build their perfect bots.
It was the discovery of learning how to build, that bought most of the fun to this game, It wasn't just a fps game, it was creativity vs practicality.

This aside it is still a good fps game and you cant still shoot and break off a robot bit by bit which is still unique, and although I’m angry with the directions they have taken with this last update I will still give thumbs up.

When I started playing the game about a year ago,(1600 hours of game time) it was a fun, diverse, and dynamic game, full of creativity and goals that could be achieved through tiers and tech points to buy into higher level gear.
The last few updates have been dismal.  The game population is falling, some weapon platforms have been reduced in effectiveness to the point where they are useless (rail guns, the sniper of the game) and some platforms (flying) have been given so many advantages that ground bots are considered legacy.  Tiers were removed to be replaced with a broken ranking system, and there is no way for a player to measure his progress.
The game abounds with trolls, griefers, and exploiters to the point where new players are often scared off.  The same trolls also strafe the game forums to mock and belittle players with complaints and concerns.  The forum Mods to next to nothing, and the Developers only seem to post when they are forced to.
Recently 2 game modes were eliminated from all but the highest ranked bots (the pit and deathmatch) so all a lower ranked player can join is the normal mode (very long and usually very imbalanced matches) and practice mode.  There is little or no effort spent fixing bugs and exploits, and the Developers seem deaf to the ever shrinking fan base begging for more maps and bug fixes.
As of late, the developers are nearly absent from their own forums, seemingly ignoring the pleas and rants from its core fan base.  Gross imbalances in the game are not addressed, and some made worse (SMG buff to damage over range) despite the data to show what needs to be tweaked.  The overall feeling you get is that the game developers have lost touch, and are not interested in the game succeeding at all.  Almost as if they bit off more than they can chew and are trying to run the game into the ground.
I do not recommend spending any money at all on the game.  Try it for free and see what you think.  As you go up the levels, you will see more and more completely one sided matches and griefers that will camp you all game as you spawn hoping that you rage quit.
The overall lack direction and failure to fix glitches has been attributed to the game being in "alpha" where it has been for well over a year.   Out of touch developers, nasty core fanbase, and lack of variety results in a boring, frustrating, and overall dis-satisfying game experience.  I do not recommend it

Literally everything about this review was killed in it's sleep with a blunt butter knife during the last update, the 'epic' loot update...
The creative freedom is dead, every single block is now behind either grinding for many countless hours to gamble to get the things you want, or just pay the devs a bunch of money to get hundreds of super-rare crates...
The tiers are dead in several different ways...
Robot tiers are completely meaningless, you're either going to get pitted against people using robots that take advantage of OP exploits, or you're going to be pitted against people who can't even figure out how to shoot decently, either way it's just mind-numbing
Armour tiers are dead, your robot now has the exact same durability as the default robot you're given at the start of the game...
The weapon tiers have been turned into a damage/fire-rate ratio system, the fastest firing weapons being the lower tier weapons, the highest damage per shot weapons being highest tier, either way every weapon does the same damage and has the same play-style
The ingame currency is dead... If you're not willing to fork out several hundred *insert currency here*s to buy a decent amount of crates to get a CHANCE at getting the part you want, then you have to keep playing the game until you either manage to find the item you're looking for in a crate, or wait until you delete the blocks you're not using to turn them into currency at a STUPIDLY LOW exchange rate, if you want a specific block then you're looking at easily more than 100 hours of loot grinding to turn into enough game currency to turn into the block you want, only to realise that it doesn't actually fit on your robot and you now need 50 more blocks to re-shape your robot to accomidate for the block you've already spent hundreds of hours building up enough money to get...
The game is only fair to veterans who stockpiled absurd amounts of blocks before the update, anyone who picks up the game now is looking at spending the best part of the year to maybe-possibly-potentially build a half-decent robot thanks to the new gambling system. You can't build anything without grinding for an absurd amount of time, and the grinding is just painful since you can't last very long if you don't have the right kind of gun(depending on your play style), and you can't get the gun without countless hours grinding...
The game is now completely P2W, it's designed to be as painful and horrible as possible to people who aren't willing to give over fistfulls of cash, with grinding, with madatory incredibly-unfair gambling, premium users steamrolling every non-premium user(thanks to their loot being doubled and them having access to paint that lets them be practically invisible)... The list could go on, but i've already tried writing this review twice now and i can't be bothered....
The community is now dead, it's either the typical pay-to-win ragelords who have unlimited funds to splash on a P2W game such as this, or really really cranky people who don't have that kind of money and are just trying to enjoy the game but can't because of everything i listed above
The devs aren't going to do anything, all you have to do is check their twitter and they're openly mocking the critisism against the game as just being a natural backlash(if you ask me, going from something like 80% positive reviews right down to 30% after an update isn't something that just 'happens')
There's even been talk of them censoring critisism(Not sure how legitimate this is, so don't take my word for it), so be thankful that Steam isn't a platform where they can do that...
In conclusion, this game used to be unique, fun, challenging(in a fun way, not a psychologically scarring way), the devs killed it, regardless of how many people said they didn't like that they'd taken a game they loved and turned it into a cashgrab monster, they're trying to use the early access label like a shield...
