I came across this game a while back, I can't exactly remember when, but, It was back when the only game mode was the  Deathmatch gamemode. After failing gloriously to create an all terrain robot, and subsequently spending hours refining it, battling in it and eventually gettingTier 3 parts on the chasis, I found myself in love with this game. Sure it wasn't perfect, the servers were spotty at best and there were some players around who were exploiting the tier limit (I.E.: puting a huge over-tiered Plasma cannon on a tiny chasis made of the game's equivelent of duct tape and wagon wheels), the lack of teamwork was certainly palapable, but, it was such a refreshing concept.
No more could the players curse the Dev's for making a vehicle imbalanced, as they were the developers of their own combat vessels. The game rewarded those with the hindsight and know how to create truely wonderful combat units. Sure the learning curve was a bit... interesting and the physics were borked to all hell at times, but, it didn't matter, those who wanted suceed learned from thier mistakes and did better. It was truely wonderful.
Then the patches came.
I lost track of them after a while but I do remeber them making the game more and more "Noob friendly", I guess? The last patch was an okay attempt at making the game a MOBA, but, it didn't feel like the same game I'd played months before.  Sure it was fun, but there was something missing.
Then this latest patch came out.
As soon as I logged on, I was immeidiately leveled to the top level, and everything was available for purchase, even the things I was still grinding towards. The thing that had kept me with the game in the first place had died and was instead replaced with what I can only assume is a wierd crack at getting some of LEGO Universe's playerbase to briefly consider playing robocraft. The match I got into was a hodge-podge of robots, the strongest of which had parts that could tear through my Tier 8 vehicle in a few seconds. Not that it mattered, I guess, each time I died, I would get a little miffed that I had been destroyed, but, then remembered that there was no longer anything left to achieve, so it didn't matter. I closed the client shortly after dying to something 3x the size of me and 2 tiers up.
This game has been on the decline from the very beginning, if you take a step back and look at it. They hit it clear out of the park with he first itteration, then kept tweaking until it was unrecongnizable. I guess complete and utter sucess is hard to replicate after doing so well to begin with. It saddens me so, though, to see the developers ignoring the playerbase who made them so sucessful to begin with. It is sad to watch this beautiful creature die.
In the words of a fellow reviewer:
"The community is slowly dying." -IKSlayer7
I can only hope that the Devs will eventually pull up in time to avoid crashing and burning, but, things are not looking hopeful.
TL;DR?
There's nothing left  to see here people, move along...

I've played Portal (The original) and the graphics were a bit funky, quite a few bugs, and it was also a bit hard. Portal 2 continues the rather confusing storyline of Portal and enhances it by a lot! If you've never played Portal the beginning may be a bit confusing at first. The only hard part for me was when you ended up in the old Aperture Science area. I believe the name of the Chapter was "The Fall". I've played a bit of the Co-op and it was fun to play. Just try to actually do well or GLaDoS will go crazy and start insulting you just like she did with Chell. The graphics for this game are OUTSTANDING! After a while of playing you simply cannot stop unless someone pries your fingers off your keyboard. (Don't worry, that didn't happen to me) Although, after playing all this and figuring out all the puzzles, I have quite a few questions... What does Chell do after she escapes? Does she find civilization? Can she actually talk? Is she the only human alive now? And why the heck is Aperture Science in a shack?! This gives me the suspicion that they are going to make a Portal 3. You may be asking why. My reason is because in Portal, the story ends with a party escort bot dragging you back inside, and that's all she wrote. It fills your mind with questions. Then Portal 2 came out. In the ending of Portal 2, it simply ends with Chell escaping and Wheatley wishing he never betrayed Chell. Overall, I can tell the game had a lot of effort put into it. If I had to recommend this to anyone on a scale of 1 to 10, I would say 9. Why not 10? Because some of the puzzles can be quite difficult and can make you rage. Other than that, great game! Keep it up, Valve!

This game combines the first person shooter, creative builders, a modifications/purcasing systems, and team matches in a most certainly fun and exciting manner. Get online with your buddies to form a platoon and then go out and kick some robot hiney. You can purchase a prebuilt bot from the developers, or you can work on your own designs. Based on your level, you can only use so many parts of a given point value, which limits how tough your opponents will be at a given level. You progress quickly in prowes at the lower levels, and then you begin to have your serving of despair when you reach level 5 until you gain enough points to purchase the higher cost parts that are just plain better. When they added boss battles in, the game got much more amusing. You will randombly be tossed in to fight a higher level boss with other low level players, or you will be tossed in to fight a bunch of low level players. It is quite amusing. Generally you will be playing capture the flag type combat where you either destroy all enemy team members, or you stay on their pad long enough to win. Overall, I love the game.

+ Amazing co-op gameplay

There is no game like this one. Portal 2 manages to soar far above the original Portal and add yet another level of intricate artistic enrichment and dazzling gameplay. I sometimes feel like I shouldn't be allowed to play this game because it is so fun, and should go back to playing other games that get dwarfed in comparison to this one.
When a novel gives me a strong emotional response to its contents, I applaud it for being superior to many others. When a game does this, I know I'm playing Portal 2. Some of the dialogue is the funniest I've ever heard; some of it deeply bothers me and drives me, in true anger and passion, to beat the game and prove myself... to a character in a video game. I actually feel like I am the main character in this game. At the very least, I empathize with them 100%.
And the gameplay... like I said, there is nothing like it. Riding the learning curve of Portal 2 and realizing that no, some of the levels really aren't impossible, are incredible experiences. The achievement and satisfaction of solving a difficult and very intellectual 3-D puzzle feels wonderful.
You may have heard people speak well of this game, and I'd like to speak greatly of it. But if all that hasn't convinced you to get it, then maybe this will: it's just fun. It's an FPS with no gun, a purely intellectual flourish of discovery, mystery, immersive gameplay, and, if you stay with it, the greatest victories you can find on Steam. Please get Portal 2 (after you get Portal). Please do it. I would be happy for anyone that decided to pick up and play Portal 2, because I would be absolutly confident that they will have as much fun in it as I did.

Imagine a game that takes a brilliant concept and adds a brilliant writing, a brilliant history and a brilliant acting, making a brilliant game. That's Portal 2.

Portal 2 is the perfect sequel to the original. It uses the same basic elements and gameplay, but adds so much more. New elements like gels, lasers, the excursion Funnel, the Hard Light Bridge and even the Edgeless Safety Cube (among many others), contribute to a fresh and new atmosphere that will never seem a simply copy from the original.
In the solo campaign you play again as Chell, but it's not more of the same. Besides an interesting and brilliant history packed with a magnificent voice acting and challenging puzzles with unique gameplays, the writing of this game is absolutely amazing. The monologues of glados and wheatley and their jokes create a immersive and a really special atmosphere where you feel like the protagonist (despite you being a mute dangerous lunatic)
Besides that, the game brings a extremely well executed multiplayer co-op that grabs everything that is perfect in the solo campaign and adds the perfect element: a friend. The Perpetual Testing Initiative will make you spend hours playing maps from other people or making your own puzzle.
I'll recommend Portal 2 to any creature. If you want to have fun and play an excellent game, BUY IT. One of the best games ever and maybe the best Valve game.

Right now, the max level is 100. The higher the level, the more parts you unlock. Parts include weapons, thrusters, helicopter blades, aerofoils (wings needed for flying), simple cubes, parts for the body of the aircraft,
It takes way too long to reach level 100, the game is clearly designed to test your patience and suck money from you. As someone who's only interested in playing in the air vehicles but is for now stuck with ground/land vehicles (because I don't have the necessary parts needed for flight - heli blades, aerofoils, and enough thrusters), THIS IS EXTREMELY FRUSTRATING.

Haters gon' hate, but I think this game is and always was a great one. Started playing it in the summer of 2013 after a friend recommended it to me, started out just like any other player and worked my way through the tiers.
+
So far, FJ have kept their promise of Robocraft being 100% free, but that looks like it's about to change...
+ There is no one "best design" or "best strategy", so be creative and do as you please!
+ Weapons and bot designs counter each other in a "rock-paper-scissors" manner, thus making the game very well balanced. If you feel that something's too weak or too OP, try another bot design and see things from the other guy's perspective.
+ Simplicity is one of FJ's top priorities, and the gameplay's challenging and at the same time easy to get into. However, they've been dumbing it down a bit too much recently. As Einstein once said, things should be made as simple as possible - but not any simpler.
- Servers are struggling most of the time, and the matchmaking can be frustrating at times.
- There are a few glitches and exploits, but most of those get patched up with haste.
- The community is mainly composed of 8-year-old fanboys who whine about everything and anything they don't quite get. (Which is in our instincts, I suppose... we have a tendency to fear things we don't understand.)

I wish I could write a good review for this game, I really do.
But I can't.
3-4 months ago, I easily would have given this game 10/10. It had simple but strategic gameplay and complex engineering and building. And if you wanted to, you could build "artbots" and be creative to your heart's extent.
What the game really needed, was to keep it's core gameplay (building and 1 life battling) and polish the battle aspect of the game. The building aspect was great, all it needed was more content and accurate statistics. The battle aspect was great, all it needed was more variety.
But instead, the devs went off on a limb and ruined everything. Instead of enhancing the gameplay, it completely changed it. They threw everything good away to appeal to the moba crowd. And, being a MOBA fan, I hated it. Overclocking ruined bot design, I could spend 8 hours designing a bot, and that bot would perform no better than a simple brick with guns on it that I could design in 5 minutes.
The devs seemed to think staring mindlessly at a tower was fun, so they added towers simply to appear to the MOBA crowd. Everyone hated them, but instead of getting rid of them, they made them more integral to the gameplay.
The devs made bad decision after bad decision. After every update more and more people complained, more people left. The devs refused to listen to the playerbase, and when they did. They listened to the fanatics and white knights instead of the critical but reasoned responses from players who only wanted to see the game succeed.
And after all this, they go chasing after imaginary problems and spend 1 month of dev time doing nothing to improve gameplay, but trying to fix a problem they made 2 updates before, instead of just rolling back the said update.
But hey, we got a new map.
All in all, the devs ruined this game. I highly reccomend ignoring this game if you don't want to be constantly dissapointed until you quit.

I wish I could write a good review for this game, I really do.
But I can't.
3-4 months ago, I easily would have given this game 10/10. It had simple but strategic gameplay and complex engineering and building. And if you wanted to, you could build "artbots" and be creative to your heart's extent.
What the game really needed, was to keep it's core gameplay (building and 1 life battling) and polish the battle aspect of the game. The building aspect was great, all it needed was more content and accurate statistics. The battle aspect was great, all it needed was more variety.
But instead, the devs went off on a limb and ruined everything. Instead of enhancing the gameplay, it completely changed it. They threw everything good away to appeal to the moba crowd. And, being a MOBA fan, I hated it. Overclocking ruined bot design, I could spend 8 hours designing a bot, and that bot would perform no better than a simple brick with guns on it that I could design in 5 minutes.
The devs seemed to think staring mindlessly at a tower was fun, so they added towers simply to appear to the MOBA crowd. Everyone hated them, but instead of getting rid of them, they made them more integral to the gameplay.
The devs made bad decision after bad decision. After every update more and more people complained, more people left. The devs refused to listen to the playerbase, and when they did. They listened to the fanatics and white knights instead of the critical but reasoned responses from players who only wanted to see the game succeed.
And after all this, they go chasing after imaginary problems and spend 1 month of dev time doing nothing to improve gameplay, but trying to fix a problem they made 2 updates before, instead of just rolling back the said update.
But hey, we got a new map.
All in all, the devs ruined this game. I highly reccomend ignoring this game if you don't want to be constantly dissapointed until you quit.

For a free game, it's surprisingly great.  Excellent customization options, unique gameplay styles, and significant amount of updates and improvements.  Each ship can be customized heavily, from its movement style, to its armor class, to its weapon choice, with even some cosmetic items thrown in.  This allows for bombing planes, hovering snipers, speedy car medics, and lumbering laser tanks, all of which are completely customizable!
The major downsides is the grind, and the sameness.  Despite the incredible variety of vehicle types, there is a lack of variety in game modes and in maps, sometimes leading to boredom.  This issue is constantly being fixed with fairly consistent updates.  But, like most free-to-play games, there is a bit of a grind.  That being said, the grind isn't outrageous, and makes building your ship feel worth it.
I haven't spent a dime on this game, but still had a fantastic time.  Huge recommendation for fans of building or battling games.

Rating this game negatively genuinely breaks my heart. It really does. Robocraft had so much going for it and, up until june 22, I completely loved the game. I have been with this game from the beginning. I started playing several months after it's humble release in 2013. Back at this time, Robocraft had 1 weapon type, limited movement types, and little to no playerbase. It has since then grown into an indie-game powerhouse and even won the prestigious indie game of the year award.  I hope someone important reads this review and others like it and decides to make a change, although I doubt it will happen considering the sheer amount of reviews that are posted. But I digress. Time to start the review.
Gameplay- Pre-update gameplay was downright fantastic. You started out with a small bot and weak lasers, then completed battles and moved up through the ranks until you had built your unstoppable robot killing machine. Gameplay was always fast-paced and fun, and the building system only got better as the game progressed. The variety of weapon and movement types that the game had made sure that every robot that you built and encountered was unique. In fact, the building process was the most important and in-depth part of the game. The way that damage works in this game is quite in depth and complex, so you could spend hours upon hours learning how to build a bot that would use the system to it's advantage and still have loads to learn. Although this building knowledge was very important, your goal to build this perfect bot was always limited by 3 other things: CPU, RP, and tier. CPU was how much space you had to put movement types, armor, guns, and other objects on your robot. You unlocked more CPU by leveling up, which you did by playing games. Obviously, your level was always pretty indicative of your general skill, so a higher level player with a robot as good as a lower level player's will probably beat them out. RP was the in-game money used to buy new objects to put on your robot, which you earned by playing games. The final restriction, tier, was the one that mattered the most and truly made the game what it was. There were 10 different tiers originally with 1 being the easiest and 10 being the hardest. You started out in 1 then unlocked new items and increased your bot's RR until you had reached the next tier. You increased RR by adding more powerful versions of you current guns/wheels/wings/etc until you crossed the threshold into the next tier. you could only unlock the more powerful items by playing in the next tier, so this allowed you to progress until you hit tier 10. This ment that you always played with people near your level, but there was enough difference that you had an incentive to build better robots so you would be met with more success in that tier. Once you hit 10, you were no longer restricted by tier and you recieved lots of RP. This ment your only restriction was CPU, so you could play tier 10 until you hit level 100 and maxed out your CPU to build the best bot possible. They later added an 11th tier for "megabots" which was an absolutely fantastic idea, because it allowed all of the super rich experienced max-level players to work towards something else. All of these "Pre-June" features worked wonderfully together, and the steam rating remained above 92%. After the update, aptly named "Robocraft: Unleashed! Time for another one of these.
Portal 2, the puzzling action game built around the cognitive ability to solve logic puzzles. Basically, if you're stupid, you'll have a hard time getting through the campaign. Its mechanics are well integrated and they aren't just the use-once-then-forget-about-it-for-the-rest-of-the-game things you see so often in other games. Based a few (hundred) years after the original Portal, this game has a very different theme to the uniform, perfect white chambers that it's predecessor, mostly featuring rusted, old and destroyed elements.
And if playing the campaign and finding the hidden secrets the sneaky, tricksy valve has left you isn't enough, then there is a workshop where you can upload your own test-chambers, made in the aptly named test-chamber editor, or download other chambers built by people with mods, who will then make you judge your own chambers because you have no idea how to do what they did.
All-in-all, this game is psychologically taxing for idiots, has a very decent bit of humour mixed in, gives you the freedom to make a small white box and call it a test-chamber, and also eligibility for picking up cards.

Valve’s Portal 2 is the 2011 sequel to the original Portal which holds my shortest review to date and that was because it was a game of few flaws.
I am going to be honest, as of 2015 I still haven’t played a game that surpasses Portal 2, it is my favorite game of all time. It has a lot more puzzle elements in the form of gels which does different things and also added gravity lifts. The dark humor is excellent, the writing is absolutely amazing through the entire game, the “tutorial” if I dare call it that is quick and introduces the story of the game nicely and within a couple of minutes you can start solving puzzles (unless you want to stand around listening to what the AI Wheatley has to say when you do nothing).
I had a few problems with the original Portal but only one really big one, and that was that the game was too easy, the first puzzles in Portal 2 are very easy too but as you get farther into the game it gets harder. Everything past chapter 7 is harder than the hardest chamber in the original which was Chamber 18, and several chambers before were harder than Chamber 18 as well. The Final Boss fight is also vastly improved requiring careful Portal placement and timing rather than the extremely easy fight at the end of the original.
But what problems do I have with this game? 1 issue, and it’s what would probably be considered a nitpick, that is that they tried to recreate the feeling of  “Still Alive” from the first game by doing a very similar song, that is my only problem with this game.
The online co-op maps, what about those? I don’t have a single complaint there, not one. They require teamwork to beat and trying to figure it out with a friend is great fun, I recommend using voice-chat though.
There is no such thing as objectively perfect, but this is probably as close as a game is ever going to get to perfect for me. And that doesn’t mean I think puzzle games are the best genre, rather the game is perfect in what it sets out to be except for that one little thing. But since it is to me subjectively perfect I cannot promise that it will be for you, however I believe strongly that the vast majority of people out there will find enjoyment out of this title. Have fun, ciao.

There is something deeply satisfying about creating a robot that not only looks bad-a$$, but can also dominate other bots in the battle modes. Creativity, strategy and... epic battles that turn your knuckles white and get your heart pounding.
Having played for a little over a year now, I have paid attention to how the development team operates. As a tech exec with over 30 years experience, I am genuinely impressed by their vision, their creativity and their values. FreeJam (the development team) should be commended for not only creating a truly great game... but also for their commitment to rapid innovation, guided by strong instincts, along with well-cultivated user feedback. They also seem to place a high value on creativity and experimentation. And while aren't always perfect, when issues arise, they listen, are transparent in their communications and act quickly to get things right.
This a game that I recommend to every gamer (and parent's of gamers) that I meet.

A sequal to Valves 2007 Masterpiece Portal was never going to be easy but in 2011 Portal 2 graced our screens and truely expanded on what was already quite a rich universe.
Portal 2 continues the Mythos of the Apature science building and is rather magical in the sense of its a sequal that doesnt seem to fall into being "A retred of old ground" while also avoiding the pitfall of being "To different" the balance is quite wonderful in balancing the old portal test chambers you know and love and further allowing exploration beyond the test chambers. The Graphics are as sharp as ever for a 4 year old game and feel crisp and sharp, the storyline picks up after the events of portal and it quickly becomes clear that the dark humour that was heavily present in the original game has not escaped the sequal expect plenty of Laugh out loud moments . the controls are on the nail with only a couple of occasions I can recount where the controlling of the character was ever an issue, its one of those games where if you screw up you know it's on you rather than the game.

tl;dr: Great game with fun gamemodes, very intuitive, easy controls, many maps. It's basically WoT, except that you can build your on tanks.
The game itself :
When I first started to look at this game, I expected it to be rubbish. Most games, in which you have the freedom to build something the way you want it, are bad. Minecraft did inspire many gamemakers to make something similar, which mostly horribly failed, and I looked at this the same way. Because I was so preoccupied I didn't get this game first. I do regret this today and if your reading this, download it already and continue reading afterwards. This game is basically WoT with different gamemodes. The first is "Siege", in which you have to destroy the enemy base structure. But you have to protect your own, that's why teamplay is very important. You can destroy smaller towers to create a shield around your main structure, if those where destroyed, they fill up with blocks in the color of your team. If, however, the enemys destroy a towey, it fills up with blocks of their color, which you can destroy again to get another shield.
There is also "Team Deathmatch", which is exactly what says.
There are also some others, which I didn't unlock yet
The building:
In this game, you can build structures out of blocks, wheels, wings, vertical rotors and many more. In this way you can build your very own war machine, which is most likely unique. You can get new blocks by unlocking them in the "Tech Tree" with "Tech Points", which you get by playing. So the more you play, the more you can build. The are many variations of the weapons, some are more effective against towers, others are more effective against player, you get the point. If you have unlocked more weapons or blocks, your robot will raise a "Tier" and you will fight against stronger enemys. The maximum tier is "Tier 10".
Result:
This game is great for 24/7 gamers, but also for casual players, as you don't have to play hours to have fun and/or to reach something. The game itself feels really smooth, but sometimes the controls get out of control and your robot spins around itself for a few times. But as this is more funny than annoying, it doesn't bother you after a while.
9/10
Edit: On the 29th of July a patch came out, changing most of the game. It now is harder for low-level gamers and easier for high-level gamers, as everybody can now fight against everybody. Still a great game, just not as great as before.

I've been actively on the fence about Portal 2 for years, but when I got a coupon for it earlier this year I finally decided to check it out.
All I do now is ask myself why I didn't get it sooner. Portal 2 is immersive, creative, and surprisingly hysterical in its humor. Every single character is memorable, although I give notable to credit to Wheatley (voiced by Stephen Merchant from The Office) for being an outstanding one with his dialogue and humor.
Portal 2's environment is vast, empty, but compelling as you learn and discover some backstory to the mechanical menace known as GLaDOS. Coupled with the enjoyable dual portal mechanics and puzzles, along with a well done cooperative mode for friends, I enjoyed every single bit of this game.

A sequal to Valves 2007 Masterpiece Portal was never going to be easy but in 2011 Portal 2 graced our screens and truely expanded on what was already quite a rich universe.
Portal 2 continues the Mythos of the Apature science building and is rather magical in the sense of its a sequal that doesnt seem to fall into being "A retred of old ground" while also avoiding the pitfall of being "To different" the balance is quite wonderful in balancing the old portal test chambers you know and love and further allowing exploration beyond the test chambers. The Graphics are as sharp as ever for a 4 year old game and feel crisp and sharp, the storyline picks up after the events of portal and it quickly becomes clear that the dark humour that was heavily present in the original game has not escaped the sequal expect plenty of Laugh out loud moments . the controls are on the nail with only a couple of occasions I can recount where the controlling of the character was ever an issue, its one of those games where if you screw up you know it's on you rather than the game.
I hold only one personal issue with this game and that is that to me it doesnt quite feel as tight as it's predecessor. while I love the idea of a free and sprawling game with which to use the portal gun once the free roaming levels begin I feel the game slows down a touch as your forced to think of unique solutions to getting to the next level of the game. the chambers feel fine but these underground sections never hung as tightly to me. though I suppose it's the rose tinted glasses talking for my preference for the original Portal.
Pick this game up. it's essential playing if your a gamer. if you havent played the original Portal then good lord go and play that first because it's beautiful. if you have played the original portal why are you reading reviews for the sequal this should be in your download cue already...it may not be a perfect game to me but it's a bloody good one.

Robocraft is a game centered around building bots that you can use to fight other players in a mutliplayer arena.
Sounds fun right? Using your imagination to create an awesome bot!
Except in the game that concept falls flat.
The problem with Robocraft is that unless you build your bot a VERY certain way it will be outclassed. This is especially true after you have ranked up in the game, if you deviate from the copy-paste build everyone uses you will always lose (Unless your team carries you)
Currently Robotcraft is plagued, almost every bot in competetive play is identical in one way or another, they all follow the same formula. In order to survive you must copy the same formula.
Another problem with Robocraft is that every previously mentioned copy-paste bot has capabilties to do lethal damage to your bot VERY quickly, even if you make an extremely tanky armored bot. Armor is useless in the game. The meta has revolved around all damage no armor. This has turned the game into a robot version of Call of Duty.
The developers have not yet addressed this issue, but seeing as how the playerbase is declining I am sure they will fix it, but as for now I do not recommend this game.
---------------------------------------
TL:DNR= If you want to win in Robocraft you must follow a very specific non-creative formula. This is counterintuitive as the core point of the game is to be creative.

I'm seeing a lot of reviews saying that Freejam ruined the game. This isn't entirely true. I mean, yes, they did alienate a lot of players who used to play, myself included, but they were only trying to make their game better. But don't go to the nearest person who will listen and start ranting about Freejam ruined the game, where's the tiers, where's the tech tree just yet. Here's my honest opinion after over 100 hours of playing both before and after the "crate catastrophe" about what Freejam did wrong and what they could change to make the game better.
I agree with a lot of people. The old system was great! It had an easy system to start on with lots of opportunities to improve your vehicle. It had a great system of balances already: Sure, you can make a gunbed, but you can break the gunbed from above or afar with plasmas. Oh, you made a plasma satellite? Allow me to break that with railguns.
Then came Freejam's attempts to balance the game. Freejam, if you're reading this, balancing was the right direction to go, but you took a wrong turn. The tech tree was a lot of what players wanted in a game in my opinion. Yes, you could easily take high tier weapons and bring them to lower tiers, but that could have been fixed separately. Thing is, you eliminated the tech tree and added crates and robits. I feel like these have degraded the quality of the game, because you now need so much money just to grab one more part. The game was about taking a lot of parts and making a vehicle which both dealt and either took or dodged damage. The hard part was going up a tier and getting better tech tokens to unlock those parts.
Which brings me to the crates. This was the point where I stopped playing Robocraft for a while. I personally don't like the crate system. I think I see the original idea behind them: A player would play or pay for crates which gave them a chance to get a better weapon than their tier gave them. It would help players progress while keeping the middle tiers so diverse, with those high tier weapons giving weaker vehicles the push they needed to compete, even slightly, with the higher tiers.
This game was, in my opinion, the best game to get into, because it was free, offered a lot of content, and didn’t throw advertisement in your face. I feel like Freejam lived up to their name at that point. The game was free, and it was extremely fun to play.
This isn’t everything I wanted to say because honestly, a lot of what I didn’t say is just nitpicks. These are the big problems with the game as I see them. If Freejam fixed them, I would be glad to play. But now I just can’t enjoy the game the same way. For the same reason I cannot recommend this game to new players.

If you're interested in Portal 2 because you enjoyed Portal, think twice. Portal 2 doesn't have the same emotional feel, satisfying conclusion, or wry seriousness throughout. The problems start from the beginning and really don't let up, although the puzzles are interesting enough to keep that part of your mind engaged.
-----SPOILER ALERT-----
Apparently many years have passed and animals have evolved so that they terrify humans, and humans now worship giant apes - or something. That's farcial, and this underlying lack of seriousness leaves you rolling your eyes at the sophmoricism on display throughout the game. Of course, GLADOS wakes up and must be killed all over again, but this time she is not killed, but reduced to a potato. Yes, you read that right. More farcial humor. (She's also feasted on by a bird later on.)
The geography doesn't make much sense, either. Parts of the game are set in a giant salt mine, which exists apparently in the middle of nowhere, Iowa. Seriously. There's no evidence that any mining activity takes place in the local area.
The puzzles are ok, with none of them as difficult as the last few in Portal, which is kind of disappointing. I'm no masochist, but I found if I didn't get the puzzle in 20 minutes, if I slept on it, I'd figure it out the next day. It wasn't terribly challenging. The atmosphere is appropriately eerie and occasionally unsettling.
The game is also way too long - it's at least 8 chapters, and I only kept playing to see what the ending was. Unfortunately, the ending is completely unsatisfying. Once you reach it, you end up opening a portal to the moon (funny how the Portal gun fizzles out after distances even half that everywhere else in the game), and chucking Wheatley into space. If that wasn't bad enough, then after you reach the surface, you're treated to more silliness - Wheatley floating in space, talking, and Glados singing a song. It reduces the whole impression of something meaningful and sinister created by the first game to some spat between frenemies in junior high. It's ridiculous.
So while the puzzles were fairly enjoyable, and the atmosphere generally involving, everything else about the game was sub par.

I'm editing/changing my review. As of right now, I would not recommend this game to friends anymore.
I want to say this outright, before I get in to my reasoning.
At it's core, Robocraft has been a very fun game, and had a lot of potential to be competitive.
It has complete customization control, and interesting mechanics.
But, in it's current state, the game can be incredibly rough to play. As a comparison, getting parts to build a robot, and get to the end game [to play a bit mroe competitively] was a lot easier than it is now. Previously you were able to earn currency, and spend it on specific parts, to build the robot you envisioned to battle with. Now, it is up to a pseudo-random crate system; in which you get parts from [to build your robots].
The crate system, though left with a lot of potential, has it's downfall in sellback. As mentioned; you used to be able to earn currency, now you can break down parts you have won in order to gain currency. This would not be an issue if prices of parts was substantially lower, or if sellback was a lot higher. When you break down a part you gain around 10% of it's value, and most parts are already generally low value. Cubes, and lower tiered items cost a lot less,a nd are common. Where-as high-tier functional parts that are important to a build, and astronomically priced. Some important parts take you around 150 games just to gain a functional piece. This is no good for someoen who has a specific build in mind.
On top of the crate system, there are very few weapons that are viable, at the moment. The pool of weapons we have vs. that in which are viable is a little ridiculous. The weapons were recently flattened from a tier system in order to give plausible viability to ever form of weapon present. This may change in the future, but at the moment it is no good. Energy is a component in the game similar to mana; and some weapons eat up mana too quickly, other weapons may not use mana efficiently, yet do not do enough damage to be plausible in the current meta.
The second last gripe of the game is loyalty. I have played many hours of this game, and I can say that loyalty is only a pat on the head, and a brush to the side. There are those who are loyal, and popular, who get Freejam's attention, but overall being loyal has no perks. When Freejam make changes to the game, it is the new player base who have voices, and only in statistics. It seems that those who have stayed throughout the years have little to no say in the gamestate, now.
The vocal members of the community have been met with much resistance at times, and other times outright ignored. This is something I find to be an issue, due to the fact I very much like this game, and I want to see it move forward. This makes it feel that the community that was built almost doesn't matter, and might not matter moving forward.
Lastly; Freejam's communication skills have always seemed to be low. i'm unsure if it's due to low staff, or... Well, I'm not even sure. Some of the staff are rude, sometimes they are dismissive. Other times when Freejam communicates things they are 100% transparent [which you should never be], and take back what they say soon after. Othertimes, there are concepts brought up; promised, but then dropped without a word. Overall Freejam have been very heavy handed in a lot of what they do, and at times it's been frustrating.
This game has potential to thrive again, I believe in it. But at the moment, I feel it would be very hard to recommend to people, seeing how hard it is to pick up and play. How hard it is to get to the real gameplay [max level, a decent amount of parts], and how hard it is to learn a lot of things [no tutorial, unintuitive hud].
So until this haze clears up, This is my stance.

I've been playing Robocraft since July of 2014 shortly after it was released from beta, and I can honestly say that this game is one of the most fun games that I have ever played; I just keep coming back to it! The concept is simple: make a block out of armor cubes, stick it to a pilot seat, and slap some wheels and guns on it, too. Just like that, you have a working robot that you can use to drive around and fight other players and their robots. You start out small, but eventually you level-up further and further until you can make huge, complex crafts with shields, wings, hoverblades, "triforced" armor... Tons! Each robot takes real-time damage during battle, which means that parts of your robot will fall off once enough damage is dealt to them; this adds a whole new dimension to combat and thought when building a robot.
Recently, the game has gotten a lot of flak because of the implementation of the new MOBA gametype "Battle Mode," in which your team must fight the opposing team to capture and control 3 towers on the map to aid in destroying the enemy base. Older players grew accostumed to playing "Classic Mode" (now called "Team Deathmatch") and complained about the new addition of Battle Mode, failing to realize that CLASSIC MODE (TEAM DEATHMATCH) STILL EXISTS. Whereas in Battle Mode, players respawn after being killed and focus on taking/retaining towers for their team, Team Deathmatch is a game mode which consists of no respawns, ~10v10 combat, no towers, and -- if you are in a high enough tier -- a MEGA bot on each team. Mega bots are HUGE robots that players can build eventually. So yes, Robocraft has two awesome gametypes that you may choose to play at your whim with the high chance of additional gametypes being added in the future.
One of the biggest strengths of Robocraft is how responsive the development team is. It is worth noting that the game is still in its alpha stage, and FreeJam is a pretty small team. Despite this, FreeJam is very active on Twitter, Reddit, and the Robocraft forums and open to discussion with their playerbase on how to improve Robocraft. Yes, FreeJam made some mistakes (limiting building capacity for each tier, ruining artbots, nerfing hoverblades, for instance) but they have ALREADY ACKNOWLEDGED these issues and have promised to fix them. Though FreeJam can't fix every mistake immediately, they are extremely aware of what the Robocraft playerbase feels is wrong. Some examples when FreeJam did RIGHT was: when the servers got clogged with an explosion of new players (last summer) they got more servers within a week, they implemented an anticheating software program when hackers became an issue which significantly reduced the amount of cheaters in games, they implemented a CPU restriction to each tier to prevent "overtiering" in matches which a lot of new players were complaining about -- not an example of a GREAT solution but definitely an active, attentive solution (this update made it so a lot of artbots had to be deleted). So yes, sometimes FreeJam makes a mistake with an update, but they are always aware of the mistakes and actively trying to fix them. I want to reiterate that the game is still in alpha and that FreeJam is a small indie team. Despite this, FreeJam has already recognized the issue and has promised a solution to make artbots possible again.
I think a current issue that some new players may face is the brief tutorial the game offers. I would recommend watching a youtube video to learn how to properly play/make a good robot/learn the controls in the garage bay.
Overall, I think Robocraft is a spectacular game even in its alpha state with a lot of promise for the future. The developers actively listen to their playerbase's concerns and always deliver solutions to their problems. I could not recommend this game anymore to anyone!

So, let's talk about some of the bad reviews you saw.
I saw them too before playing this game and was skeptical, they were along the lines of "The Dev's made things more competitive and less art/fun"
This is the case. But it's not bad and let me explain why.
The game is VERY competitive, and VERY VERY VERY FUN.
You build whatever the hell you want and then play Team Death Match or destroy the enemy base (more gamemodes as you level up).
I've see people make intricate doom machines, but the last match I played the guy had a brick with one wheel and all it did was drive in circles...why did he only put one wheel??! It's chaos and fun. My first sessions was 10 hours without realizing, I can't think of the last time I played a game that long because I lost track of time.
There are a few bugs, but it's Early Access and they are VERY minor bugs. This game feels like a full release game.
Now, there are microtransactions.
You play matches to get points to buy blocks, and points to buy upgrades.
You can buy the points to buy blocks
You cannot buy the points to unlock blocks.
It's not "pay to win" it's "Pay because I'm dumb and don't like playing the game"
Each round gives you a TON of in game currency.
This game is GOOD. This game is FUN.
If you like Legos and BattleBots, this game is for you.

Fun little game, but has some quirks, can be tough to figure out (no real tutorial or help menu to explain things, or at least I couldn't easily find anything), and can get a bit stale quickly.
The building section is good, but not great. Kerbal Space Program had much easier building. You can only rotate parts on one axis and this can make things difficult with some pieces, especially in tight spots. The opacity on the preview is so light too you can barely see how the part will be oriented sometimes. My bigest grip is there is no undo feature. Sometimes I've accidently deleted pieces and instead of a quick undo, I'm faced with the difficult task of trying to put it back together (goes back to the difficult building). I would like to be able to fabricate sections as well and save them for easier building in the future.
The game is pretty fun for a few hours, but starts to get stale with only two game modes (you need to unlock two others). It's either team deathmatch or team deathmatch where you have to shoot these balloon things.
My biggest gripe is probably the match maker. First off, it takes pretty long to get in games. Add bots if there aren't enough human players. My main gripe though is sometimes I'm tiered where I should be with my parts and build, and sometimes I'm tiered 1-2 tiers higher and have absolutely no chance. Maybe I'm building too much for the tier, if only the game had an easy help menu that could explain things to me...I have one game though where I'm tiered properly, then get uptiered the next game, even without any changes to my robot. I don't understand it at all.
This is a free game, so I suppose I can live with some quirks, however if this game was over 10$ I'd want a refund.

This game used to be pretty fun. Sure, it was never amazing, but it was great for a few laughs and just spending some time destroying other creations on what actually was a unique battlefield.
Today I return to Robocraft, after many months of inactivity. I had gotten a full set of T10 weapons, but never honestly bothered to grind any further to get my armor to T10 as well, I'd grown tired of the grind, in fact, that's actually why I quit.
Nevertheless, when I return, I'm greeted almost instantly with a glitch, before I had done anything in the game whatsoever. I was presented with a message saying "Some of the cubes on your robot are obsolete. These will be removed from your inventory and your RP and TP will be fully reimbursed." with an "OK" button. Naturally, I would just click the OK button, but I couldn't, because when I'd attempt to move the cursor, I'd instead find it just twitching around in the same spot rather than actually moving toward the OK button.
This was fixed by returning to the desktop and right clicking on the icon and clicking "close", this brought up a prompt in-game asking if I was sure I wanted to close it. Out of curiosity if it would fix the bug, I clicked "no", and to my surprise, the cursor worked and I was able to do stuff! Wonderful! Time to play!
Wait... Where's the bar at the top that shows me my RP and stuff? It's... It's gone? Maybe that's part of some weird update... Whatever, I know the hotkeys for this game.
And so, I pressed the button to bring up the mode selection to go ahead and enter a battle. What do I see? Apparently I can't access anything except practice mode, because I can't enter T9 with T10 weapons, which is fine, except I apparently also can't enter T10 with T9 armor. Now, considering there was no real need to keep the previous tier's weapons before, I'd always sell the previous tier's things to boost myself a bit into the next tier's equipment (selling T9 SMGs/plasma/etc and putting the RP from that toward the T10 variant), but apparently now I require T9 weapons or T10 armor, both of which I'd have to grind more for just to play the same tier that I used to be able to play before, but now I can't.
So I bring up the store just to see if I could buy some T9 SMGs, and notice the RP still isn't showing and that the UI looks a little weird because the bar at the top is very clearly missing from it. It was then that I concluded that the bar was indeed supposed to be there, but wasn't because of a glitch - yes, a part of the UI was literally just missing.
So I close the game and re-open it, only to find that the T10 SMGs I had taken off my tank were now back on my tank, and now the bar at the top displayed, showing that I apparently only have 20,000 RP, which isn't enough to buy the T9 SMGs I'd need, which come at 58,000+ a piece, which I didn't even need to play the game prior to this, and honestly, I'm not going to grind lower tiers just to play the same tier that I used to be able to play. I wouldn't even care if I were playing T10 with T9 armor - I'd played very similarly before and still did well.
That's Robocraft in a nutshell now, glitches everywhere, and screwing over their players for no reason at all. Want to invest your time in this game? I honestly don't see why you would, but by no means should you spend a single dollar on this game, you'll only come to regret it when you realize how little the devs actually care about their playerbase.
That said, after two major glitches right off the bat, and what appears to be the ultimate "screw you" in this update, I closed the game and have no intentions on trying it again until a supposed future update where they remove tiers entirely is to arrive.

Robocraft was easily one of the most enjoyable voxel style games I have ever played, you had complete creative freedom, the F2P model was well designed and never forced you to pay money in order to gain an advantage over others, the tiering system meant that you could play against people of any skill level whilst at the same time preventing you from building a robot that was TOO powerful (you could join the game with an overtiered and powerful gun, but it was balanced by the fact that you had extremely weak armour).
Then, THAT update came.
The update that changed Robocraft from a fun game in which you messed about with robots into a more competitive game which discourages you  from building a fun models and instead forces you to build super-efficient robots in order to stand a chance in any match.  They completely removied any kind of overtiering and quashed the previously mentioned creative freedom by forcing a new meta of gun beds and gun blocks (platforms covered in as many guns as possible), they chose to listen to the elitists which resulted in unnecessary nerfs and led to most builds (walker etc) being made completely obsolete in favour of gun blocks which ruined most bot builds, they also tried to jump on the MOBA bandwagon by introducing a MOBA style gamemode that often results on hour long matches due to stalemates and a broken surrendering system. Experience gain was also nerfed and now forces players to grind endlessly for EVERY tier in order to raise your CPU level (which allows you to place more/better blocks and guns on your robot) and get into the higher tiers.
I cannot recommend this game until Freejam get their act together and fix their once great game.

Portal 2 not only brings better gameplay, story, sound, and overall design, but also brings the addition of multiplayer to the table which wasn't present in the first game.
SIngleplayer not only has new things and mechanics to toy around with, but also brings better music that fits the tone of the game, but also better levels to play with, and a more developed story that opens up a lot more than the first game. The ending credits music is amazing and it is on the same level as the first game's credits music and is just a joy to listen to even if you're not playing the game. Even if you're not a fan of the game, you have to admit the soundtrack is incredible.
The multiplayer not only excels in making the two players connect and work together, but also provides the same amount of quality as the singleplayer experience. There are a ton of levels and types of levels to toy around with throughout co-op, and easily beats many other games in the co-op aspect.
The workshop for this game is also awesome, there is tons and tons and tons of maps to download and play. The community has really outdone themselves with the amount of downloadable maps and such that are available only a click away.
All of this combined and more makes for one heck of  a gaming experience.

One of my favorite games ever. The creative freedom of a building game, the action of a shooter, all wrapped up on Mars. Really, I'm making this review because I think the community is being really hard on it, and I don't want that to scare off people looking to start this game.
The Good: It's like Legos, but way better. You can build whatever you want, get in fights with other people and their builds, and don't have to worry about stepping on them when you're done playing. The weapons could you a little tweaking, but they are relatively balanced. Each mode of transportation (wheels, hovers, walkers, etc.) each have a tactical role that they specialize in, leaving no resources wasted or made redundant. There's tons of stuff in the works, so there's plenty to look forward to.
The Bad: Like I said the weapons could use a little tweaking, but it won't ruin the game for you. Megas are a little homeless right now, but the devs have said they have plans. In the mean time though, not a whole lot of reason to do Mega builds. There's, like, four maps in rotation, and it's been that way for a very long time. No two games are alike, but knowing that a sniper is going be on THAT rock at THAT time can be a little grating.
The Ugly: The community can be really bipolar. Some people are nice as anything, but others are more toxic than Chernobyl. The community has also been really hard on this game since the anti-overtier update, which makes no sense. The ant-OT system in place now really levels the playing field for everyone, no matter what these yahoos are trying to say. It doesn't limit creativity, it doesn't hurt the game at all, and it isn't that big a deal. The game itself is rock solid, and I can't wait to see where they take it.
TL;DR Great game with lots of creativity and action. The community can be a pain in the rear, but don't let them scare you. Get building and get shooting! And remember, MOAR WHEEL MOAR GUNS

I echo the sentiments of the most recent reviews in that the most recent update turned a good game into a bad one. I had played for a long time, and some time after reaching tier 10 / tx-1, I bought 30 days of premium, and a couple of garage bays. I figured I enjoyed the game so much and got so many hours out of it, why not. About 2 weeks into my premium time, the "competitive" patch came out. I almost instantly stopped playing the game after seeing the changes.
The game was competitive before. But like many games before it, Freejam has ruined its product by yielding to the call of the carebears who decry any and all slight advantages. For example, over tiered robots where somehow considered a blight. These robots that had more powerful guns then most, had also basically no health. While they could kill quick, they could be killed just as quickly if not quicker. Now, these bots, and all other bots that added variety to the game, are gone.
Also, many players, myself included, found good playing time experimenting with lower tier bots. In time, some people spent way more time playing other then tier 10. Freejam killed this.
At the same time Freejam destroyed the variety of builds and battles, they have done nothing to the thing that truly ruins the standard matchups - disconnecting players. Most Standard Battle games have 1 team basically become the loser by default due to disconnecting players. The games turn into laughable lobsided matches.
So, to recap, Freejam lets people ruin competitive matches by letting people disconnect with impunity, while at the same time breaks the game in a patch that ruined peoples' builds.

I downloaded this game after my sister whined for around 1 hour(she doesn't have a Steam account). So we open the game, and we are immediately amazed:you could build whatever you want! While is said so in the description, we expected some limitations,but we were completely free to unleash our creative spirit! Little did we know what was about to happen...
We gladly observed that we had 3 garage slots:one for me,one for her,one for creating derpy madness. I built a really large smg cruiser , she had a smaller,faster SMG cruiser, and for the 3rd garage slot... We created so many things: A penguin like robot, a stick with propellers, a robot child named Br4nd0n(That robot was so cute!), even a bloody TABLE  with a plate on it and a cup,which we drove around in classic mode in tier 1-2.
Tier 1-2, how innocent those tiers were! We experimented and saw other people experimenting: cage-like robots, cubes, robots with the wheels facing inside, hovers, ,robots so large they glitched through the map...
As we progressed in tiers, things got a little more competitive, but we  could still experiment:nano-disruptors,flyers...
In the upper tiers, we ended up with a really heavy armored rail tank with 4 guns for me, and a plasma helicopter for her, but the 3rd garage slot was still random stuff. The more we progressed,the more farming was needed,but we enjoyed every match.
I enjoyed the Overlocked upgrade,even if it had its quirqs. I was kinda confused,to be honest:there were thousands of great ideas for weapons,yet they add another game mode? I enjoyed it,but i saw the community dividing, and people leaving. Sadly,that was the end for the Challange mode, which greatly disappointed me,but I really enjoyed the a-little-more competitive battle mode.
Eventually,i got a little bored(so did my sister) and didn't play for some time. I check the forums,and what do i see? A new update! i was overjoyed! And free premium?! It was incredible!
I enter the game,admire my old tanl, prepare to join the battle... and i can't play. None of my robots worked. My tank was tier 8,but about 10% of it was  t5, and the rest of the chasis was t6. i grinded levels to have more cpu,i farmed money, just to get to this:no robot able to play.
That was a problem the game always had:the prices grow exponentially,the rewards don't. But until this update,i didn't have a problem with it. But now,there is no creativity left. You can't make something colorful,you can't make something unique, you can just watch the forums full of children telling the veteran players to "GIT GOOD IDIOTS". It is hardbreaking,and i never expected to give this game a negative review,but maybe it was meant to be...

Lots of fun with the engineering to build a combat capable robot and actually testing it in combat against a huge amount of different robot designs. This depends on combination of parts, terrain and players.
What is annoying are the number of leavers and rage quit players. The other more annoying thing is the repeat problem of the Steam login giving I/O errors and the network code being not that great since players on my friends list get dropped repeatedly and the network traffic is a huge amount. Because of this bad network nonsense I was tempted several times to uninstall and might still do so if nothing gets done. Players have been complaining for weeks in the forums and nothing happens. This is also why I am not spending money on premium until something gets done.
Some players in the community are making a fuss about art robots. That is something to be considered for maximum rank, but since repeat login issues, robots not saving and other rubbish are slowing down my progress, art is the least of my concern. Besides, I prefer a practically functioning robot to get a win than some monster which is useless in battle. Robots can be made pretty later, but they need to work first.
Edit: Until the developers finally get their network issues sorted out, my review stays negative since I cannot log in for days often. The recent announcement about more developers is no guarantee that the problems will be fixed. The developers also claim that keeping track of Steam forums is too much effort and they want to be mailed. I suspect that they cannot keep track of their emails either.

Let me tell you a tale... the tale of Robocraft!
T'was not that long ago, a little game appeared on Steam by the name of Robocraft. A game where you could build robots of epic looks and sizes, customized to your liking, which could then take part in pvp capture the flag and deathmatches!
For months, Robocraft reigned supreme, topping the Free to Play section for an age. Until, out of nowhere, something happened.
Freejam, the father of Robocraft, became corrupted; their epic plans of bringing a creative, fun game to the people, shattered into a plan for money-grubbing and overcomplication; destroying everything about Robocraft that the people of the world had come to love!
Freejam made Robocraft overcomplicated, adding in many unfair, overly-expensive components that very easily promoted pay-to-win; they Nerfed and Bugged many components to build with, ruining any semblance of balance. They even removed the ability to freely color your creations, limiting you to 3 or 4 ugly, basic colors, locking the rest behind a subscription!!!
Robocraft quickly became hated. Robocraft lost a huge number of its supporters and lovers, who came to despise these changes. "How could you betray us Robocraft?!" They all screamed in anger, "How could you turn from something so amazing into this ♥♥♥♥♥how of a game?!"
Little do they know, that this was not the doing of Robocraft... it was the Father, Freejam, that was slowly trying to kill off Robocraft, sending him into the pits of hell, from where only the most unpleasant and easily-pleased crowd would come to play with Robocraft, forcing him to play through the crappy, ruined, tainted game that he had become.
The Old Followers of Robocraft, however, have not forgotten the joy they had with him, and to this day pray that things will turn around, back into the glory days, and restore peace and fun for all...
Legend has it that Robocraft himself, cries in agony as Freejam shoves more crap at him, forcing him into a monster... a monster which he himself, did not wish to become...

Robocraft is a fun and thrilling game.  You get to build awesome robots and them fight them against others' creations.  As you tier up you get faster, stronger, and altogether cooler parts.  But then you reach t10 and megabots.  And you reach level 100.  Then what else do you have to do?  Sure, you can build more robots, and fight more people, but you run out of interest fast.  This is why I am proposing a plan to liven up the game.  Now I know there are physics engine limitations, and I know that this is a free-to-play game that is run by FreeJam and that we already got more than we deserve, but I think there are ways that with enough effort, Robocraft could develop even further from its amazing state.  'What is your proposition?' you might ask, and I would answer "Water."  Just imagine it- submarines, hydroplanes, and maybe even torpedoes.  All in all, I believe the Robocraft experience would be greatly improved by the addition of water and aquatic robots

If you came here to build epic robots and fight against other amazing creations then I'm afraid to say that you're too late. It seems the developers forgot what made Robocraft an amazing game and why it was so popular and recieved so much praise. The game used to be extremely creative and fun leting you build whatever you wanted as long as the weapons and armor cubes where in check for your tier. The amazing/crazy creations I saw people make was 70% of the fun in the game. From Commander Ackbar from Star Wars (It's a trap) to a giant pony, to Miku riding Nyan cat, from really efficient machines of destruction to epic failures, it was hilarious and fun, something to see.
Now the developers tought it would be a good idea to trash all of this in favor of a competitive MLG Moba game with strict rules and balancing ala League of Legends. Discarting all form of creativity and turning it into a BORING, bland moba with some build options. Every robot is the same and the game play is just ok, this is not worth your time. It seems the developers forgot the Craft part of their title's name, it's plain missleading and a waste.
tl;dr This game used to be an epic build robots / moba game, it's now a mediocre "competitive" moba with no identity or charm. The developers don't listen to feedback and the community is abandoning them in droves. It's sad to see such an amazing game slowly die because the Devs forgot what got them here in the first place.

UPDATE: With the new robocraft: unleashed i expect all of what's been written in this review to be taken away and to make the game better, but read on if you want to.
(In this review I will be summing up what i've heard from other reviews mixed with my own personal opinion, please enjoy)
This game, ooooh this game. When I began playing the game was pre-meta and I had fun with this new, exiting concept of "build your own bot" or as they called it "build, drive, fight". It was an amazing FTP game for the casual as well as the competetive fellow.
And from what I see when meta came some people disliked it turning into a MOBA, but I liked the new style and im sure at least some others did as well. I saw myself slowly teiring up using my tier 5-6 smg filled, low armoured but armor filled gun barrage monster! And I was enjoying myself. Then team orders happened. I was checking in on the new hype around the update but didnt pay enought attention to the actual events other than pings and i thought "this is gonna be great!"
Then, when it finally came out i entered robocraft, looking at my robot with its multiple t6, t5 and i think t4 guns and one t7 smg. But then it struck me that it said I was tier 7, oh what joy! But not for long, because as i was opening the battle menu the game said i needed my bot to have all t6 armor to advance, and I thought "it might only be for higher tiers with this armor restirction, well, back to playing t6 i guess" and replaced it with a t6 smg.
but sadly, my armor still didnt make the cut, and I put the game down. Reading reviews about this had people point the issue towards FreeJam (the creators of Robocraft) listening to the small minority of "elitists". This minority kept bugging FreeJam with the same issues, overtiering, overtiering, overtiering and so on. They told FreeJam they had to limit everything and guess what, they did.
So until FreeJam decides to listen to the majority (that mostly thinks the limits were never needed) I wont play this game again and I wouldnt recommend it either. I hope this review proved useful.
;)

This game is fantastic, I'm utterly appalled at all the downvotes to this game, especially when it seems that a majority of them are about creative purposes, that of which are not broken just because the developer wants to make the game a little more competitive.
I've really enjoyed playing this game just from the small amount of hours I've put into it, and I have only a few complaints. however, I believe the absolute lambasting of this game is completely uncalled for, and that it is a gem. The engine is almost flawless, and I've barely run into any bugs in this game, and this has by far been one of the best alpha states for a game I have ever been a part of.
Gameplay wise the game is very fun and in my opinion fairly balanced as well, with the ability to tune your robot to your playstyle.
My only complaints remain with some UI things, where I believe the building manager could have some better tools like Undo and a 'Move' key that can move select parts. However I know some of the features that I wish to have are on the roadmap anyway, so I can't complain.
Lastly, the platoon limit is something that I'm not a huge fan of. I have a rather big friend group, and I would love it if we could all play together, or get some kind of lobby system so that friends could play together, even with different tiered robots. If there is some way to play with more people than just 3 (I believe paying for a fourth spot is preposterous) then I would honeslty give this game a 9/10
tl;dr
Great game, good engine, play with your friends and have an amazing time.

First off, this game is amazing. I started playing it about two weeks before the ever dreaded "META UPDATE". Frankly, I don't see what everyone is so bent out of shape about. It stopped pros from going down a tier and pwning noobs with overpowered guns, and I'm sure all of the people who are now not getting pwned by pros are happy. I know I am, I never believed in overtiering so you can use a plasma stick to one shot everyone. The other thing that was changed is the minimum armor level, which made people go into battle with at least half decent armor. I don't understand complaints about that either.
This game is a Multiplayer game where you construct robots out of blocks (Minecraft Style) and then attach guns and wheels and hoverblades and thrusters and wings and legs etc. You can basically build anything you can imagine, as you are only limited by your CPU power, which gradually increases throughout the game. You start off with a sprinkling of three different robots, and you can either jump into battle or go to the garage and build a robot from scratch. After every battle, you gain an amount of RoboPoints (For buying parts) and TechPoints (For unlocking new parts). The amount you gain depends on if your team won and what your personal performance was in the battle. As you unlock new parts and blocks, you can build progressivly stronger robots that are able to fight with higher and higher tiers. At the end game you are able to build massive Megarobots in the TX-1 tier that tower above everything else.
I am currently beginning to fight in tier 6 and I have never bought anything. So you can see by my hours that this game doesn't drag on, but it doesn't fly by. I personally think it has a very good pace. If you like FPS games, you will like this, but it also has a sprinkling of strategy in the robotic construction that can get as complicated as you want it.
Have fun Crafting!

Very cool game.
At first, I thought it was just some janky minecraft-shooter knockoff. Its really not.
The concept is pretty simple. Build a combat vehicle, use it to destroy the other team's base. The fun really comes from building and tweaking your fleet of vehicles. Does your fighter jet need more armor to survive anti air snipers? Maybe you should strip some armor for more speed? Maybe what you really need are more guns? Wha if I just made it look cool? These design questions are what really make the game fun.
Even though its in beta, the developers are keeping close tabs on the community, release pretty solid regular updates, and dont endorse a pay-to-win system. The game is free with only cosmetic upgrades costing any real money.
The game is free and a solid gaming experience. What are you waiting for? Pick it up!

This game won IndieDB's Game of the Year for 2014. That alone should speak for itself!
... Except it's no longer that game.
It's been a tough pill to swallow, and I'm still scratching my head over it, but Robocraft is no longer the game I fell in love with nor the game that won GotY '14. I'm not alone in this, either: if you look very carefully, you'll see that almost every review here that was posted after June 2015 is a negative one, with the positive reviews coming from before that fateful month. Robocraft, the entertaining game I
to have, is no longer.
Let me pitch an idea to you:
You have a game where you build a robot out of blocks and triangular "prisms," add guns and some form of mobility like wheels and thrusters, then take it into an arena battle of anywhere from 8v8 to 15v15 players to duel to the death. Your building options include fast-moving wheels, faster-moving hoverblades, wings, helicopter rotors, caterpillar tracks with amazing grip, and insect-like walker legs that cling to walls and ceilings; also included are thrusters for that extra helping of
, and helium for balancing your flier, or if you like making miniature blimps.
As you progress through the game's ten tiers, you unlock more and more cool things to play with, and the colour of your armor changes along the way; plus, as you level up to 100, a special "CPU cap" increases, allowing you to build bigger and better robots. You can build whatever you like, be it a bot that's designed for pure functionality, or a big ol' statue of Garfield the cat that rolls around on tank tracks with railguns for sniping. The artistic potential is endless; but wait, there's more! If you want to actually do well in this game, you'll have to learn to build better as well. On the battlefield, you literally only get one single life, so the tougher your bot is, the longer you survive, and the better your team's odds of winning the match. Learn the damage mechanics, learn better armoring techniques, and suddenly even your Garfield statue can be an intricate, battle-ready monster... While looking as goofy as ever.
Sounds good, right? It was; I dumped a thousand hours into that game in the six months I played it. But then came the Robo-Moba.
The PvP arena team deathmatch mechanic was repetitive at times, but that was probably mostly due to the fact that the game only has five maps, which get REALLY stale after the first month or so. But then, the devs decided they wanted to be another League of Legends or Dota, with their own block-building spin on it. The problem with this is that a game like Robocraft - free-to-play, and oriented around building blocks - primarily attracts from the 8-14 age range, and this is NOT the demographic for a complicated tower-capture moba setup.
What Robocraft is NOW is a game in which you run out into the field, and instead of shooting the enemy bots to win the game, you shoot the stationary crystals on the enemy base. That's it. There's no point in being tactical, because you respawn if you die now, so neither death nor your building ability matter as much any more. Plus, the new gamemode has introduced "overclocking," a mechanic which increases your weapon power as you continue in a match, without increasing armor HP; this has resulted in making bots even MORE squishy as the game continues, so whether they're well-designed or not they all die in moments. Why take the time to build smart when you can just slap guns on a brick, charge in, and do just as well?
On top of this, the movement parts have all gotten progressively slower and less appealing since the update. Wheels and hoverblades barely go faster than tank tracks now, meaning you have absolutely no hope of outrunning enemy fire. Wings have so little HP that you lose an entire wing from a single randomly-sprayed SMG shot. The matchmaker is terrible, often putting three medics on the enemy team while giving you none at all (!). This is an incredible game. It's developed by 5 guys! Yep, only 5 people work on this MMO. Let it sink in. Only 5. Most mmo's require teams of 100's and budgets of millions of dollars, but the fact that this indie studio can pull a game off this good is incredible enough!
And the game itself is very well done, and it being in early stages right now, I am excited to see it's future! Gameplay itself is quite simple, destroy the enemy base, and with 3 towers in the field that can give buffs if you control them, essentially. It kinda reminds me of games like WoT, or War thunder, but dumbed down a bit. But the best part of the game is the fact that you build your own machine! I spent atleast an hour just trying to engineer my perfect war machine that fits my play style. And I also went through a ton of trial and error to get there! Action in battle is fast paced, with some tactics needed. (It's not tactic heavy, unfortunately)
The graphics are not the best, but the art direction is! This game looks  good. It doesn't need fancy shadows and what have you, it looks good. And to top it all off, it runs like a dream!
Now one thing all MMO's have trouble with is payment... the genre is plagued with "pay to win", "pay to play" blah blah blah. But this game does it right! (Indie pride!!!) You pay for cosmetics and convenience, which is how most free to play games should be. So you can pay for stuff like earning RP faster, earning tech points faster, more garage slots, pre-built monsters, (which isn't op because you could technically make it yourself) cosmetic parts, (unfortunetly there isn't to much yet, but more will come) and the ability to pay for more blocks using real currency. And fortunetly, you can't pay for a million blocks to create a super OP robo, since they cap you on "flops". (Which is essentially the value of each piece) So even though you may have a ton of pieces, you won't be able to use them. This may sound really restricting, but it really makes you plan out and design great things. So your designs aren't abut quanity, it's about quality. This is a great system! So why would you pay to get more blocks? Convenience. At higher levels, it defintly would take a lot more time to get enough blocks to creat the machine of your dreams.
This game is really fun!  All around, it's well worth playing. It looks good, and it has a great team of people behind it! I am super excited for the future of this game! It's free, and will only take 5-20 minutes to download, so heck, just try it out!
P.S. the prices of the game are also very very reasonable. A 12 month subscription is a little less than $50. (Considering most mmo's will charge you over $100 for 12 months, this is a steal) Also a lot of the cosmetics only cost change!
