There are different types of game mode you can play in game:
-Battle mode
-Classic mode
-Challenge mode
-Megaboss mode
-Practice mode
In battle mode, your main objective is to destory emery base. You and your teammate can become more powerful by killing the emery bots or capture the three towers located in the map. As of the current update, three towers are refered as top, middle and bottom according to your mini-map.
This game mode usually take a long time before finish, approximate 15-20 minutes. But your will always receive a large amount of rewards.
In classic mode, the objective is simple. either kill all emery or capture the emery base by staying at emery base for some time. This mode gives super fast game experience, normally less than 5 minutes. If your team win, you walk out with a suitable amount of rewards. If your team lost, you can still get a small amount of payback for your hard work in game.
Challenge mode is only avaliable after you reach tier 6. It's a mode take 4 high tier bots to fight against 12+ lower tier bots. The objective as a challenger is much simplar than classic, kill all the emery bots. Nothing much needed to say in this mode. JUST KILL THEM ALL.
Megaboss mode is completely the same as challenge mode but this mode only avaliable to mega bot which is idenified as Tier TX-1.
Nothing needed to say for practice mode. A test ground for your bots. However the practive mode currently is not quite realistic to what your bot actually performs in other game mode. The reason is that the team FJ is too busy to fix stuffs from other mode and changes from update. Hopefully they will come to have a look in practice mode some day.
That's all about the basic of this game you really need to know if you are new to this game. As a new player to this game, you don't need to worry about lots of the other reviews complainting about. They are mostly irrelvent to new player.
As a new player, what you need to do in this game is to build your own bot and fight to the death in different game modes. Just use your imagination and construct your own beast.
And when you go into fight, you gain level and build bigger bot. As your bot getting bigger, your bot will go to next tier. Then you upgrade your bot to fight. However i can tell you that there is no end point of this game. TX-1 is not the end. It just give you another way to build your own machine. You can always go back to lower tier and fight to the death alongside with the lower tier players. Don't just narrow your own goal to reaching TX-1.
Overall i strongly recommend that you, as a new player, to experience this great game. If robocraft doesn't fit you, it's ok. At least you now know there is a game call robocraft in the market. If you like this game, please tell your friends about this game. Write down some good reviews. Let's work together and make robocraft community become bigger and stronger.

Portal 1 had made history. Valve had created a hit on a relatively small budget. The question now was: what’s next? Would there be a sequel? Could Portal handle the AAA deluxe treatment? Well, Valve remained the same Valve as ever. Quiet and secretive about any potential plans for the series. But in the background, work had already begun on a sequel. The team and scope was expanded dramatically. New mechanics and ideas were experimented with. It wouldn’t be until three years later in March 2010 and a patch to Portal 1’s ending that the world would learn of the coming sequel. However, Valve worked on Valve time and despite the original release date being August 2010, it wouldn’t be until April 2011 that Portal 2 would finally hit the shelves. It released to resounding applause and critical acclaim. The question was answered: Portal could be a fully featured AAA experience and still have all the best parts of the original.
Portal 2 features has three main components that you can play in. The solo campaign of around 10 hours that features the main characters of the Portal universe in a rather epic storyline. There’s the co-op campaign of around 5-6 hours that features a more lighthearted and fun storyline, with two new robot characters and GLaDOS directing their actions. Finally, there’s the Steam Workshop section, where you can test community developed chambers or design your own puzzles for both solo and co-op players. How many hours you’ll get out of this depends upon you but you can experience quite a lot if you want to. These are generally logic puzzles that require a lot of methodical thinking through the solution, with some exhilarating sections to shake things up. You’ll need to take your time and have patience to figure them out. As far as the Valve-crafted puzzles go, they should be solvable on your own. I only used a guide for two particularly difficult puzzles towards the end of the solo campaign and that was mostly because I couldn’t figure out one step in the solution. In the co-op campaign, you probably won’t need any help so long as you and your partner work together.
An unknown number of years have passed since the events of Portal 1. Chell is awakened from a long hibernation sleep to a very different Aperture Laboratories. The place is falling apart without the direction of GLaDOS or the team of scientists killed by the now deceased AI. Chell is awakened by a quirky personality core named Wheatley, who helps her progress through the ruins of Aperture. Wheatley is...a idiot as described by GLaDOS. But a funny idiot. Chell hopes that his assistance will lead to her finally escaping from Aperture Laboratories, a place that seems bound and determined to keep her here. Along the way though, mistakes were made (by Wheatley) and GLaDOS is awakened again. She’s furious at having been blown up by Chell in Portal 1 and is determined to make sure Chell pays for killing her. By making her advance the limits of science via some test chambers, of course. Duh. That’s what we all do to our arch enemies. It’s just so obvious.
Portal 2 has a lot of settings at your disposal to create the optimal experience for any rig, even low-end ones. Bit of a side note, but I’m glad that Portal 2 explains every setting in detail when you configure it. Far too many companies forget to add these explanations on what each setting does and it can be confusing to go through this menu without those helpful tooltips. Anyway, in the video settings you have the expected aspect ratios with multiple resolution configurations of up to at least 1080p. There’s fullscreen, borderless window and windowed mode along with a laptop power savings mode. Anti-aliasing supports MSAA and CSAA up to 8x and 16X respectively. Anisotropic filtering goes up to 16X and there’s v-sync up to Triple buffered along with multicore rendering. Shader Detail, Effect Detail and Model/Texture detail have low/medium/high settings. Portal 2 is optimized well enough that even low-end hardware can run the game without too many issues. That being said, there are loading screens between every level which can be tiresome. But, at least we get flashy animations to watch while we wait. Portal 2 really refines the look that Portal 1 started and I really like it. Between the overgrown areas, the bright and distinctive colors with the dystopian feel to it, Portal 2 really stands out.
Audio settings allow for multiple speaker configurations and audio quality. Master volume and music are the only sliders you can mess with. Closed captioning and voice can be enabled or disabled as well. You can also fully rebind your keys, change mouse sensitivity and acceleration as well as reverse the mouse for left handed people. The game also supports controllers with plenty of options from vibration, stick sensitivity, button layouts (custom support) and more. Portal 2 has pretty much everything you’ll need to run it on your machine and I haven’t noticed anything significant missing.
Portal 2 is one of my favorite games I’ve had the pleasure of playing. It’s a rare sequel where it stands on its own, building upon what came before but feeling fresh and unique the entire time. It cleverly avoids being a rehash of ideas, jokes or character arcs. The heavily expanded sequel comes with plenty of a solo campaign to chew on, new puzzles and refined mechanics, a new co-operative campaign and the backstory of Aperture Laboratories. The campaign is well done in general, though I felt like the ending started to drag a bit. The Co-Op campaign is also very enjoyable and is worth tackling
you get the right friend to do it with. While both campaigns don't offer any real reason to replay them, that’s where the Steam Workshop and modding community come in. With over 450,000+ puzzles to choose from, you’re spoiled for choice. There’s puzzles that introduce user-created mechanics, new campaigns with their own unique storylines and a plethora of simple test chambers to try and solve. Science is fun, Portal 2 is fun and it gets one of my highest recommendations to give it a go.
If you love puzzles, this is the game for you ^^

This is a great game.  You'll find hours of free fun play, free promo codes to at times help you progress levels quicker, but progress is fine without them.  And you don't need to pay to win.  Though I spend a little to support the game, it was that good.
Ever complain about the base weapon/character you start a game with?   Now you build you own, so if you have a bad bot, it's your fault not the game.
And they recently added a fix that, though you'll hear players complain about, it is a great fix.  It basically prevents higher level players from using their rp/money and higher tech items, stripped down, to join lower level battles, kill newbies, and do nothing but make gaming unfun for others, which trolls call "fun".
There are only 1 downside  to the game, but it shouldn't prevent you from playing.  The main issue is the Megas.  You get all this creativity and choices when building bots on tech tiers 1-10, flyers, hovercraft, wheels, drone, tank tread, 3 shoot weapon choices, healer, and a tesla/melee weapon.  But as soon as you get to Mega, you get wheels, that is it.  Eventually, you can get a hovercraft after you have played with wheels for a while.  And your only gun choice is SMG, eventually you can get a plasma after you played a while.
So all the skill, tactics, and bot engineering you did to learn and get good at your favorite type, all goes out the window.  Wheels are clunky, they don't turn good with megas, and the SMG guns on the megas blow up with a single hit, making a  mega in battle quite useless without a pocket medic.
Megas lack style, most look alike because you'll find there are only a few good designs, and there have been calls for "Mega on Mega" only battles, but what's the point?  It would just be a a bunch of trucks with smg's shooting at each other, having trouble turning around, unable to climb hills or over obstacles like lower class characters.  The winner would always be the last mega who had a gun left, that didn't get shot off.
Overall, a great game, and if they allowed megas the diversity of every other level,  megas would truly be what there name was, a terrifying machine of destruction.

I give this game an 8/10. It's only flaw is a lack of gamemodes.

The thing is, this was already a fair use because 1. The flak is less accurate while movine. This means you had to get close to another flyer. and 2. Ground based flak due to their accuracy still makes any flyer run, and flak on air doesn't have any effect on ground units. So now my style, my tatic, what was fun for me, is gone and I have to re learn the game. I like the game, but I don't want to do that today. So I'm done for a while. Months ago I have recommended this to many friends. I've worked my butt off to TX-1 (Though never actually made a working TX-1, just T10) Now with the Competitive updates, the fun of the game has dwindled, the rage has increased,  and the matches have become competitive with many exploits. Yes, some exploits are strategical, but the CPU capped bots I've seen are down right wrong and mostly trolling AFKers.
Many art bots I used to see in the lower tiers, though not very competitive, were still fun to watch or even shoot. Now we hardly see any, and if any, look like crap due to the caps on low/hightier armor usage. I had a nice heli bomber that was nice to look at, and be effective in Tier 8. After the last update, it was half way into Tier 9. I replaced all the T9 blocks and jammers (2) with T8 blocks and T7 jammers. Not only can I be easily shot down in a few SMG shots, unlike the many Rail shots I could take, my bot looks flat out bland.
They should take out the concern of over tiering and CPU caps after Tier 5. T10 may seem to be where the real game begins, no one is going to make it to the end of the race and do the exact same over and over. I play multiple tiers for the change, and occasionally help low tier players with their questions while ingame, along with tips on taking towers and smg firing. However, it's hard to show my hard work ingame, besides the tag infront of my name in chat, when I have boths that are nearly 90%+ same tier and no upper tiering.
Out of my group of 8 other friends I used to play with, I'm the last to leave the game. I do hope things improve soon. I do play some, but generally Tier 4 batles if you want to catch me sometime ingame.

THIS IS TECHNICALLY A NEGATIVE REVIEW, BUT...
I'd like to start by saying I have really enjoyed this game. The construction system is fairly effecient, and you used to be able to make pretty much anything you want and still pit it against others, and the devs are always working on something new for you to build/destroy.
I couldn't even bring myself to say I wouldn't recommend it since I know things could change for the better again.
The problem is, though, that the world doesn't need another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ MOBA game. I like DOTA as much as the next guy but Robocraft was something else; something different - at least before they starting putting in restrictions as to what you could do with your bots and who you could play against. I'm not implying that style of play/game mode should be removed, but even the early access description says it was supposed to be more of an mmo, and a fun, casual experience. Why change that? At the very least we should be provided with access to  a more free-form style of group play. (Games have been letting players customize mp match settings since Win95. Get with it, guys.)
The Robocraft community wants to build crazy robots and blow them to pieces with friends.
We don't care if it's "pro gaming" eligible or if someone has a better computer so they get a 3ms advantage in combat.
We don't care what you recommend that we do with our designs either. Half the fun of the game was in trying to create something no one else was using. Now your best bet is to cover a barrel in guns and not bother with moving at all. Just fly straight into the air and fire down at everyone. Sounds super fun right?  ... right?  ........oh. Maybe competition isn't everything after all.
I sincerely hope that a game that could be great won't be rendered mediocre by its developer's desire to cash in on a trend. Robocraft is too cool for that sh*t.

tl;dr This game was amazing. With all the negative changes they keep adding, don't spend any money on this, free play is worth it.
I used to recommend this game, but I can do that no longer.
The last couple updates have ruined the gameplay, ship building, and more. Every update in the last couple months has been a complete change of the game and none of it has been fun. The devs are good, but their vision and updates are terrible. It used to be a fun game of building and attacking (see old review below). Now it's just a "see what curveball the devs will throw this update." All these changes do is ruin your loadouts and the enjoyability of the game.
I have over 50 days of premium left from what I bought and I don't even feel like playing anymore. That should give you an idea what the updates keep doing. This used to be one of my top games, now it's a game that I wish I hadn't spent money on. It's more than ok for a free game, but I do not recommend spending any money on this game. If you do you will likely regret it as I have.
This is a warning for Early Access games, they will change, and the money you spent won't come back. There needs to be a way to differentiate am early access game that will change completely and one that will just be polished. It would be nice to see an Alpha and Beta classification on these things. As Alpha typically means the core game is still being developed and implemented and may not work correctly. And Beta where the core game is present and won't be changed except to squash bugs and add extra armor, blocks, etc. This game mentions that they are in Early Alpha, but it's obvious that the core mechanics are in place, and they only use that designation to justify changes at even the core level.
It's frustrating to think that the game that was stable and running great for my 140 exceedingly fun hours over the last year is now a different game that I don't feel like playing anymore. Thanks a lot devs.
----Begin old review----
Incredibly fun game. Here's the skinny:
You get blocks and guns and make a car/tank/ship/hovercraft/train... anything you want (within a set "power" limit)
then you test your bot out to make sure it operates right
then you battle other player's creations
It's that simple, and so much fun.
Yes it's free. I just unlocked Tier 3 and so far other players can be good or bad. Regardless if people spend money, whatever tier you want to fight on, you have to be within a power limit. If some guy wants to put a tier 4 gun on a tier 1 match ship, then he's basically a crap car with 4 wheels, a chair and a gun. so easy to take out.. as long as you can dodge, or take the hit. The game has a unique way of allowing you to unlock stuff through money or by grinding, but either way, the design of your craft and your ability to pilot it (especially when damaged) is what wins overall.
Watch out for the snipers, they float over bases and try and take you out, then there's the armored tanks that slam you with damage while being able to take more damage. Then there's the hovercrafts that try and fly over to take your team's base... the list goes on and on.
I'm shocked this game is free as it's the most fun I've had in a long time.
----End old review----

Game was fun? Yes. Game was much fun before it became Robo-MOBA.
The "Classic" mode made you think about designing your robot for longevity, since you do not respawn. Forced you to think outside of the box(Wahaha), get creative! But why not just play Classic mode then? Simple: just not the most rewarding mode anymore.
And Robo-MOBA? If you have more guns and more blocks, you'll be winning more. It's no fun when the most practical design is a brick on catepillar treads. Or a brick covered in panels, on catepillar treads. It's become boring! Confusing! For up to half an hour or longer! All for a reward that's just too little. And if you do feel you got big reward, what do? Make a tougher brick with tougher guns with tougher catepillar treads.
Cook had fun with this game, yes, but the 60 or so hours were spent before Robo-MOBA hit. What came after was trying to enjoy Robo-MOBA and disliking it.
If you want MOBA with robo-bricks, you'll love this game! Making robots and making them fight, fun! But personally, I think the point of the game, making a creative or practical design that's cool, tough, but powerful, was killed.
I mean hei, who needs to make something smart and live long if you come back anyway?
Just don't forget-- the only thing this game costs will be your time and some hard drive space.

Ingredients

Directions
1 Cut thin slice from stem end of each bell pepper to remove top of pepper. Remove seeds and membranes; rinse peppers. If necessary, cut thin slice from bottom of each pepper so they stand up straight. In 4-quart Dutch oven, add enough water to cover peppers. Heat to boiling; add peppers. Cook about 2 minutes; drain.
2 In 10-inch skillet, cook beef and onion over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beef is brown; drain. Stir in rice, salt, garlic and 1 cup of the tomato sauce; cook until hot.
3 Heat oven to 350°F.
4 Stuff peppers with beef mixture. Stand peppers upright in ungreased 8-inch square glass baking dish. Pour remaining tomato sauce over peppers.

Portal 2 is still my favorite puzzle game to this day and is also one of my favorite games of all time. Portal 2 is the drastic improvement of the original Portal with amazing voice acting, story telling, and gameplay. You play as the character Chell who wakes up in containment and is thrust back into her old surroundings as a former test subject. There is a deeper story to this game that I'm not going to spoil in this review, but it is a good one. As you may have figured out already, you are equipped with one weapon: A portal gun. This gun creates two holes on any white surface, one orange, one blue, in which you and other objects can pass through. You goal is to use this gun and a variety of other testing elements to help you complete many test chambers and get through hours of puzzles. The great thing about this game is that the dialouge, the story, and the sheer joy of completing a test chamber is enough to keep you addicted to this game. But you have to actually PLAY the game for yourself to enjoy it and appreciate how well-crafted it is. I'm such a huge fan of portal that not only have I played through it on steam, but I've also played it multiple times on my 360. The other great thing about this game is the Co-op, which offers many more hours of fun gameplay and humourus moments in a whole nother story with two unique characters: Atlas and P-Body. I CANNOT reccomend this game enough.

I would reccomend this game as well as the first to anyone who hasn't heard or played it. It was on sale when my friend bought it for me and it hasn't been a waste of money in any case. It runs super well on default settings on my laptop. I get 40-60 fps in this game, and 10-25 fps in Counter Strike: Global Offensive, just to give you an idea on how easy it runs.

First off as a person who's been playing robocraft for quite a while, I want to say 1 thing;
Robocraft has changed alot over the past year, it is no longer a teir based game about building a thick shield around one single item on your robot (the pilot seat) but instead is what the game always advertised; a game about comeing up with a cool yet effective robot that you can take out into team based online matches and battle your enemies.
Currently Robocraft's mechanics are pretty easy to understand, you build a robot using parts you bought or were given in supply crates and use it in certain online gamemodes. there are quite a few wepon and movement options to chose but you dont even have to pick only one, I built a sniper robot that can walk around with insect legs but also fly away if its in danger, I'v even seen people who created helicopters that have wheels so they can drive away if they get shot down.
Robocraft (at the moment) is mostly a great game that i'd reccomend to anyone who likes the idea of creating their own completely customizable robot that can liturally be anything.
PROS:
Robots are completely customizable
There are a ton of different movement and wepon options
there are quite a few gamemodes to play ( including sinlge player)
CONS:
getting the parts you want may some take time
some wepons are slighly unbalanced

Well... Portal 2. It's one of my favorite games of all time, but it's so hard to review. So let's start with the basic info.
Portal 2 is a puzzle/fpp game released by valve in 2011 for ps3, xbox360 and pc. It's the sequel
to Portal, a game featured on valve's orange box. It uses the source engine.
But what do i think about the game itself?
I think Portal 2 is the best game Valve has ever released and I think it's a true masterpiece.
The first three chapters are your usual testing. You solve some fairly easy puzzles, you listen to
GlaDOS' dialogue. But you can see that a long time has passed
Other chapters change locations within aperture science, you learn some backstory.
And you
But the best part of the game is the ending. This one of the best endings of all time.
It answers almost all questions, but it leaves you...
I just don't know what to say the feeling after the ending is so special that there is only
one other ending that i can compare this to, but i won't say what game it is.
Anyway it also has a co-op mode which is pretty good. It's fun for the first playthrough, but then it get's boring.
The graphics are good, considering that the source engine is turning 13 this year.
The music is awesome. The elecronic tracks fit the game perfectly. And I think both the ending tracks are much better that Still Alive which i personally didn't like.
And that's all. I think I could write a bit more, but I don't like to. This was my first paid game on steam (my first game was Team Fortress 2) and I loved it from the first time I played it.
I really recommend this game to everyone!

Portal 2 is still my favorite puzzle game to this day and is also one of my favorite games of all time. There is a deeper story to this game that I'm not going to spoil in this review, but it is a good one. As you may have figured out already, you are equipped with one weapon: A portal gun. This gun creates two holes on any white surface, one orange, one blue, in which you and other objects can pass through. You goal is to use this gun and a variety of other testing elements to help you complete many test chambers and get through hours of puzzles. The great thing about this game is that the dialouge, the story, and the sheer joy of completing a test chamber is enough to keep you addicted to this game. Despite its predecessor being nearly perfect, Portal 2 is even better, introducing new mechanics, new characters, and new atmosphere. And while it is not absolutely necessary to have played the original Portal, it is highly recommended.
Starting off where Portal ended, you are a test subject for for Aperture Science that wakes up in a stasis chamber, only to be put back into stasis for tens of thousands of years. Until, the facility's power runs out and you awaken.
Being set so long after the events of Portal 1, there has been enough time for much of the Aperture facility to be reclaimed by nature or to just fall apart from age. This introduces new atmosphere that makes progressing through the game much less repetitive.
Throughout the story, more and more mechanics come into play and are utilized by their integration into the world. This allows for more diverse and enjoyable puzzles to be solved. From Aerial Faith Plates, to Propulsion gel, puzzles continue to get more complicated and more interesting.
With a compelling story, an atmospheric and unique world, and many interesting mechanics to use, Portal 2 is a must have for anyone that enjoys action, story-driven, atmospheric, or puzzle games. 95/100

I rate Portal 2, 3.5/5. Pretty good.
This is a solidly built game with not a single bug that I noticed and is perhaps one of the more simultaneously stressful and exhilarating games I have recently played (so stressful that like the first Portal game, I do not see myself ever wanting to play this game again). I think it is also the most topsy-turvy, vertiginous game I have ever played (even more so than Forsaken in some ways). The plot is simple (with basically the same goal as the first Portal game, to escape the facility). The graphics are wonderful (and interestingly styled, in an ultra-utilitarian and extremely clean and often stark manner), the gameplay is intellectually challenging (and often mind-bending), but I found the characters to be largely irritating distractions with primarily unfunny jokes. Generally the game feels like whoever wrote the dialogue for it may have thought that they were far more funny than they actually were. The game feels full of itself oftentimes. Most jokes fell flat (for me) though the ones that were funny really were excellent in an absurdist sort of way. The funniest thing in the game, the corrupted fact core, I have posted in the comments below. Overall this game is a very oddly balanced combination of intellectual challenge, stress, fun and irritation. Playing it I found to be a sort of intellectually masochistic experience...probably a fun enough game to play through once...but I would not want to repeat the experience.
Pros: Great, interestingly styled, clean graphics, no bugs at all, great controls, great sound, interesting (though occasionally annoying) music, lots of intellectual, mind-bending challenge throughout, intense (but up to and past the point of being stressful), If you are good ad 3-dimensional visual-spacial reasoning this game will make you feel very intelligent as you run through the game solving puzzle after puzzle in 10 minutes or less, good ending which makes me want to go outside and not be in by my computer for a while. A great final-boss level with an excellent, surprising, truly funny ending, the designers left the best parts of this game to the end.
Cons: Linear gameplay with puzzles which mostly have only one essential answer, only 1 ending, graphics can seem a bit stark at times (though this is part of the game's inherent uniqueness, irritating, largely unfunny characters, If you're good at the game the game can be quite short (but I got the game for only 5 dollars),
I also Wish they had more game modes and maps but over all, the best free game ive ever played in my life.

No idea why I am reviewing this game, but here we go.
Portal.  Play it.  Play it now.  Easily one of my top three favorite games of all time, Portal is amazing in every way.  From creative dialog to the now-famous mechanics, there’s not much I can say about this game in a broad sense that has not already been said.  Both the single player and co-op modes are fully realized and are a ton of fun to play through, time and time again.  It’s one of those games you can play thirty times and still find humor or something new in it.
Now the thing I can really say stuff about - the achievements.  I’m a hardcore completionist, and my work on Portal was some of the most fun I have had, grinding at the same level over and over again.  To get all 51 achievements, you not only need to complete both the single player and co-op campaigns, but you also must discover more obscure things hidden within levels.  The non-story based ones range in difficulty from fairly simple (if you know what you’re doing) to brutally complicated (Still Alive and Smash TV - I’m looking at you here).  It took me 30 hours to complete all the achievements.  With this in mind, it’s clear to see that it’s a doable task, yet not the thing for everyone. (but let’s say that the joy I got upon getting that last achievement was pretty great.)
Seriously go play this game now, your life will never be the same.
Overall rating: 10/10

***This review is for the story mode of Portal 2 only***
This is overall a worthy successor to Portal. In terms of gameplay, at least. The puzzles are infinitely more fun and varied, and there is so much richness that comes with the section of the game devoted to backstory.
Sadly, it all comes at the expense of altering the tone of the whole game. Your original antagonist, GLADoS, is back--but is nothing like the cold, humourless, emotionless AI who ran the facility in the first game. There are some possible fridge logic reasons for this, but nothing is stated in-game about her personality change. It's a jarring note and it almost destroys the first game's experience as a result. Almost.
The othe rmain character, a robot which helps you escape the crumbling facility and get to safety is called Wheately. Wheatley is funny in a bumbling way, completely at odds with the tone of what Portal was. In a roundabout way, his manner can be related to the plot, but it doesn't fit with what you are expecting. Portal.  Play it.  Play it now.  Easily one of my top three favorite games of all time, Portal is amazing in every way. Seriously go play this game now, your life will never be the same.

In case you don't know, Robocraft has had a couple of years in Alpha to evolve into a game loved by the community. It's still on its way to even Beta, and doesn't seem to show it. This is an amazing game for designing and for shooting: you build a fearsome (or at first not so fearsome) robot, take a few seconds to marvel at it, and fight with it. Because of the nature of the design process, no two bots are the same. A variety of weapons and movement types mean you could have any kind of bot that appeals to you. Scorpion-like snipers, Lancaster Bombers, floating medics and lumbering SMG tanks are but a few examples.
The actual battle involves a true test of piloting skill. You drive, fly, or walk your bot to the objective, to either capture or destroy it. The original game mode requires a King-of-the-Hill type of victory, while the new one involves destroying Protonium Fusion Towers to deactivate the enemy forcefield and destroy their reactor.
Seriously, I'd recommend it. It's free, the developers listen to reason, it takes you on a learning curve, and it's a great way to improve design skills.
Why are you still reading this? Download the game; you won't regret it! 9.99/10
Edit: I haven't actually played this in a while. There have been a lot of updates since I made this review, and I'll say this now: it is NOT the same game anymore. They've tried to make it 'meta' and easier for younger players I guess, and have kind of forsaken the original vision of the game. It's still OK as far as I'm aware, but that 9.99/10 is probably now a 6.5/10. It's a shame, really.

Then another character comes into the story. A core named Wheatley comes knocking on your door. You want to know who it is, so obviously, you open it. He comes in, talks for a bit, and then the room starts moving, smashing into walls, until you jump out. Then you are put into a whole lot of test chambers. I could beat most of them, some of them it took me a bit to figure them out. What I really didn't like was how Wheatley, my favorite character, turns into the bad guy. I've beaten the game, and my favorite chapter is 'The Part Where He Kills You', so sometimes, if I don't want to play from the beginning, I will play that chapter. So, my favorite part of that chapter is when I'm in his lair. I know what to do, how to do it, but I think it's cool when I shoot a portal to the moon, and everything gets sucked in. It really stands out to me when GLaDOS deletes Caroline, and her voice changes, I don't like how she gets rid of me. I like the ride up, the singing turrets and all that, I don't like how I'm in a feild with no city around me, or no building around me. If she was going to get rid of me, why not leave me close to a city? I really think they should make a free Portal three game of me getting back into the building, hanging out with GLados, Wheatley coming back and apologizing and bemcoming friends with us again, and let me be able to go out to the city, live in a house, and be able to visit GLaDOS and Wheatley. I really want to see what happens after that. I don't like how GLaDOS got rid of me, and how there's no city near me, and how I don't know what happens after that. I really want Valve to make another Portal.

This is a solidly built game with not a single bug that I noticed and is perhaps one of the more simultaneously stressful and exhilarating games I have recently played (so stressful that like the first Portal game, I do not see myself ever wanting to play this game again). I think it is also the most topsy-turvy, vertiginous game I have ever played (even more so than Forsaken in some ways). The plot is simple (with basically the same goal as the first Portal game, to escape the facility). The graphics are wonderful (and interestingly styled, in an ultra-utilitarian and extremely clean and often stark manner), the gameplay is intellectually challenging (and often mind-bending), but I found the characters to be largely irritating distractions with primarily unfunny jokes. Generally the game feels like whoever wrote the dialogue for it may have thought that they were far more funny than they actually were. The game feels full of itself oftentimes. Most jokes fell flat (for me) though the ones that were funny really were excellent in an absurdist sort of way. The funniest thing in the game, the corrupted fact core, I have posted in the comments below. Overall this game is a very oddly balanced combination of intellectual challenge, stress, fun and irritation. Playing it I found to be a sort of intellectually masochistic experience...probably a fun enough game to play through once...but I would not want to repeat the experience.
Pros: Great, interestingly styled, clean graphics, no bugs at all, great controls, great sound, interesting (though occasionally annoying) music, lots of intellectual, mind-bending challenge throughout, intense (but up to and past the point of being stressful), If you are good ad 3-dimensional visual-spacial reasoning this game will make you feel very intelligent as you run through the game solving puzzle after puzzle in 10 minutes or less, good ending which makes me want to go outside and not be in by my computer for a while. A great final-boss level with an excellent, surprising, truly funny ending, the designers left the best parts of this game to the end.
Cons: Linear gameplay with puzzles which mostly have only one essential answer, only 1 ending, graphics can seem a bit stark at times (though this is part of the game's inherent uniqueness, irritating, largely unfunny characters, If you're good at the game the game can be quite short (but I got the game for only 5 dollars),

I loved this game, and I still do. It's like finding out that someone you loved came down with dementia or something like that. It was heartbreaking to find that the game I loved once before was now little more than a game that you would need to pour lots of money into to get an enjoyable time. I still love Robocraft. I still do. But it's not quite the same love that got me into the game, to get over 500 hours under my belt in this game and an appreciation for the community.
The community is degrading due to these changes, everyone is becoming more malicious than ever. We're all frustrated by these changes. The Robocraft we loved has been wounded by Epic Loot, this crate system crippling the enjoyment of this game.
I would wait it out. I bet one day we'll get through this and the Robocraft I loved would return, and our suffering would not be in vain. But for now, I'll hold my head high, grin and bear it, and wait, like many other fellow Robocrafters.

WAS the Awesomenes Construction Simulator 2014. That is what this game WAS. Note that I'm a Tier 9 and have just recently played this game to update my review.
I have Built:
M-35 Mako from Mass Effect 1
M-44 Hammerhead from Mass Effect 2.
UT-47A Kodiak from Mass Effect 3.
Terran Diamondback from Starcraft 2.
Terran Ar♥♥♥♥e Mercenary Siege Tank. (YES. THE SIEGE BREAKER FROM WINGS OF LIBERTY.)
But none of that matters when the base physics of the game have been modified from what was established, the weapons continuously nerfed until being 6 feet under, Rewards being lowered with "Improvments to the system", and a plethora of other problems.
Back in early 2014 I STRONGLY, I repeat, STRONGLY supported this game. STRONGLY, I emphasize this, say it with me. STRONGLY... SUPPORTED THIS GAME. But with every step forward, FreeJam has shown they intend to take two steps back every time.
- "Clone Wars"
So let's first start off with the removal of all the nice cool gadgets that were originally available right at the start. This included the Hoverblades, Plasma launchers, Railguns, and thrusters. From level 1 upward of Level 3. Yes, this happened. Freejam didn't change THIS until 7 months later, when people stopped crying and moaning for it to come back.
- "Double Edged Butt-♥♥♥♥ery"
Now PRIOR to this, they also made some modifications to the reward system, adding a "Repair function" to the game, which put a drain on casual players Tiers 6 and up back then. What was the kick in the balls here? a 25% decrease in rewards. Yes, BOTH RP and TP (Robopoints and Techpoints).
- "Hero Zero"
Next up was the "Hero System", which allowed you to get the full RP and TP from a match you died in if your team won, but WAIT! ...At the cost of the entire reward system getting another 25% decrease. At this point, managing to make enough money to get new parts was an uphill battle, and at a 50% reward decrease that has remained permanent to this day, It's been a massive pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
- "Turn up for Hate"
Now, next up, THEY REMOVE repair cost, yet YET again, ANOTHER FREAKING REWARD QUANTITY DECREASE. You getting the pattern yet? Don't worry I'll explain it in a second. At this point, it got rediculous, but oh no, there's even MORE.
- "From Intense to Indense"
This game was always a One-life team Death Match game. The "Respawned and Overclocked" update has killed everything that made it original and turned it into a confused MOBA wannabe. Even worse, is that they've now set the original mode, now named "Classic" So far on the back burner it can take from 5 minutes to 3 hours just to get on a match, gradually decreasing the time needed to even get into one with each tier you go up. But here's the final blow to the old mode: A 80% decrease at this point... To the profit you make from it. "Classic" is now as worthwhile as dumping your♥♥♥♥♥in a toilet...Or on a development team. Think that's the worst part? Oh no. I'm not even FINISHED.
- "WHAT IS WRONG WITH MY ♥♥♥♥ING KEYBOARD!?!"
The controls with any movement design other than Tank treads will feel so obliterated you will literally ask... Yeah that's right, the subtitle of this paragraph. As of the R&O Update, Wheels are incredibly sluggish, Rockets provide minimal momentum, hoverblades are highly unstable if you lose even ONE, Aerofoils are a disaster to use, Walker legs are bloody hell to even keep still on a ceiling or a steep hill if you want to stay in place, and believe me, it's going to walk down to the surface on you while you shoot. And LASTLY, the rotor blade design is sluggish as well.

Played for like a year now, and the game has come on a long way, the devs are incredibly active.
First of all, this game runs absolutely fantastic. I literally have the worst possible computer, with intel HD3000 graphics, and it still looks good. Not much in the way of settings for specific effects etc, but there's fastest fast good great beautiful so I guess that's okay. Since they baked in shadows to the maps it looks even better.
Building a robot is FUN. The interface is intuitive, you float around in your garage and place blocks. Menu's are easy to use (though the tech tree is a little cluttered). There are a lot of types of robot to choose from. In movement there's wheels, tracks, wings, helicopters, hoverblades, walker legs and blimps (or nonsensical combinations of these). They all require a certain amount of skill to use, and good players really have an advantage over people who are trying a new type of robot out, which is cool in my opinion. You have to learn your class.
Weapons are all fairly balanced. People will argue that any weapon is OP, but it just depends who is using it. Medics can kill SMGs if they are good, and so on. Rails seem a bit buggy, and they don't seem to shoot as far as you can see, maybe they need some work.
Teamwork is important, a plasma helping a rail out can destroy every flyer that comes near your base, a medic and smg combo can be unbreakable if they play well. (lest we talk of 2 medics).
The gamemodes are good. About a month ago they introduced the 'new meta', with overclocking robots, towers, bases, and everyone screaming "OH NO IT'S AN MMO NOW HELP WTF FREEJAM". The new gamemode is fun. It's fairly complex but easy to learn, still based on how good a pilot you are and still dependant on teamwork. You cap fight over towers to gain advantages over the other team, until eventually one team is powerful enough to take the fusion reactor. I think it is absolutely necessary that new maps are made, because I don't think the current ones are all really suitable for the new gamemode, where they just adapted them a little for it. But it's in development so whatever.
Progression is interesting. It's a sort of tug or war between how much money you have, what weapons you have unlocked, and your CPU (rank effectively) which allows you to build bigger robots. It's certainly fun to go through, but it takes a long time (though some people just blast though the ranks somehow). I know a lot of people won't be into drawn out progression, so if you aren't maybe this isn't for you. But even still, all the time you are matched with robots at the same level as you, so it is never really unfair.
The game isn't pay to win. You can pay to get to higher tiers faster, but you will never have an advantage over another player because you payed freejam money (you can certainly look prettier though!).
This game is a lot of fun. Platooning with friends is great, you can always build a robot for a lower tier (you have multiple garages), so won't have to worry about being too high a level like when you grab someone to play borderlands with you.
I hope they introduce a voice client other than curse voice (though it looks like it's here to stay) since there's no mac or linux support and clients like teamspeak 3 and mumble are already established and great.
Otherwise, absolutely would recommend.

This game is fun and mildly addicting at first. It revolves around a pretty interesting concept of creating your own vehicle to battle with. It even locked simple features of the game like being able to play with more than 2 of your other friends at once behind a paywall. I know the developers have to make money somehow. Plus, the gameplay was kinda clunky and it became stale very quickly. I didn’t hate Robocraft. I thought it was just kind of average. But, Steam only allows for a thumbs up or a thumbs down. It took me awhile to decide whether I should recommend it or not. After much consideration, I came to the conclusion that it bared more negative aspects than positive. So, I decided to leave a negative review. Overall, Robocraft is a very limited and repetitive experience especially if you refuse to pay. It might keep you entertained for a few hours. Thats all.

While the game's single player game may be short (around 8-10 hours), there is a lot more to Portal 2 than its length. The amount of thought that went into GlaDOS and Wheatley is impressive. Being the only two main characters with main speaking parts, their place in the story is delightfully entertaining at every turn. The level design and texture-mapping, for a four year old game, are just as impressive as the character development. I was surprised to see how much work went into the test chambers, and found myself genuinely annoyed by the difficulties I faced trying to solve each one. For a puzzle/adventure game, I would suggest Portal 2 before any other I've played. Even though I just finished, I want to go back and play through again.

The premise of the game is fantastic. Who wouldn't like the idea of building your own robot and fighting it against other people's creation? The core idea of the game is great, and having played it well before it came to Steam; the game has come a long way.
However, there are still two issues I see (having taken a hiatus from playing) that still linger in the game. Armor blocks still don't have enough health. Shields help, but it isn't enough.
This is the big one for me: Ditching the game early. You'll find alot of games aren't going too go well. With no penalty (not getting a reward is not a penalty) to ditching the game, why not? The one issue that infuriates me to nigh apocalypse is people ditching games.
There needs to be a lock-out timer on that robot like there was pre-Steam for ditching early. I think locking it out for three times the amount of time that was missed would work because as right now, the lack of a real ditch penalty is what makes for frustrating times in the game.
These two issues aside, the game is fantastic and being free is simply icing on the cake.

This game is a ton of fun simply because you can build and design your own vehicles, and then ride/fly them into combat. It's an intuitive construction system with a moderate learning curve and tons of upgrades to unlock and use. A few different weapon types and lots of mobility options make for many vehicle variations.
But there are not infinite designs due to the limited weapon types. You'll run into a lot of the same vehicles in the game that other people have made:
The Cube: as many square blocks as can be put on a vehicle at once, with SMG weapons and whatever movement type.
The Discoball: a small circular hovercraft bubble of shields with healing weapons,
The Sniper: Walker mobility with railguns, for hiding on top of hills,
The Bomber: Winged vehicle with as many thrusters and plasma bombs stuck on it as possible.
The game mechanics don't encourage much creativity, but it is certainly allowed. I did build a Millenium Falcon, which flew just like the Falcon, but it was ineffective in combat. Scrapped it. Also built an attack chopper, with good control mechanics and lots of firepower and speed, it can swoop on snipers, counter bombers, and chase retreating enemies down. It also captures decently. But the chopper blades are so fragile that they disappear with one hit. Which brings me to the issue of balance.
The game is balanced, but not really well. Expect to get rocked by OP build combinations. These are easily recognized by their lack of design originality. Floating cubes with guns. Also expect lots of droppers, AFKers, non-team players, and just people who don't know what to do. On top of that, expect unbalanced teams and uneven teams. The team with a healer will win vs a team without healers, unless of course the healer is an idiot.
Reccomended only for people who really love to build... stuff.
Money well spent. Grab it while it's still on sale.

Robocraft, for me, is a bit of a difficult game to talk about. It has lots of good points, and lots of bad points, too, some of them not even being because of the game itself.
+Creative aspect: The game encourages you to think about how you're going to strategically build your robot for it to fulfill its desired purpose. If you want to make a flying robot, you need to think about the weight distribution (and the weight), the position from which you will be shot at and the position from which you will shoot. This makes badly-built robots pretty useless and easy to kill once you find their weak point.
+Variety: There are lots of weapons and movement blocks (e.g. tracks, hoverblades, plasma cannons, healing lasers) to choose from that each give you a different advantage in the game, as well as some structure blocks to reinforce your robot with. The addition of curved blocks looks really nice and helps to make builds look smooth and aerodynamic.
+Map design: The maps don't have much scenery and aren't very special, but they have varied paths that you can take and places that you can shoot from.
+Definitely not P2W: If anyone says that this game is Pay-to-Win, they clearly need to play it more. The only things that are worth spending money on in this game are the cosmetic blocks like trails and flags, some of which I have bought because they look nice. The pre-built robots, which I rarely see in players' possession, take away the whole point of building your own, and the tech point conversion system using the premium currency is absolutely pointless.
Now to the bad points.
-Grinding: It was to be expected. There is a lot of grinding in this game, meaning that you will often spend hours and hours getting into the next tier. Although this means that you need determination and patience to progress, such progress within a single tier isn't exactly fun (because of the point below).
-Teamwork: The maps don't encourage teamwork; the chat UI is messy and difficult to use; and the level of difficulty in the game means that healer robots will charge on their own when they're supposed to help their own team (which happens almost all the time). There is absolutely no teamwork in this game, and most of the time you will be ignored if you send a message to the team. It gets slightly better towards the later tiers, as everyone is more careful with their actions, but it still always feels like a silent game that you can only win in if your robot is indestructible.
-Graphics: This isn't necessarily a big part of the game, but I think that the blocks look unclean, jaggy and way too glossy. The colours in the early tiers are so ugly that I feel like I could puke staring at them, and they shine so much that your robot might as well be a teacup rather than a raging hunk of metal.
-The community: For the most part, the players of Robocraft are normal. However, especially in the global chat, they will often talk about things unrelated to the game, using BBcode to spam and just post referral links and the sort. This also links to the teamwork, in the way that there is none because Robocraft's player mostly feel like clueless, unstrategic 9-year-olds. Also, most players won't aim for other robots' weak points or try to decapitate them strategically, and won't aim for the parts where the tower bases are connected to the blocks in the Battle Arena mode to capture them more rapidly. This makes the team extremely inefficient and you will most likely only win the game if you're extraordinarily good at single-handedly killing the entire enemy team.
Conclusion: If you don't mind throwing away your love for tactical thinking and teamwork for mindless target shooting and the occasional intense moment, then I recommend this game. However, beware that there will be times that you get fed-up of it because it gets annoying and boring because of some of its players (also note that I am only in T6 right now, so I'm not sure if it gets much better on the highest few tiers).

Fantastic and creative game, but there is a few things that i think need improving, like:
Personally I love the way that you can make your own robot and you dont need to just stick to one design until u move up to the next tier. But i do wish that it would be possible to start off with a tier robot that you are on, for example a tier 7 standard robot to get you started. Then once you have enough cash you can then start to make it your own robot. The only reason why i say this is because the amount of times i come across someone with a robot that is basically a tier 1 armored box is a lot, it just makes killing them boring now, it would be nice to have a challenge.
I would like the tiers to be a little longer as well, I do find that i can go from tiers 5 to tier 6 in about 10 or so games, maybe even less. Dont get me wrong there is nothing wrong with this, but i do like games that give me a goal, and my goal was to get to tier 10 and now TX but it feels like if I throw some premium at this game i could do it in about a day or two.
Maybe a new tech tree. What i mean by this is, now that we have TX-1 why not do TX tiers up to 10 again. Yeah i know that would take you for ever to do, but for example in World of Tanks or War Thunder, it takes a long time to get everything in that game, sometimes even years, and to think that you can pretty much get to TX-1 in about a few weeks maybe shorter, is quite quick for a grinding game.
Servers do need to be fixed for once and for all. i know sometimes this problem is not even there, but if this many people play this game once an update comes out, then the servers really do need to be fixed. Not saying that there bad, but i just think robocraft should invest in it, if they havent already.
Now, before you all have a go at me and say that im being harsh on robocraft, im not. i know its only in alpha, but im just suggesting what they should do. I personally think this game is brilliant if you love the grinding type of game, but you do like to custom build your own robot. I hope that anyone who downloads this game for the first time really does enjoy it as much as i did.

It's an alright game, but the main mechanic was already fully fleshed out in the first portal game, and I felt like the game designers played it too safe with this sequal.  The puzzles themselves were lower quality as well, and felt much more "on-rails" with very little in the way of alternate solutions.
There were also some less structured, non-puzzle rooms are mostly garbage, just giant incoherent spaces, often with one tiny portal spot a half mile away that you portal to.  They felt like shameless padding, just stuck in to lengthen the game and justify a full price tag.
Paint is by far the best addition to the game - it's satisfying to see it fly around and cover the level, it's fun to go fast and bounce high, and most importantly, it adds extra depth too the puzzles.  But, I get the sense that the designers might have been too afraid of players exploiting the paint mechanic, and as result, really railroad the player into the intended solution on those puzzles.
Anyway, there's a lot of great stuff in this game, so I guess in a vacuum, I'd recommend it, but I just don't think they expanded enough on the portal concept.  And, the overwhelming praise of it is way over the top.

The Good
Truly a free to play game.
Very creative game, you can build any fighting vehicle you can think of.
You can pay a small amount to advance quickly and get unlocked tech tree and a cool premade vehicle but it is unnecessary.
You can eventually get all the paid for stuff for free if you just play the game. In 2 days I've unlocked everything up to Lv4, and it goes up to Lv10 on technology tree. Having a premium account would double your earnings so that's cool.
The Bad
Very fun game but at times it can be frustrating because of occasional overpowered weapons in low level lobbys. Game does a cumulative sum of all elements of your ship/vehicle and puts you in an appropiate lobby. However you can have a really crappy ship and a powerful weapon and just wreck people left and right as you kill them before they can even get close to you.
The Ugly
Sometimes the game can't find people of similar level so you get paired with people DOUBLE YOUR OWN LEVEL but with only half the team size on their side. It seems like that would be fair however a player double in level can easily whipe out 2-3 other players without dieing and if they are good they can whipe the entire team out single handedly.
Edit: No vsync works, even when forced from GPU app. Stutter was noticed much less on laptop (weak laptopn in fact) and much more stutter with a powerful gpu (ATI R9 270 2GB GDDR5, AMD FX-octa 8core CPU, 8GB ram, 60" Vizio E series 1080P 60HZ Tv in HDMI)

Recipe for Strawberry Shortcake
Ingredients
Original recipe makes 1 8-inch round cake Change Servings
3 pints fresh strawberries
1/2 cup white sugar
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
4 teaspoons baking powder
2 tablespoons white sugar
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/3 cup shortening
1 egg
2/3 cup milk
2 cups whipped heavy cream
Directions
Slice the strawberries and toss them with 1/2 cup of white sugar. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease and flour one 8 inch round cake pan.
In a medium bowl combine the flour, baking powder, 2 tablespoons white sugar and the salt. With a pastry blender cut in the shortening until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Make a well in the center and add the beaten egg and milk. Stir until just combined.
Spread the batter into the prepared pan. Bake at 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool partially in pan on wire rack.
Slice partially cooled cake in half, making two layers. Place half of the strawberries on one layer and top with the other layer. Top with remaining strawberries and cover with the whipped cream.
Preperation Time: 30 Mins
Cooking: 20 Mins
Total: 50 Mins

This is a personal review from someone who has over 1.5k hours (950 hrs on steam and another 600 hrs on its own launcher)
Robocraft once used to be a special, unique game on its own. It allowed people to unleash their creativity and "engineering skills" to have specialized robots. Sure back then there were many unbalanced things, but in my opinion those things made the game competitive to overcome simple gunbed bots.
The Old Robocraft had a system and structure that kept you in the game as you wanted to go a higher tier; its premium (when you use real money in the game) gave you only special cosmetics so the game was not a pay to win. The old game had classes so each personal had a special role and we had to work together to win. MegaBots were considered the "final stage to grinding" meaning if you had such a megabot you were successful with enough parts and you were a "TX" rank.
The new robocraft, I was open minded at first because it gave us new content and expanded the game in its attempt to reach more players and make it more fun. But the new updates made the game a play to win with new weapons that require no aiming and can be a simple one shot kill. The gameplay is now filled with players stocking a huge "shotgun" weapon on top of a block. The game lost its creative aspect and its uniqueness when they try to copy other game traits.
Excelente.

TL;DR - The old gamemode was great, but is now obsolete in the shadow of the new, grindy, and unfitting MOBA-style gamemode. Although a fantastic idea and a wonderfully made paying system that minimalizes P2W, the idea of a MOBA for this game does not fit the fast and fun gameplay this was meant to be. By making a simple game complex, the grind was massively intensified and somewhat ruined the game for me.
TL;DR of TL;DR - They tried to fit a round peg into a square hole.
It was actually a really nice little game. OK graphics, decent mechanics, and overall a great idea. But recently a new gametype has been added and the original gameplay, essentially team deathmatch, has become outmoded. While the new gametype is a pretty nice concept, its way too MOBA-esque for a game like this. Even the company admits that yes, this is in fact a MOBA oriented update. I just feel that this is a game thats about building robots for quick, easy fun. The added complexity to gameplay takes away from the lightness of this game. I would have recommened this game a month or two ago but now, I feel that the developers are pushing a good concept of robot-building and fighting into MOBA gameplay that is unfit for this style.
I would like to talk about more than just the new gamemode though. The original gamemode, now labeled "Classic", was far more entertaining. This is a tier based game, from tier 1-10, more advanced items are available, blah-blah, basic F2P aspects. The reason why I played so much, as seen by my play-time, was the rounds were quick and profitable. At some points, the grind was pretty bad, but overall the fast rounds and ease of getting into the game made for not too slow leveling. For a single round I could instantly buy a new piece of equipment for a 5 minute match. Now, the matches last anywhere from 15 to 30 minutes, and although slightly more profitable, the time spent is not worth the money. I would have just stuck with the classic if it were not for the "nerfing" of the money gained. All classic matches now give LESS money. On top of that, Few people play it anymore, and one mode, "Challenge" (4 high-tier VS 12 lower-tier) is broken beyond repair.
(There is much more I would love to mention but it would only make sense to those who have played the game.)

Minecraft meets World of Tanks. Robocraft is still in early access, but it's free to play, a small download, and has generous system requirements.
Honestly, it's one of a few F2P games out there that isn't to some extent pay-to-win. Game currency bought with real life money only allows you to go up the tiers faster or buy cosmetic items. And since the game has a way of gauging your bot's strength and matchmaking accordingly, the playing field is nearly always level. You can even look at the buyable crafts and easily replicate them without buying them, if you wanted, in just a manner of minutes.
As for the gameplay, it's rather straight forward. Playing rewards you with in game currency with which you can buy building blocks to build a craft. Tweaking your craft is half the fun, the other is taking it out into the battlefield and blowing other people's machinations to pieces. Creativity as well as quick thinking are rewarding in both these aspects respectively.
I recommend anyone with a Steam account to give it a try.

A while back I would've recommended this game thoroughly. It was an excellent and creative game that allowed you to test your best designs against that of other players to see who is the victor and flecks of robot fly about the map!
Sadly however the new"update" to the game has killed off any love I had for it...
The new main gamemode (classic is still and option but for severly reduced credits) has players shooting at cap points in an attempt to destroy the enemies main hub, Not so bad eh? Well here lies the problem, there is now respawning as opposed to the one and done mechanic previously. This has led to a lot of players taking the paths of least resistance as there is no fear of death, no more is there marvellous creations and ingenious designs to maximise longevity on the battlefield. Now the current 'Best plan' appears to make spazzy flyers covered in electroplates and smgs, if you die so what? you can just respawn and annoy people all over again.
This respawn feature also removes any hope of a quick game of robocraft as games now last up to half an hours on average (kinda like a MOBA huh?)
Also like a MOBA is the idea of 'Overclocks', these are basically levels that a players gains for killing, capping ect and this is probably the main thing that upsets me about the current game. People snowball and they snowball hard, you can quite happily just sit on a hill and snipe your way to victory, so what if people attempt to confront you? Your higher level basically negates their hard thought design and you can just happily tank their low damage attacks until your rail is recharged...
So in summary, the game as is stand is a mere husk of a previously awesome game. And if the developers where to return to such a game I would be all ears, however as it stands I cannot endorse this game. It's trying to be something that nobody wants it to be :(

This game is the biggest piece of rage I've ever played... And I've played freaking Dark Souls. First off, there are quite a few bugs and lag spikes at certain times. A recent bug was that I kept receiving an error message whenever I tried to enter a battle... A couple re-logs did the trick, as it does with most bugs. Started playing this game ages ago and it was pretty good, original and a very creative game. Now there is a new game mode!!! ooh! I was pretty happy to see that. I played for a while and I enjoyed it... But there were a few game-breakers that put me off this game, thus making me not recommend it. There are a lot of, shall we say, 'cocky' 10 y/o kids on this game who absolutely ruin your experience.Half of the time in the new battle mode the fate of which teams winners is decided straight from the start! Whoever has the most players, wins! Yes, people actually spend time searching for matches then as soon as they get in them... Instantly leave. How fun... :/  Team balancing isn't exactly a thing in this game. Out of about seven or eight players in one team (can't exactly remember how much) You could have five medics... Or no medics. It seems pretty random. The moderators on this game's chat are a little... Worthless. There was a massive amount of spam at one point and all you could see every now and then was a moderator saying "Don't spam". I don't think they realize... If you tell a troll to do something, he will do the opposite. Also, the tier system is extremely broken. You could have a white block (The worst armor block) tiny car but with one very high tier rail cannon and be in a very low tier. This breaks the game as you get cocky little cowards one shotting all the low levels. Making them leave, and as I said before... Making that team lose the game. Servers are often broken, leaving people in lobbies searching for matches for over ten minutes, as I have done many times.
Improvements? Yes, there should be a blue-print system for the newbies of this game so they have an idea of what to build. Private matches with friends should be introduced. Practice mode should have the robots with weapons who try to kill you again. Battle mode should have a join mid-game feature for those teams with less people. Major bug fixes. Fix servers, they're almost as bad as EA's. Fix the tier system, seeing a TX-1 with a high tier sniper and a couple white blocks one shotting everything is a little bit annoying. Reduce your freaking prices, no one wants to pay $10 for a crappy robot that can get easily killed. Replace some moderators as they don't do anything. Reduce damage on plasma cannons? Bombers can pretty much one shot anything with little accuracy. Filter some offensive words? Seeing robots named as profanity is a little eye-rolling. Rotor-blades need improving.Private Multi-player practice and battle and classic mode please?
TLDR?
-Team balancing = bad
-Online community = bad
-Any bugs? = lots
-Are the matches good? = nope, one person leaves and that's it... You've lost.
-Are there in-game purchases? = Do you want to go into debt? =)
-Do you want this game? = If you want to lose your mind then you should get it!

This game has a great base concept.  It is relatively simple to play and fun.
However, this game is very unbalanced which often kills the fun.  Aircraft can be flying tanks and do as much damage as land based units.  It is very tiring to leave base and within 10 seconds get 1 shot by a plasma bomber, or 1 shot by a sniper on top of a ridge just outside of his base.  I have tried all of the weapons and found that smg’s are my favorite weapon type / class, but, they are painful to play.
The plasma launchers in general are over powered.  Every 3 seconds they can fire a 1 shot salvo at someone.  While it may be challenging to aim because it is not a direct fire weapon system, with some practice, you can be very accurate.  If you put the plasma launchers on an aircraft, you can fly around bombing other people, haul♥♥♥♥♥back to base and heal up.  Plasma bombers can simultaneously be the fastest, hardest hitting, least effected by terrain and be tanky.  All you have to do to realize how over powered they are is look at how many of them there are.  The easiest and first fix that should be tried here is to decrease reload speed.  I would start by trying the reload time to 6 seconds and then re-evaluate after a week or 2.
Rail guns are really strong.  The only down sound to them is the lengthy reload time.  To counter this issue, most snipers will sit near their base, snipping ¾ of the map.  Upon detection, damage or reload they will just hide inside their shield with impunity.  I believe the easiest fix to this is to decrease the vision range of them or to decrease the number of guns they can carry.
Flying devices need to be able to lift far less than they can presently.  All flyers can be tanky, be the fastest, least effected by terrain and do the same damage as land based units.
A friend of mine purchased a real money transaction vehicle.  In order for him to use this vehicle, the game increased his cpu (cpu determines of much stuff you can put on your vehicles.).  I am now 10 levels above him and he has 270 cpu (1204 approx. to his 1476 approx) more than me.  This means that even though I am higher level, he can have bigger and better equipped vehicles.
The leveling process can be a little brutal at times.  You can be in a tier 5 match and be up against someone who has weapons 3 tiers above you.  The 1 block/1 gun wonder is really frustrating to play against. You should be limited to using pieces that are only 1 tier above the tier of your vehicle.
I am eager to see how much the dev’s do to balance this game in the near future.  In general though the dev’s need to re-evaluate risk vs reward, positive vs negative of all of the vehicle/weapon choices.
As a free game I suggest giving it a try for yourself.  I would advise against spending real money on this game at this time.

This game is highly addicting and has a variety that will make you frustrated and giddy all at the same time.  The Free to Win concept is key in this game as this game does allow everyone to get access to all the good tier items and expand their weaponry to plasma launchers, rail snipers, nano healers, and even tesla blades.   However, with that being said, here's where I think the game devs are starting to tear the game apart.  My short list of all my complaints are below:
1. Leaving a Battle offers no real penalties
2. Balance is often favored between Sniper and Plasma
3. Some movement options are unbalanced when compared to others (Hover, Helo, Tank, etc.)
4. Constantly improving on what isn't broken (Tier system, CPU Limits, Robot Ranking)
5. New unbalanced game modes (Battle Towers going from 4 to 3, the pit being all SMG and Plasma)
6. No way to detect or defend against hackers (Players falling through floor, invincibility cheats, higher damage output than normal, punting other players)
Do I still recommend the game?  Tentatively, yes.  There are issues with the game, but I think they will be solved in due time.  The developers are still considering this an Alpha game because they are trying to fix a lot of the bugs with poor balancing, tier systems, hackers, etc., before making it into a final state where the game will merely need some balance reworks here and there.  The devs are trying, but they need to keep on showing the community more progress and consider more options, such as the Community Market, for ways in which the game can be made better and more beneficial to other players.  I have a feeling this game will be great when it fianlly leaves alpha, if it even does that.  But, even if it doesn't, it doesn't change the fact that playing with a group of your friends through Steam's chatting service isn't fun.  It still is.  The question is are you smart enough to come up with a better tank?

Hands down one of the best games I have ever played. The puzzles are mentally stimulating and challenging, and the humor is fresh and hilarious. The sci-fi undertones held in the game make for an intriguing, and sometimes even creepy backstory while keeping a lighthearted tone with the humor. The game expands on the first Portal's story and series of puzzles. The coop is excellent as well and will keep you and a friend entertained for at least four hours (the main game is much longer). The new "Perpetual Testing Initiative" (ability to create and share your own puzzles) is excellent and adds a whole new level of entertainment to the game. Unlike the first Portal, this is a full length game and lasts as long as a standard AAA game.
Pros:
+ Excellent puzzles
+ Smooth gameplay
+ Great sense of humor
+ Mysterious and intriguing plot
+ Fun and quirky characters
Cons:
None
(Note: I only have 6.2 hours because I originally played the game on Xbox 360. I bought it on Steam so that I could use the Perpetual Testing Initiative.)

This game is utterly gronked. Its fun, but god does FreeJam sure seem to not encourage it.

Tiers and progression have been ruined. Bots that would have been fairly "mid teir" can and often will now absolutely stomp bots that would have previously been higher tier. There is no sense of achievement from leveling up really. This isn't inherently bad, but it feels like larger bots are practically useless at this point. You either go full blockspam, or you try and get the highest damage boost you can without being a complete twig. Part of the issue with this new "blockspam" tactic is that tri-forcing is no longer viable. Gone are the days of skillfull building. Shields are also pretty useless. relegated to use only in key areas. Also, can we have more tiered blocks that are well balanced? It would add to the complexity of balancing structural strength versus offensive power, which would be a good thing.

Multiple movement types are straight up useless. Mechs have been what tanks should have been for a long time for some reason, hovers feel like trash to use, helicopters are mushy and hardly any more maneuverable than planes, and insect legs are completely broken.

The new "reward" system is trash too.  You can completely carry your team but lose, and only get a gold. Rewards should be based on how well you did in comparison to your team imo. No matter how good you are, if you have a few complete idiots on your team who do nothing but feed the enemy, you'll lose. Base rewards on how well you did in comparison to your team, and then add bonuses for winning.

People leaving are also a major issue. I've had a lot of connection issues with robocraft. It's not my internet either as it persisted when I changed networks. But, user issue or not, people leaving needs to be addressed. The dumb "boost" that the team gets doesn't mean jack against a properly functional oppositional team. It helps with 1v1 fights sure, but past that you're going to lose. The game should automatically end and just "tie" when somebody leaves witching the first minute or two. Past that, there are a few solutions. One that I'd be okay with is if the enemy team leaves, then one person on the other team gets the option to "sit out" in exchange for a gold/diamond crate or something. Not hard to come up with solutions. If FJ fixed the dumb disconnection issues then more harsh punishments could be introduced too. People leaving is my biggest issue with this game. I can go down entire tiers of MMR rating simply because over 50% of the time, some dumb idiot leaves at the start of the game.

Weapon balance isn't
bad right now, but I don't see SMGs a lot. I find protos kinda took their place as an option for sustained fire. If SMGs had a bit more accuracy they'd probably do well, especially as an air to air weapon. Plasma is a bit OP when in the air, but I think the completely broken state of insect legs is contributing to that. It's much harder to have a functional anti-air role when you can't get to high ground without falling over fifty ♥♥♥♥ing thousand times. If insects were fixed we'd have more rails and flaks combating air bots, meaning plasma bombers would be a more risky bot type.

It is free to play. That statement is not all true. In Robocraft, the player gets to build (a) robot(s) and then battle other players' robots with your robot. The parts used to create a robot, after the first game cost RP. (an in game currency) This rewarded to the player for playing in games. The more kills you get, you get more RP you get for that game. If you cap the points, you get more RP for that game. However, if you die without any kills, you get hardly any RP. Thus cannot build a better robot for future games.
