As a sequel to one of the most innovative games of all time, this game doesn't fail to impress. The physics engine and graphics make the experience so beautiful and with a story that will get you both laughing, crying and rethinking your life really enhances the experience. As an all round Portal fan, this game was great. Not brilliant, but great none the less. The scripting was amazing as always and the voice acting and animation was even better and with a longer length story + a coop campaign, there is a lot more to explore and keep you playing until the next Half-Life comes out. The thing I found with Portal 2 is that it worked if you had played through the first game (allowing you to grab a hold of the overall story) but it also worked for those whom hadn't played the first one, even giving some nostalgia/viewings of content that belonged in the first game to begin with. However, apart from shouting at a friend to place a portal on the right surface, the game has very little replay value. The challenge mode might have you replaying levels to beat your friends by 1 second but it gets boring after quite a while. It's the same with the co-op, you'll just find yourself speeding ahead with the other player lagging behind after not knowing where to put the disc. Of course, there are some really well (and some really not well) made community test chambers that adds another story to try. Another thing I found is that the main single player campaign is just a little too easy and you shouldn't need to spend any longer than 10 minutes on each test before moving onto the next. Although it does get slightly harder near to the end but the puzzles don't exactly challenge your brain too much. Oh, and one last con - the cake really is a lie this time. The reference came and then swiftly disappeared along with the party escort bot. However, Hoopy is still a part of the story, assuming you knew where to look and what it's significance was.

Where to start?
Robotcraft is overall a fun game to play, based on the tried and true voxel(cubes essentially) design this game has various construction and strategy elements that leads to a satisfying experience. Players can build almost everything imaginable, from tanks, aircraft , hover vehicles and more. If you ever played Spore and browsed thru the creations that is basically how Robotcraft is  when it comes to random designs. A little confusing at first for players unfamiliar to this type of game , the game nevertheless encourages constant re-designing , especially as you move thru the tiers.
Now for the Negatives,
The game can still be a little buggy in some places( ie game will crash as soon as you finish a fight ) but overall the game does well to handle the crazy creations some players create and manage to make it work. Unfortunately the game suffers from an odd problem. You'll find on average that players D/C in literally every game. Almost always one, and very often 2-3 sometimes all from the same team. This ruins it for everyone and completely unbalances the game. The game tries to help my shortening respawn rates but its not much in the long run. The game fails to punish players to force them not to D/C. In my opinion adopting a strategy used in a  similar game that has a heavy emphasis on teams to win would be League of Legends. The "Tribunal System" allows players to be accountable for leaving their teammates to fend for themselves. Alas, the game is still in development so i hope to see someway to fix this in the near future, overall i would recommend this game to anyone.

Pros:
-Customization is limited only by your imagination (and petaFLOPS!).  Some really funny looking robots, too.
-Various weapons systems, including (SMGs, Cannons, Railguns, Healing Turrets, and Tesla Blades)
-Plenty of replaying, i.e. progressing through tiers, playing as a wheeled/tank/jet/helicopter/hover/blimp/unmovable box robot, with any of the above listed weapon systems
-FreeJam is ALWAYS pushing more content to the game.
-It's not P2W, but definitely P2Progress faster.  Not necessary to spend a dime.
-It's very addictive sometimes.  surviving a match with only 1 block remaining (+ your command seat), healing someone back to full from aforementioned brink of death, one-shotting a massive tank because you hit that sweetspot with your railgun and killed his pilot, limping back to a healer with a severely damaged robot, it never really stops
-the teamplay is sometimes really good.  sometimes you'll get an awesome team who all works together (sometimes you wont)
-Several game modes, from a Moba-style with respawns, to a single-life deathmatch, to boss battles (several high tiers vs a bunch of low tiers).
Cons:
-definitely grind heavy.  You'll need to be prepared to sink a lot of hours into this to achieve T10.  Even if you pay for premium membership (bonus xp/rp)
-sometimes it can take forever to find a match.  especially if you're trying to play off-peak times
-sniping can be bothersome occasionally as you'll see a target outline way off in the distance but your railgun doesnt actually reach it, because your guns only have certain range before the projectile disappears.
Overall, this is a really fun game to play.  It's free and doesnt require a single penny.  I downloaded it a while ago just to try it and I keep coming back to play it after every update and I will probably continue to play this for a while.  You really have nothing to lose by trying it. Who knows, maybe you'll love it.

(Cons firsts)
I really enjoy Robocraft "when I can get on and play". That being said, lately the game has had some issues with logging in and before with anti-cheat verification. It's been a lot of misses and a few hits to get on and play. When I do get on, I better be playing for my day or weeks worth cause it may not let me log in again that day or days to come. I have done the verification of files and such and other checks with re-installs. The problem still persists, which makes this my biggest issue for this game. (If I could force choke the code to work I would.)
Other then that, I want to see items where they have centered shielding, where I can mount a deflector dead center and have it look symmetrical, not looped sided, shift shields one way to work or leave a gap dead center for enemy fire to enter. Also more on symmetrical issues, I find it out that after every few patches, even at times constant, that when I build both sides of my robot craft the same, I can't mount the left side shields when the ride side mounts perfectly fine (same issue if its inverted). The above pretty much sums up my discontent with the game so far. On to a more positive aspect.
(Pros)
I love the building aspect of the game and to simplify it, Lego combat. I enjoy building each robot, I can easily spend an hour building a new robo for battle. The maps and addition of battle modes keep the game interesting. I like how the game has evolved since joining and will continue to enjoy it 'when I can get on'. I also find it fair play by the way of pain play, I don't feel the need to blow cash in order to get ahead or just get the annoyance out of my way. I like the accomplishment of pure will power to destroy my enemies in a blaze of plasma fire or laser blasts. I do like the team link where you can make a team for matches, the double daily bonus is a good incentive just to get on and play for 30 mins to just rack up quick points. What else.... the aesthetics, I very much like the way the game looks. Not over childish and not over kill to seduce the more destructive demographic with in the community. In essence when you make your robotic craft, it's like a piece of art. A colorful moving piece that has the ability to destroy other art that it deems unworthy.
That will wrap it up for my review on Robocraft. I do intend to keep playing, when I can. Have a wonderful build!

I love this game!  I generally don't like competitive first person shooters.  I don't have the best reflexes; I'm not the guy that's going to spin around and shoot you between the eyes before you have a chance to shoot back.
But with this game I can make up for some of that by spending time building better robots and playing smarter.  Once I got a bot that I liked and started winning this game became incredibly fun!
There is a decent variety of weapons, movement (wheels, tracks. hover, flying etc.), and armor.  It's fun to try them and see what suits your style of game play.
There are (and probably always will be) some odd mechanics and balance issues.  There's always an a__hole who puts a gun two tiers up on a tiny robot.  I've wanted to throw my computer out the window a few times after dying from one shot of plasma.  But by building better bots and playing better you can overcome those things.
I've spent $20 on galaxy cash (GC) and I was glad to give them my money.  With GC you can buy premium (more tech points and robot points earned in game), extra garages (for when you want to build a new robot and keep the old), and to buy blocks and unlock tech.  I recommend that you just use GC for premium and garages, and then earn your tech and blocks through game play.
I enthusiastically recommend this game.

The concept is simple:
Get a crazy idea, build it, and watch the magic!
I think what most people are worried about is whether it's pay to win or not, so I'll explain why it's not.
Every tiny bit you can put on your vehicle has a "robot ranking" which is ultimately added all together and your vehicle is given a tier number. Tiers are 1 - 10 and finally the "TX-1" Which is for insanely large robots.
As people buy premium or credits to unlock stuff faster they are only speeding up the unlocking process and getting some cosmetics for their robots. They get no advantage over you in battles. They got the same robot ranking calculations as you do.
Game modes:
Practise
Classic (2 teams win by killing entire enemy team or capture their base)
Battlemode (MOBA Destroy the enemy crystal (there's power crystals that grants bonuses)
Challenger (A handful of higher tiers go up against a full team of lower tiers (Too overpowered in my opinion though))
Megaboss battle (A TX-1 tier robot against 15 tier 6 robots (It's reviewed to be overpowered but I haven't tried it myself.))
There's more in the making.
Social features:
Friend list
Friend list score board from tier 2 and up
Platoons (Premade team)
Global/platoon chats from lobby
Team/All chat in battles
And more (but I don't use more and don't know it too well)

Robocraft can be a very frustrating experience of a game. The concept is great and the gameplay is fun, but there are problems with it and the community... oh the community.
The good:
Creating robots is fun. You have free reign over how it's built and you have an interesting assortment of parts. Four different weapon types and several movement parts.
Weapons:
SMGs are your basic weapon, fire lasers in a straight-ish line; It's the main fighting weapon. However NEVER buy front mounted SMGs. They are useless. Why? Because shields get mounted in the same spots. If you have an SMG on the front, not only do you not have shields, but that gun is going to be the first thing hit and you'll be crippled. They are underpowered and useless.
Rail guns are basic sniper rifles. Load seven on your robot and you have seven shots, load three and you'll have three before you need to reload.
Plasma launchers are arcing explosions. Pain in the♥♥♥♥♥when they are ALWAYS on flying vehicles.
And the Nano thing. It heals and it hurts at a very short range. It's useful and doesn't replace the      SMG.
The Bad:
The community is awful. God awful. And the people running it cannot run the community.
I'm wiling to bet the vast majority of the players are quite young and they are prone to fits.
The main thing is people ragequiting out of their new game mode. The game mode entails four towers dotted across the same maps they have been using since the beginning with hexes inside that you can break. The only advantage to having them is a shield over your main base that heals you if you are inside it and blocks enemy fire from entering. This game mode takes time to win, and the problem is that even if you have a majority of the towers, or even all of them, the only advantage you have is that shield of theirs being gone. It's not as though the towers give you a significant advantage over the enemy. So in the end the victor is decided by how many leavers the enemy has in comparison to your team.
That is not a good gameplay mechanic. As far as I know, there is no penalty or at least no significant penalty, to players leaving the game.
The matchmaking. What ends up happening is that players from a higher tier ( who have unlocked stronger building blocks etc. ) will come back into lower tiers with much more resistant blocks quite easily. I was in tier six for example, and I fought a robot made completely out of tier 8 armour. Needless to say he wiped the floor with about three to four robots before going down himself. The reason this can happen is that armour does not account in any significant way to your robot's tier. It's primarily about your weapons and movement parts.
All in all, it's frustrating and very grindy. It takes forever to earn enough of the in game currency to afford the parts it takes to bump up your tier so that you can unlock the tech tree points for that tier so you can get ready for the next tier and then you have to worry about buying blocks which are very expensive....  It's a race that you won't win and you'll constantly be playing catch up to people who have put more hours in than you.

TL;DR:
Painstakingly build a robot, a child of metal and love, forged to destroy your foes. Load into a match to drive across the battle scared landscape of the red earth, cursed by the misfortune to hold valuable resources. You push into enemy territory, backed by your team. You punish their retaliation with a volley of plasma, instantly destroying the weak and crippling the strong. Then a screen shows up. "Would you like to return to the mothership?" You've just been destroyed by a flying pink♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ welcome to Robocraft, enjoy your stay.
Pre-face:
You are given a set of blocks, guns, wheels, and a seat. From this toolkit you will build a multitude of amazing art bots or maybe some crazy death machine. Most likely however you will start with the battle brick/puck/bus or some other simple shape. Slowly you will build up a more and more personalized robot as you grow through the tiers. Eventually you'll end up where I am, making slowly realizing that my most effective shape is that of a phallic origin.
Pros:
(+++) Extensive customization
(+++) FREE
(+++) Constant updates
(++) Clean UI and visuals
(++) F2P model I can agree with (more on that bellow)
(+) Quick matches in the classic mode of a few minutes, or long matches in the new MOBA mode
(?)Dickbots
Cons:
(---) You might have a gripe with their F2P model (Once again addressed later)
(---) RECENT PROBLEM MOST LIKELY TO BE FIXED, but the que times have gone through the roof! (12+ mins for classic)
(--) Color of blocks determines it's stats. So no cool coloring in certain tiers (T6 bots get pink armor, it's fab)
(--)  No way to "save" designs or auto mirror
(--)  All team matches, thus you can get sweeped by a moderately well built tank with a healer
(--) Compounded by the previous point, but only 3 man squads (4 with subsciption)
(--) THE DEEP FOGS OF MARS (Visibility on maps has this strange fog after a certain distance)
(-) It's gotten better lately, but plasma bombers make me salty and they will do it to you too
F2p Conflict:
Now before I shake the bees nest here I'll tell you what they do. So they have a point system GC akin to Riot Points, Gems, Platnum, Premium currency X. Normally it's sold in okay amounts if you want to buy certain items, like some cosmetic or some extra blocks. But if you want to "subscribe" it's in a awkward amount that it will never come out to some nice number and will instead leave just enough left over to annoy you. Additionally blocks you've unlocked through the tech tree in the game by playing can be bought for GC at a fair rate. Now on the matter of P2W, while you can buy blocks that would indeed have game value and are not cosmetic they are fair. The guy who drops $60 on premium and some bots and blocks will have a lot of options, but two things.
1. No blocks or guns he can ever buy will be out of your reach mechanically, each block or gun is identical in stats to something that exists in game already or is that item. As such, they are buying to skip leveling in a way.
2. The pre-made bots are debatably inferior to bots made by hand. Don't get me wrong, they are very pretty and in terms of design obviously are a caliber above anything I can crap out, but if my "Ribbed for Pleasure" bot went against a pre-made bot from the store it would die very quickly.
With those two points their cash store model is more then satisfactory and they often give away premium time to the player base with promocodes and events. All in all I like how they compose themselves, but understand frustration with money -> points systems that cause you to spend more then you want to for a product.
Conclusion:
While you might have qualms with it's F2P model, they practice it well enough to earn my respect. The robot balance is good enough that so long as you pay attention to where you are getting hit and how you position yourself, you can never make a bad bot. This is a well executed exercise in robot MMOs and at the price of free you can't lose.

This is by far the single best two-player co-op split-screen game I have ever played.  It is so much fun to shoot portals beneath your teammate's feet and watch him fall through the floor and reappear at the ceiling.  When a game makes you laugh so hard while spending hours messing around--not even doing any missions or completing any objectives--you know you've found something good.  Not to mention the missions, single-player game, and everything else is awesome as well.
Co-op mode consists of rooms filled with challenging puzzles that need to be solved using portals.  You and your team-mate are equipped with a gun that shoots two different portals.  These portals are pathways to each other.  So, you could shoot a portal on the ceiling, and then shoot the other portal at your feet, and 'viola!', you're falling through the floor, through the ceiling, back to the floor, and... you get the idea.
The single-player missions feature a story in which you play a heroine trying to escape a facility run by an artificial intelligence known as Glados, who is determined to inadvertently kill you.  The protagonist is silent throughout the game, but Glados more than makes up for it with witty dialogue and sarcastic jokes.  The murderous A.I. actually becomes an endearing personality at one point.  Never really expected that.
All in all, this game is awesome.  Buy it.  Play it.  Have sex with it.  You will not regret it.

The game is currently in Early Access. On their website it says this game is in an alpha stage of development. This can be seen throughout everything you see. As can be expected. The weird thing to me is that the monetization system is already in place and functioning.
Overall the game has an interesting concept. You play matches in order to gather currency and experience. As you gain tech points it is possible to unlock new building blocks, weapons, shields and more. This allows you to build a unique and interesting vehicle to pit against others. Since this game is still in Alpha more and more customization is being added over time. A short while back we gained the use of rotary blades allowing the build of helicopters. As can be expected this will cause balancing issues which will be dealt with in later stages of development. For the time being however the balancing is quite severe causing the bad case of "best build". This does NOT mean other builds aren't viable and fun to play with as well. Just might take a bit more practice to become sufficient at them.
The game offers various battle modes. Through Challenge Mode it is possible to have a large group of low tiered vehicles do battle against 3 or 4 huge opponents. Classic is, in part, the original game mode where you basically capture the opponents base and camp on it for a certain amount of time. The new Battle Mode is more complex with capture the flag elements and taking out the opponents base. This allows for more tactics and battles across the map. However it needs significant fine-tuning. At this time it often feels like an endless and tedious tug-of-war untill the 30minute mark. Then all shields drop and everyone is overclocked to the max level of 13. Which means the final part of the battle is reduced to rushing the opponents base.
Destroying opponents towers also lets you respawn all team members instantly adding another layer to tactics. Will you destroy a tower completely or let it sit on a few blocks that can be easily destroyed at a convenient point in time. Lining up the towers to take them down at once to respawn your team while also taking down the opponents reactor shields while their entire team is on cool down is a really good timing strategy. This is also where the problem lies. There is no real communication among team members. Curse chat support doesn't really work. A few people form platoons among themselves using Skype. This means only 2 or 3 people in a team actually work together while the rest runs around like headless chickens.
Overclocking is also a recently added mechanic. You start at lvl0 meaning your vehicle is at normal speed and power. By capturing towers and killing opponents you gain XP. This allows you to gain levels of Overclocking to a max of 13lvls. Each level enhances your vehicle effecting defence, movement speed, rate of fire, damage dealt etc. However after a few battles you notice that around OC8 you feel good and strong. Meaning that having to start at OC0 again being slow and weak becomes a frustrating experience in due time. Early game is reduced to farming towers and occasional opponents to get stronger, before you can actually start to enjoy the match.
The game has some stability issues and glitches occur during matches. Such glitches are towers that can't be captures by a team, or you don't do damage at all for a while etc. These are quite advantagous for the opponents. Matchmaking seems to be working reasonably well. If one team has platoon of friends that communicate with each other, then so does the other team. SMG's, Rails, Plasma, Healers, Airborn or ground force...it all seems to be balanced out most of the time. Only once did I occur a situation where my team had no healers and the other team had two. Other then that it seems to be functioning just fine. Sometimes the game crashes, or has memory issues. But hey it is alpha after all.
The maps are few in number, but well designed. There are open areas in the middle with enough rocks and canyons to move about. Or even lay an ambush or hide hoping opponents pass by so you can rush their base. It is also possible to use mountain ranges to sneak into an enemies base, get behind their reactor and stay decently hidden and out of harms way for a while. It also seems to take into account all forms of movement and builds. Can't wait to see more maps. Just hope the map design won't derail the gameplay and tactics into a typical MOBA game. Instead I hope they'll aim more towards World of Tanks style. Time will tell.
The female voice-over and background music is annoying as hell. Would like to replace this. Might even record my own sound files and override those in the game folder.
Community support is good. There are a fair amount of websites, youtube and twitch channels. They deal with custom builds on requests, tutorials and more. Being able to build and test all ideas you have is a large chunk of the fun this game offers. Of course there are a lot of whiners on the forums, but most often they don't have a clue what they're talking about. So best to ignore them. In game it is mostly polite among players as well. Only a few insecure pubescents shout n00b in a demeaning way. And yes there is always one person in your team that is AFK the entire match. Overall community is better then most.
FreeJam is hiring new people to work for them on a full time base. Seeing the functions they're looking, and the experience of the rest of the team, I'm confident that in a year or two we'll have an awesome game. For now we need to be patient, enjoy the free to play state and don't invest too much money through the monetization system just yet.

There is some merit to this game, but unfortunately combat efficiency stands in the way of any fun.
The meat of the game is building your robot. It uses Minecraft inspired block placement to allow the creation of robots using a selection of chasis blocks (the bits that hold everything together), mobility attachments (wheels, thrusters, legs, wings, etc), and a fairly narrow selection of guns (pew pew).
Now you'd expect that with this you'd be able to make all sorts of entertaining robots, and you could - sort of. Hopefully a recount of my experiences will effectively elaborate on this. First I made a little tricycle styled robot strapped with a gun or two because like the fool I am, I thought this would allow me greater speed and maneuverability than larger vehicles. It didn't. Then I decided it might be fun to make a vehicle that was a wall of guns. Sure - I'd be a bigger target than everyone else, but with all those guns I'd have greater fire power right? Nope. Diminishing returns.
I know! I'll make a wedge on the front of my robot so that I can attempt to flip other robots!... Surely that would work... no? Not viable in your physics engine? WHAT EXACTLY CAN I DO IN THIS GAME THAT ISN'T CREATE A TANK COVERED IN GUNS?
So, if you can't really have any fun crafting robots, then hopefully there some fun to be had in the game modes once you've built your gun tank (product number 3510604)?
Nope. The standard game mode is a team battle, in which you're tasked with pointing your guns at the other guys power energy fusion watsit and holding down the shoot button. In between you and the other teams power station are the other team, which again, you will be pointing your guns in the vague direction of and holding down the fire button.
So would I recommend you play this game? Well, there's fun to be had here exploring the building system and making weird and wonderful robots, but only for the 20-30 minutes it takes you to become frustrated at the fact that none of them have any merit when compared to the mass produced moving blocks of guns.
But hey, it's a free game. Those 20-30 minutes of fun are free. WHAT A DEAL

This game is one of the best Early Access games I've ever played, and here is why:
Your robots are limited by your imagination, and the time and effort you put into the game. There are tons of options for mobility (wheels, legs, treads, fixed and rotor wings, hover blades, helium blocks and thrusters.) and several weapon types to choose from.
The physics engine is pretty good. You have to think carefully about how you build your bot so that it will move the way you want it to, and that the weapons are able to hit targets, and not just splash uselessly against part of your own bot.
The developers are putting a lot of work into constantly updating and improving game play.
This game is NOT pay-to-win! There is are in game purchases and there is a "premium" currency (Galactic Credits, or GC) can be used to upgrade to a "Premium" membership access or to by parts for your bots or to buy fully constructed bots. However, there is a well developed player leveling system and a tier system for bots (Tier 1-10 and TX-1) based on the total combat rating of all the pieces of your bot. So, you won't find someone in Tier 1 mercing noobs with Tier 10 weapons. Also each component adds the load on your bot's CPU (measured in pFlops) which is directly related you your player level. Raise your level by winning matches and getting kills. So it is very balanced.
There is also a good learning curve for new players. At starting levels, the standard mode is pretty straight forward (fight past the enemy team to attack and destroy their protonium reactor core at their base) and as you go up in tier it adds additional mechanics to increase the challenge.
If you loved Legos as a kid (like I did) and were constantly building armies of vehicles to have at each other (like I was) then you will love this game. Download it, try it out, and prepare to have hours of your life vanish before your eye!
With even the tiniest bit of lag, this game becomes unplayable. If you're going to play it make sure you are not lagging for even a moment in game. If you do lag, just quit and play something else.

As someone who has logged hundreds of hours on TF2 and Garry's Mod, I am no stranger to the first person perspective but I am newer to the puzzler aspect of Portal games.  I played through the first installment and absolutely loved it.  It was short, sweet, and reasonably challenging while having a great core mechanic and awesome sense of humor.  Now, Portal 2 has built on it and has added more of the fun from Portal.  The sense of humor is not as sardonic and dark as the first one but still pretty funny.  The game itself is a bit dull at points but the physics engine is beyond amazing and the scenery is really crisp and engaging especially on my HD monitor.  The game doesn't add too much new to the core mechanics which is a good thing because they have no need for a change.  The story drags a bit but overall the few criticisms I have for it are far outweighed by the fact that it is still one of the few games I will play over and over again, once I beat it.  Above all, play the first one before you even touch the second, the story will make much more sense and you will find better humor and tighter gameplay there.  But again, I highly recommend Portal 2, it just has the unfortunate position of being the sequel to what has to be my favorite game of all time so, I still score it 94/100.

Robocraft is a constantly changing game were starmade and world of tanks feel like they had a child.
Pros:
+You get to build your own vehicle, making your immagination important to gameplay
+Game feels unique and unlike others
+Running requirments are low
+Any design choice can have benifits and drawbacks
+Weapons all feel different
+Many ways to move your design are offered
+Maps feel a bit unique
+No pay to win issues
+Frequent updates
Cons:
-Armour block heavy designs tend to die faster than what you would think (outdated)
-SMG's have been nerfed to the point were they dont feel like they can do there old jobs now. (outdated as of 30/06/2016)
-Some of the game modes feel rather unbalanced
-Medics determine the out come of matches a little too heavily (outdated)
-Game balance seams to change faster than you can adapt your design at times
-Premium account needed inorder to make rapid progress
-Requires comitment to feel fun, do to frequent game changes
Summary:
This is a good game, don't get me wrong. Its just that there seams to often be a lack of sustaned game balance. One day, something is added and seams to make designs invulnerable, and the very next day, the opposite is true. There is often no middle ground. All that said, I still like this game. The unique and original feel helps here.
Overal, this game deserves a 8.5/10.
EDIT: I would like to add here an additional final thought. While a lot of community back lash has occured as of late, I still have faith in the developers for the most part. Having been playing since the days when this game had repair costs (pay to win issues where much more prevelent back then), I feel I know what im talking about. I do however, believe that the loot crate system, while nice, does need a few touch ups.

What a pleasant little suprise!
I downloaded this with no expectations. Its simple yet fairly addictive (its popularity despite having only 3 maps prooves this IMO). I view it as legos meats Twisted Metal: build your own robot vehicule using cubes, prisms and tetras, outfit it with wheels, hover jets, wings, skis and your choice of either lasers, rail cannons or plasma guns. Then join a match and blow each other up! Theres a lot of options, but everything is kept simple. The tech tree basicly has 3 branches (weapons, mouvement, chasis), upgrade tiers to join harder hitting matches. The gameplay is VERY simple, you can jump in and play right away, although I do suggest checking a tutorial on youtube first, just so your first vehicle doesnt completely suck ;)
The big one: The microtransaction system is fine. You can only buy cosmetics and/progression. I havent bought anything and I havent felt any abuse from paying customers through 3 tiers. Well see at higher levels.
instead of cons id go with a list of suggestions:
- Matchmaking based ont iers isnt a terrible idea but it doesnt take into account skill, and when you finaly do go up a tier... oh boy, get ready to be insta-killed. A lot. I dont have an exact solution for this but maybe basing the mathmaking on some sort of Performance ratio... All I can tell you is that it took me about 10 matches to get my first victory.
- More maps. I don't doubt theya re working on this but MORE MAPS. (Id even love for them to release reskinned maps.. just for the sake of variety!). Id add destroyable obsatcles/terrain... could be cool
- Different shapes could be nice for aesthtics, but lets be fair: the cubes and tetras function very well.
- Load times are oddly long for logging in right now.
All in all, definetly one of the better free to plays out there.

This is an amazing game. It's a MOBA where the player builds their own characters in any way they want. You can build any vehicle out of voxel-style blocks, throw on some wheels, wings, or other form of mobility, place down some laser blasters, and it's ready to fight. You do, however need to design your robots intelligently. A vehicle's "Health" bar is simply the average damage percentage across all its components. Each block on your robot has its own health value. If a block's health drops below 0, it gets destroyed. It disappears off your robot. Any block that is no longer connected to your pilot's seat is also destroyed. Yes, this means you can target the enemy blasters and render them harmless, you can take out an enemy's wheels to immobilize them, and you can shoot off an airplane's wings to bring it down. Losing key components can destroy any vehicle more efficiently than meaningless hull blocks. An airplane can be taken down with as little as 10% damage if it's off of a wing or jet. Your robot is destroyed when all movement or weapon blocks have been destroyed, which happens when the two blocks under your pilot's seat are destroyed. Then, the robot who got the last shot in gets xp, (But kill assists are practically worthless. Killsteals are very frequent, and, while being a part of internet communities, are very annoying) which increases resistance and damage, and the game goes on until, in standard mode, the enemy reactor (At their spawn) is destroyed, or in other modes, when your team has destroyed every robot on the enemy team.
All in all, amazingly done game, love the block-breaking idea, everything.
My only suggestion is to make components cheaper (Makes the game less grind-y) and to add impact damage, so when your tank crashes in a ravine, it takes damage, or when your airplane falls from the sky, it doesn't just bounce off a mountain. I know this is crazy futuristic designs with alien metals and all that, but realistically, no metal should be able to survive something like that without damage, but take damage from supercharged beams of light. I know it would be hard to add impact damage, but it would, and I say this in all sincerity, complete the game.
That conclusion turned into another paragraph, so I'll end it here. Get robocraft. Build robot. Win. Have fun. Yay. Great job, devs.

You spawn, drive towards the enemy, and find another tank. You both drive in circles shooting at each other for a bit, knocking each other's blocks off. Probably you will get all your turrets and enough engines or wheels shot off that you can't shoot any more, nor even get back to your base to repair. Eventually you die, and then wait progressively longer to respawn (more than a minute after you've died a few times, which makes the game get much slower as it goes on). Many people have said the new gamemode ruined the game as a whole as it encourages no teamwork. But I beg to differ: sure during the early game, everyone is trying to shoot each other with only five second respawns - which is quite understandable - but when you get to the higher OC level, respawns are longer making players think about their actions as much as if they were just in the old gamemode. And the towers serve as a pivot to where you launch attacks from and use them strategically to get in a wave of spawns and vice versa preventing the enemy from spawning in for as long as possibe.
The shields definitely was a different mechanic where it endorses players to take the towers to stop the enemy from retreating and to prevent protonium bombing due to the enemy having a distinct advantage due to heals and short respawn times in the early game.
Now for my opinion. This game is, as what I learned, quite an addicting game giving the player to explore the giant possibilities of creating what ever the heck they want, and eventualy find their niche on what type of vehicle they like the most; I prefer heavy bombers. And that is what makes games fun.
And the balance is very methodical as the tier system dictates what type of things you could have at a given time within the rank. You could have powerful weapons, but sacrafice getting one shotted due to you having to use T1 blocks in a T3 environment. And that gives the player the freedom to go to what tiers they want to play in when reaching a higher rank. Of course you cannont immediately jump in and reach TX-1 due to level caps and grinding.
When you start everything is, technically, available to you needing tech points to unlock. But there isn't a mean of "buying" tech points or cash as the devs have done an amazing job keeping it that way, and the only thing you can buy are pure cosmetics or pre-built bots. So everyone is on the same boat.
And you can still play the old gamemode, by the way.
Edit: After playing in the T1s, I can see why. Have no worry, because you get shields and towers in the later tiers.

Ingredients
12 whole chicken wings
3 ounces unsalted butter
1 small clove garlic, minced
1/4 cup hot sauce
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
Directions:
Place a 6-quart saucepan with a steamer basket and 1-inch of water in the bottom, over high heat, cover and bring to a boil.
Remove the tips of the wings and discard or save for making stock. Using kitchen shears, or a knife, separate the wings at the joint. Place the wings into the steamer basket, cover, reduce the heat to medium and steam for 10 minutes. Remove the wings from the basket and carefully pat dry. Lay the wings out on a cooling rack set in a half sheet pan lined with paper towels and place in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Replace the paper towels with parchment paper. Roast on the middle rack of the oven for 20 minutes. Turn the wings over and cook another 20 minutes or until meat is cooked through and the skin is golden brown.
While the chicken is roasting, melt the butter in a small bowl along with the garlic. Pour this along with hot sauce and salt into a bowl large enough to hold all of the chicken and stir to combine.
Remove the wings from the oven and transfer to the bowl and toss with the sauce. Serve warm.

It's hard to argue with free, but right now I don't feel like Robocraft is really worth the time it's sucking away from me.
There are pros there and I really hope they capitalize on them while fixing what doesn't work but it definitely suffers from early access syndrome. The physics are honestly the worst part for me, everything drives like a hovercraft and the hovercrafts drive like... drunk hovercrafts. The block building system is tedious, but addictive, and whoever made the decision to make your limited supply of blocks count towards your entire garage of robots instead of allowing you to build multiple designs with the blocks you own and play with any one of them provided you have enough blocks for it should be fired on the spot. From a cannon. Currently youneed an excessive amount of blocks to experiment with multiple designs, or a photographic memory and the patience to manually take apart and rebuild everything every single time.
Those two main are what keep me from recommending this game now. Minor nitpicks like weapon balance, and cost of blocks forcing a lot of grinding, and the upgrade stars being completely worthless by the time you've done all that grinding and not doing anything unless you pay real money to make them usefull again... I could sorta kinda live with that in the hope that one day they would fix it.
The core concept of a lego-like construction kit that you then pit against other people in a battale royale is utterly ♥♥♥♥ing awesome. And I hope I can come back to this in a few months and update my review in light of the sweeping improvements the undoubtedly brilliant dev team will surely have acomplished by then.

- Realignment only works 50% of the time

- Long load times

- No penalty for leaving battle mode
- No way to replace all armor cubes of a bot (short of rebuilding the whole thing)
- Reactor shields can be a hinderance for the defending team

Neutral:
- Graphics are mediocre
- Premium is not pay-to-win

Honestly, this game is amazing.
The builder is really simple and intuitive, yet lets you create some truly amazing bots!
The combat is fast and fun, easy to pick up and play yet there's a lot of room for teamwork and strategy.
But the real joy in this game comes when you get a few tiers in, and the variety of robots opens up a bunch - helicopter snipers, flying plasma bombers, sliding tesla-blade wielding melee machines and crawling SMG'ing spidercrabs! Combining multiple movement styles and weapon systems with different custom chassis makes for almost unlimited (practical and working!) designs.The damage model is really cool too, transferring damage through the chassis in interesting ways, forcing you to see what went wrong on your robot, and refine it over multiple matches - strengthening weak points, moving weapon placement or tacking on some extra thrusters for manouvering or speed.
For a free to play game, I've spent a lot of time on it, and it just keeps giving back. I managed to convince a handful of mates to pick it up, and went back through tiers 1-5 to play with them as they levelled up. It is insane, fast-paced fun with a bunch of friends, and you all get to laugh at how crazy all these robots you've built look - especially when 90% of your robot has been blown apart and you're trying to limp around with one wing and a leg! :D
And I've never seen queue times this short - five to ten seconds is usually all it takes to place you in a well-balanced match!
Download this game, it's free, it's small, and it'll take you twenty minutes to get addicted.

The amount of times I've found myself making major and minor tweaks to my robot designs until 2am is truely frightening! For anyone who ever thought minecraft needed giant robots, tanks, and aircraft... this game is for you!
The game allows you to custom buy and build blocks to create your own war machines in a very easy to learn, and hard to master system! You will make designs, you will fail, and you will improve until you get the results you are looking for!
Combat is fantastic. The NEW moba mode pits your teams into an evolving battlefield of towers, shielded bases, and an always respawning wave of player made combat war machines.
I've seen people flying around on simple baloon blocks hovering in the sky with a single plasma gun. I've seen heavy bombers that turn into heavy tanks when you shoot off their wings. I've seen a TON of useless robots, and crushed them beneath my tank treads! Truely, this game is creatively AWESOME!
Pros:
-Fantasticly simple construction system that's easy to start playing
-Making good robots is an art. It takes time to learn and master
-Fantastic diversity of styles&types of robots make gameplay very unique
-Nearly endless replayability
-This could easily be a family game. Grab your friends and kids, this will be a blast!
-This game is free... FREE!
Cons:
-You will wonder where your day went...
-2AM... will become your friend.
-"Classic" Mode (arena matches instead of MOBA) takes forever to find matches... because everyones in MOBA mode.
So go download it! Try it! Give it a few games and see what you think!

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing

With the introduction of a new update and content I decided to give this game a shot again, and I couldn't be happier. While the matchmaking can be shakey at times since any player can have any assortment of weapons on their vehicle, it is still refreshing to see the game back to its roots. I love the refined approach to the skill tree and making the unlocks happen through there instead of through the star system. The building blocks being set as a single type now is something that took some getting used to, but I have learned that bulky is now better than shielded since you regen your blocks after 10 seconds. I could not approve more of them removing the cockpit from building, nothing is worse than being one-shot because somebody got lucky. The biggest thing I enjoy is the servers are once again not 5+min waits, but they did remove the rank breakdown while waiting so it is a bit of give and take. A lot of the gear feels fairly balanced so the fights that include the ranks 4-11 don't feel completely usless. Overall I find that this update improved a lot from the prior and is definitely worth the time now.

Robocraft is a great game!
The building part of your own, unique robot is a copy paste of Minecraft's building system so the learning curve isn't too steep if you're familiar with that game (click to put a block down, right click to take it away).
The menus seem a little overwhelming at first but once you figure out how the tech screen works, the rest comes easily.
As for the actual gameplay : 1 team VS another, classic shooter with some twists here and there (walker robots are fragile but can climb anywhere which leads to agonizing surprise attacks if you're the victim). Maps are a bit bland but hey we're still in the pre-release!
My favourite part is this though : it is INCREDIBLY satisfying to blow other people's robots up and see all their blocks fly in diferent directions. Try it out in practice mode and see for yourself just what a rush you get from utterly destroying a bot!
Yes it's F2P but DEFINITELY not pay to win : there are microtransactions for cosmetic parts and you can pay to unlock experience points but those just throw you in a higher tier, with higher level players. Everybody still has the same gear!
Don't hesitate to throw some bucks the developers' way. A tenner can get you up and running pretty quickly and you'll have hours of gameplay to look forward too :)

With the newest updates the game has been considerably, but not completely.
Things have been rebalanced since my last review, the plasma cannon is no longer the end-all be-all of weapons as it's damage has been reduced and it's been pulled from tiers 1 and 2 giving the game a much smoother transition than before, letting you learn at your own pace without being smothered by Plasma Tanks early. They made BP much easier to get making the game no longer pay-to-win atleast by my standards, and gaining Tech Points is MUCH less of a slog making Uber-Points less mandatory at any tier.
BUT one of the major problems still has yet to be fully addressed in the almost 2 year time span since my last review, weapon restrictions. I've tested and it's still entirely possible to put a pair of T3 Plasma Cannons on a Tier 1 Car, enter Tier 1 Matches, and wreck face with 1 shot kills. Thankfully with the increased ease of getting BP and Tech Points there is almost NO neccessity for anyone to do so without the express intentions of bullying low level players.
It's still entirely possible to ruin your account by selling parts too often, and accidentally locking yourself out of your unlocked tier. Selling being a feature which has NO reason to exist at the moment due to the ease of earning BP.
A pair of NEW problems are Fusion Shield abuse, and the now OP Rail Guns. Fusion Shields allow fire one way, OUT. which can create situations where 2-3 players can shack up in the shield with Railguns, carefully 1 shot killing players of the same tier with the rest of their team rushing inside the other team's shield en-mass leaving the invaded team helpless. Again, this is rendered a non-problem both before and after T3 as before T3 the Shield is omited entirely, and T4 introduces Fusion Towers which serve as a method of turning off the shield without having to go near it and did I mention the railgun is a 1 shot kill if it hits the cockpit's general area on your machine?
Ultimately, the combat is more fun and with respawning allowing for more exciting action and less waiting, the now (Mostly) balanced combat, and the mostly improved difficulty curve I have to admit the game is now more fun and might actually be worth your time now. sure it's still basically Banjo-Kazooie N&B with the gathering and story replaced with a store and reskinned for SPACE, but N&B was fun if you ever played it for more than a hour in your entire lifetime. So, I'll give it a passing B-Grade, play it for a few weeks.

Robocraft is fun. In theory.
Yes you get to build practically whatever you can dream of, whether it is a B-17 bomber, or a Manga-inspired Mech. The creativity is a plus. I worked my way up to Tier 4 in just a few days because it started out being very enjoyable.
HOWEVER, it is very frustrating once you get to the actual meat of the game. You will constantly find yourself being utterly destroyed by players who have guns that are at least 1 tier higher than the tier you are currently playing; but because they have used low-class armor, they are gleefully placed in the same match as your lower-tier robot.
Which translates to one thing: Instakill stompfest. I have unistalled the game because I got tired of facing Meta-tanks with 6x Tier 5 Plasma Cannons and Tier 3 Armor, which could completely obliterate my well-rounded Tier 4 mech in a single shot.
Granted, this game is still in Beta, so it might not stay this way. However, I have been turned off by the sheer unbalance of the matchmaking system. Hopefully they get this fixed. Unfortunately, I will not be returning.

Alright, I've done another 20+ hours on the recent update and ready to update my Review.
They have really battled the imbalance that haunted this game. From most battles with 90% difference in scores, now most games are won by cooperation and tactic. Not overpowering yourself with 2 tiers higher weaponry as they used to be.
I wrote my review because I was strongly under the impression they where causing the imbalance on purpose, the forums where not allowed to express your unhappiness for the imba. So they really seemed to have a pay 2 win game, instead of a proper F2P game (F2P model works, don't worry about it FreeJam).
Luckily they seem to be going in the right direction, actually listen to the community. And greatly improved the major issue, imbalance.
The games feel properly balanced, most games are done by cooperation, teamwork and tactics.  You have to cover the medic, everyone can't be a machinegunnner, group up to take over or defend the towers. Unless the enemy team is as disorganised as your team, you need to work together to get things done.
And small changes like moving the leave battle option :) It's a tiny change but it's to try and get people not to leave battle without making it impossible to leave.
Or the spawntimer getting adjusted the more people leave. (This still needs some tweaking IMO, but its a good addition)
All in all, my recommendation changes from negative to positive. The game feels quite balanced, is very playable and besides Smite the best game I've played in a long time.
If you're anything like me, liked to play with Lego when little, watch Battlebots back when it was still on TV, bored with the snail like progress of Minecraft, own games like 7 days to die and other blocklike "builder" games. This game is for you!

Played this game for the last 3 weeks, and was lucky enough to experience the new spawn update... Quite fun, yet is frustrating in a few areas. This game has allot of room for greater potential, but is good.
Pros:
* Good Customisation, and has allot of variety in parts.
* Physics actually works in this game :)
* Quite a few game modes
* Tiering up was easy pre update, but I think it is fair now. Pre-update I went from T1 - T5 in couple of hours. Now the    burn is slow, but rewarding.
* Premium is good, you get twice the currencies in matches, and can have a fourth person in your platoon. But it isn't a must, which is fair.
* Allot of variety in Vehicle types, but room for more, I can think of a few at the top of my head.
Cons:
* NO PAINT CHOICE. Yep, you can't paint your own machine. You just have to look at the ugly bricks and colours you don't like. Cubes currently colour code the tiers, so Tier 4 cubes for example, are blue. Not good for people who hate the colour blue! (LIKE ME)
* Glitches. Yep in the tower mission, you must destroy the enemies tower, but sometimes it doesn't get damaged. The Ghost glitch, I HATE THIS ONE. 30 minutes into a match and someone ghost glitches, and exploits it, goes under the ground and destroys our tower, we can't attack him, just have to stand there raging!
* Matches are to long. I find the new battle mode long. As I said, 30 minutes is wow....wow. Some people eventually, quite during a match stuffing up the team. Sometimes even if the team is thrashing, a vital group mate will quit and there goes the glory! (Yes I've experienced these multiple times!)
* Lack of Environments. Just Snow and Desert. BORING.
* Devs are active on forums, but I find the forum community unhelpful.
What needs to be ingame:
* Paint Customistaion.
* More environment reskins, like dark volcanic, jungle, beach, moon and woodland forrest environments.
* More weapons, movements and extras. There's still allot of thnings that can make the cut.
* PvE npc enemies, bosses, and environment hazards like lava and water would be awesome.
* More game modes like steal the flag, arena, etc.
This game has ALLOT of room for potential, but is fun in the present.

Buying this alone, doesn't do the lore justice, I suggest that if you buy this game, you also buy the original Portal too.

I know a guy who said the game was horrible, because it was "too boring and confusing", (He probably couldn't beat the first part) I however, agree it's confusing, but it's always exciting, as maybe bullets fly around you as you run, or lasers make a criss-cross death trap, or maybe deadly goo will make "the floor is lava" a true saying. You WILL need to think outside the box to get through, you have to get so far outside the box, it may be a distant memory what "the box" was. Thought provoking chambers along with community maps always gives you something to do. Portal 2 is a must-buy for all action, puzzle, first-person fans. It truly is amazing.

Great game! Lots of fun to be had playing this, build your own little ship, whether it drives, flies, hovers or simply crashes and dies, it's a huge amount of fun! A must try for those that like World of Tanks or similar.
Of course being in Alpha means that it isn't clear of bugs and is not great on the server side at times, mainly when updates occur, but once it's working, and you get a good team together, it is brilliant! I'll continue to avoid doing more social things to play this instead.
There is in-game purchases but you can't buy things, to my knowledge, which give you an advantage over free-to-play gamers. They're either to jump ahead in terms of tiers (so you can literally just start the game and buy a tier 7 robot), or they're to buy things like holoflags to place on your robots and show off.
The system which you have to go through to progress through the game is cleverly done and keeps players at a reasonable pace when playing for free. I'm currently on Tier 8 but I have stuck in this Tier as this is where I find myself most comfortable with playing. You can quite easily jump back and fourth between Tiers so if a friend joins a week or two later you can go back and build one to play with them.
Unfortunately Platoons (how you play with friends) is limited to 3 players, unless you buy premium then you get 4. Which seems small but works well to keep teams balanced in matches.
Overall it is a fantastic start to a game which I believe will continue to grow as a community and continue to advance as it grows.

I've jumped on the Portal bandwagon a few years late, but after thoroughly enjoying the physics defying experience of Portal I pretty much went straight on to Portal 2, uncertain of how I would feel about the game in comparison to Portal.
I needn't have had any doubts. Yes it is a quite a different game but in this case it's worked wonderfully. After the fairly minimalistic plot of Portal it was great to see the story of Aperture Science fleshed out as I played through the game. The environments I encountered along the way were pretty breath taking and I really enjoyed some of the mechanics that weren't present in Portal.
I did find some of the puzzles extremely difficult to get my head around but that's mostly because I'm a bit dense in that department. If your brain works the same way as mine you may find yourself frequently understanding what you're supposed to do with each individual piece of a puzzle, but not quite being able to put them altogether. Just be prepared for the possibility of needing to seek help from the interwebs for a few things.
The co-op chambers are a lot of fun and the little Easter eggs throughout the game really add to the background detail.

Portal 2 has worked on the flaws that Portal suffered from (which was extremely short gameplay time) and has addressed these flaws into a truly beautiful gem of a game. Everything about this game just makes sense. Do yourself a favor a buy this game; it's definitely worth your time and money!

How to install Robocraft to your computer and get no lag:
Windows Vista/7:
Method 1:
Click the Start Icon.
Go to C:/Users/(username)/Appdata/roaming/.minecraft
Open bin and you will see minecraft.jar (It may appear only as minecraft).
Open the folder using an archive software (the most popular are 7zip and WinRAR). To do this, right-click on minecraft.jar and hover to the Open With menu.
Copy the class files into this folder. Exit the folder once you have copied the class files.
Certain mods will require you to copy files into other directories. Examples include:
- Resources folder (found in the main .minecraft directory)
- Config folder (found in main .minecraft directory)
- The .minecraft folder
Follow the instructions on your download for clarification on where to copy files to.

Portal 1 was basically everything and had to be and nothing it didn't. For being so focused, it was essentially the perfect experience.
Portal 2 takes Portal 1 and adds some new concepts. That alone would make it bigger, however this game doesn't have that same "focused" philosophy that the first Portal did. They wanted to create a longer experience and some padding was done because of it. Many times in the game you'll find yourself walking from test chamber to test chamber through the architecture of Aperture Science's walls. I appreciated going "behind the scenes" in the first game, but in this game it arguably detracts from the experience after a point.
However, a Portal game is still a Portal game and the puzzles that you do go through are all pretty great. As a whole, I still think the game shines--there's just tiny specks in between that fall short.
You'd think I'd end my review here and say that it's worth recommending, but Portal 2 is more than just its singleplayer campaign.
New to this sequel is a 2-player co-op mode with FOUR portals, 2 between each player. This is where the real value of the game lies, because there are tons of user-made maps that you can play through with your friends.
With this in mind, I'd DEFINITELY recommend this game--especially to the people who think that the co-op thing is up their alley.

A little too much, but there's still all that Portal goodness. Also, Cave Johnson is amazing.
Side note about something I don't like: GLaDOS DOESN'T SWEAR! I understand that she's vulnerable and confused and whatever, and she's a flawed character, but she's not flawed that way. She has command of more precise language, and I cringe both times she curses. I don't object to swearing in general in the Portal franchise (Cave Johnson again), but NOT GLaDOS!
EDIT: Kudos to Valve for making a protagonist with brain damage that reders her mute. Although I think that that may have been the case in the first one too. And Gordon Freeman probably has PTSD of some sort that makes him mute (though I just imagine him having facial expressions anyway).
EDIT 2: Actually, this game would work better as a prequel. The story of Portal 2 is completely unnecessary, but Wheatley, Cave Johnson, and the indirect history of Aperture is great stuff. What if there was, say, another earlier test subject that, one way or another, was tossed out of the test chambers and simply had to explore those old ruins, recordings, and whatnot with Wheatley also having just got down there, and being a sort of guide? That could be fun. In Portal 1, GLaDOS got all the characterization and closure she needed. Why have more? And why put Chell through more of it?
EDIT 3: You know what, it's fine the way it is. I just have nitpicks about GLaDOS's character development and the change in Aperture's "background aesthetic."
EDIT 4: Another utterly capricious change, but one I feel good about: I'll just say, for myself personally, that it's non-canon. The story's over after Portal 1, GLaDOS just reforms herself and keeps the facility running while Chell is left outside. Like Tremors 2, Portal 2 a fun little what-if that doesn't really need to exist and just needlessly extends the story, to the point of ruining the structure.

I've jumped on the Portal bandwagon a few years late, but after thoroughly enjoying the physics defying experience of Portal I pretty much went straight on to Portal 2, uncertain of how I would feel about the game in comparison to Portal.
I needn't have had any doubts. Yes it is a quite a different game but in this case it's worked wonderfully. After the fairly minimalistic plot of Portal it was great to see the story of Aperture Science fleshed out as I played through the game. The environments I encountered along the way were pretty breath taking and I really enjoyed some of the mechanics that weren't present in Portal.
I did find some of the puzzles extremely difficult to get my head around but that's mostly because I'm a bit dense in that department. If your brain works the same way as mine you may find yourself frequently understanding what you're supposed to do with each individual piece of a puzzle, but not quite being able to put them altogether. Just be prepared for the possibility of needing to seek help from the interwebs for a few things.
The co-op chambers are a lot of fun and the little Easter eggs throughout the game really add to the background detail.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

That said, loading times are horrendous; it frequently feels like the loading takes longer than the puzzle. It very much breaks the atmosphere though the game is so strong that it immediately regains it once the gaming restarts.
Oh, and then it has probably the greatest gameplay ending in video game history. This is, well, a bit special.

I was originally drawn to this game after finding 'Planet explorers', only to find that i need to upgrade my PC's graphics card and power supply to play the non creative side - (currently in the bit by bit pc upgrade stage) - I was originally drawn to Planet explorers due to the in game designing of the weapons and vehichles (and the rest of the game, but thats irrelivent/graphics card issue)...Robocraft uses a simpler version it seems, as the same creative mode in Planet explorers, so Robocraft scratches my itch for the creative aspects(amongst others)- explained further on in this review.
Robocraft is similar to such games as Hawken and World of tanks, the simple and quick battle instance shooter variety, with a sci fi/space theme.
The graphics and general gameplay are smooth and more than adequate for this type of game, i would imagine that even the lower spec pcs will have no issues running the game. ...After playing world of tanks, Robocraft seems less laggy, loading times for waiting to be injected into a battle instance, even when player numbers are at their peak, are around a minute.
Robot/vehicle creation part of the game, which is basically several different varieties of shapes/edges that fit within square fitiment manner, alongside many,many different types of battle ready parts - (armour types/shields/wheels/tracks/thrusters/hover blades/tracks etc)
has led me to spend many many hours playing about with wieghts and maximum robot/vehicle part limits - (based upon your experience level-which increases with the more time you spent playing Robocraft battles)
to create an upgraded, more battle efficient robot than its predecessor... of which you can test out of battle to fully figure out what works, and what doesnt...some of the results can be both impressive, or just a bunch of laughs messing around with things you already know wouldnt work...
I've spent more hours designing, than i have battling.
Through partaking in battles (a few game modes currently available/more to come in upcoming updates), you gain cash to spend on parts, and points to use within the quite vast array of unlockable parts within the tech tree, to further your efficiency in upcoming battles, used with knowledge gained via trial and error...
Personally, i find Robocraft to be well worth the time and effort, thoughroughly enjoyable, let alone free to play (However there is a 'cash shop' option, but its not really a 'Pay to win' kinda cash shop, unlike some/most others.

-TO DEVS:

-Skins for weapons/movement parts (would be cool and probably easy to do). Could work as premium benefits?

Robocraft is similar to such games as Hawken and World of tanks, the simple and quick battle instance shooter variety, with a sci fi/space theme.
I was originally drawn to this game after finding 'Planet explorers', only to find that i need to upgrade my PC's graphics card and power supply to play the non creative side - (currently in the bit by bit pc upgrade stage) - I was originally drawn to Planet explorers due to the in game designing of the weapons and vehichles (and the rest of the game, but thats irrelivent/graphics card issue)...Robocraft uses a simpler version it seems, as the same creative mode in Planet explorers, so Robocraft scratches my itch for the creative aspects(amongst others)- explained further on in this review.
Robocraft is similar to such games as Hawken and World of tanks, the simple and quick battle instance shooter variety, with a sci fi/space theme.
The graphics and general gameplay are smooth and more than adequate for this type of game, i would imagine that even the lower spec pcs will have no issues running the game. ...After playing world of tanks, Robocraft seems less laggy, loading times for waiting to be injected into a battle instance, even when player numbers are at their peak, are around a minute.
Robot/vehicle creation part of the game, which is basically several different varieties of shapes/edges that fit within square fitiment manner, alongside many,many different types of battle ready parts - (armour types/shields/wheels/tracks/thrusters/hover blades/tracks etc)
has led me to spend many many hours playing about with wieghts and maximum robot/vehicle part limits - (based upon your experience level-which increases with the more time you spent playing Robocraft battles)
to create an upgraded, more battle efficient robot than its predecessor... of which you can test out of battle to fully figure out what works, and what doesnt...some of the results can be both impressive, or just a bunch of laughs messing around with things you already know wouldnt work...
I've spent more hours designing, than i have battling.
Through partaking in battles (a few game modes currently available/more to come in upcoming updates), you gain cash to spend on parts, and points to use within the quite vast array of unlockable parts within the tech tree, to further your efficiency in upcoming battles, used with knowledge gained via trial and error...
Personally, i find Robocraft to be well worth the time and effort, thoughroughly enjoyable, let alone free to play (However there is a 'cash shop' option, but its not really a 'Pay to win' kinda cash shop, unlike some/most others.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

The game itself is also extremely fun, offering virtually limitless possibilites for different bots that are limited only by your creativity. The Devs are also constantly adding to this game. I in a little over 100 hours, I have reached teir 10 without paying in any money at all. 2 thumbs way up.

1 (15 ounce) can pumpkin puree
1 1/2 cups white sugar
1 cup packed brown sugar
1/2 cup butter-flavored shortening
1/2 cup butter, softened
1/4 cup whole milk
1/4 cup vegetable oil
4 eggs
2 cups cake flour
1/4 cup dry buttermilk powder
1/4 cup cornstarch
2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice
2 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
3/4 teaspoon salt
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line 24 muffin cups with paper muffin liners.
2.Beat the pumpkin puree, white sugar, brown sugar, shortening, butter, milk, vegetable oil, and eggs together in a large bowl until smooth. Whisk the cake flour, dry buttermilk powder, cornstarch, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in another bowl. Add the dry ingredients to the pumpkin mixture, stirring until mixed. Pour batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each cup about 2/3 full.
3.Bake in the preheated until the center of the cupcakes spring back when touched, about 30 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

I have to admit it: I love this game.
Maybe it's the frantic, yet strategic nature of the fights, or the hilariously imaginative community. The unobtrusive yet cleverly used chat function, or the satisfaction of hunting down your wounded enemies.
No.
No, strike that all, those arent the reasons I love this game.
The reason I love this game is because you can DO STUFF.
You want to spend the whole game building robot models of Megatron? You can do that.
You want to create the most absurd thing ever to fly, and cruise around lin a Flying Spagetti Monster? Absolutely.
You want to quickly copy a design of the net and rake in the kills? You do that.
You want to work your way up the tiers to mercilessly crush noobs in a Boss Fight? I know the feeling.
Or you want to strap a rocket to a chair and blast across the map like a lunatick, leaving bewildered freinds and enemies behind in a chaotic demonstration of individuality? Yes, you can do that too.
I don't feel like picking apart this game like a reveiwer should, because the game I play isn't the game you will play.
You can play Minecraft, World of tanks, Kerbal Space Program or Goat Simulator.
This game is whatever you want it to be.
Thats why I love this game.

Hello, ima tell you straight up why this game is GOOD and BAD.
good;
-the physics engine is pretty realistic, (weight balance, falling, flying, gravity..)
-weapon divisions are relatively balanced
-the freedom to mold and create your own form of robot is definitly +1 for creative builders
-not P2W
-can be played on low sys. specs.
bad;
-game is dominated by 6th graders
-no expandability for creation, you have players who dedicate the time to make models of actual tanks and airplane and then you have these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who make 5 brick twigs loaded with tier 10 gear to only humiliate all the time you spent building your robot in battle.
-railguns can one shot you.
-grinding your way up to tier 10 can be painful (look at how many hours I have and I'm only T6)
-playerbase communication is bad
-you can only use a specific weapon type for your vehicles (no smg + plasma combos)
-  robot design is limited early game when you only have a bit of RP and CPU to buy equipment and expand your robot with more blocks
-shield designs can be awkward and clunky to use.
verdict;
7.7/10
why? for people that need creative outlets for building ingenious functionality and robot designs, this is for you but keep in mind that this game requires dedication to rise into upper tiers of equipment, and the clunky spacing of weapons and gear can force you to redesign your robot.
