I felt like it was time to update my review:
I deleted all the old junk I wrote, as it was 2 years old and irrelevant.
So, without further ado...
I love it.  Yeah, controversial opinion here, but I love the game.
They've made tons of changes to it and lots of people have gotten upset about them, as have I, but on the whole the game is better than it used to be.
The problem is with player perception, and I have told this to Freejam many times.  If you do not put the effort into shining a good light on your own game through prolific media output and/or regular updates (which they do, but they aren't very good at writing them or speaking to their player base), then every little negative first impression people get of a change you make gets exacerbated tenfold.
I really wish Freejam would stop making excuses and advertise their game.  They have mentioned they don't think it's worth it because they would be competing against AAA titles...  Well... sigh...  I hate to break this to them, but they already ARE competing against AAA titles.  Any game your players flee to after they've had enough of yours can be considered your competition for that player's time.  The very same thing can be said for prospective players of your game.  One of hte biggest issues with Robocraft is its small concurrent player base.  They can say whatever they like about it, but it IS too small.  If it were larger, a lot of the matchmaking issues would be less of a problem.  As it is, they have too many game modes running at once to support effective matchmaking with the number of concurrent players they have.
I absolutely recommend this game, but I issue a warning:  This is not for you if you can't have a mature outlook about the loot crate system and Freejam's need to make money to support development.  This is not the game for you if you can't handle a game where you will be matched against players with far more experience than you on occasion and they will just trounce you.
This is a game for you if you have some actual patience and maturity.  This is a game for you if you believe in the potential I see in this game and I hope you will see it, too.  This is a game for you if you like a huge amount of creativity, but are aware of the fact that not everything is going to work half as well as you think at first.  A lot of players get discouraged easily and give up on this game.  If you get discouraged easily, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME.  You would be wasting your time and worsening our experience...
Some sage advice for starting out, if you're still with me:
Don't play with wheels or tank tracks right now.  They are terrible.  Instead, try to build something that uses hovers, or find a low cpu hover bot on the crf that has a decent rating and use that.
Stay under 500cpu as long as you can, because it keeps you matched against bots of mostly similar size and power to yours.
Learn not to die before you try to learn anything else.  Learn to watch the minimap, learn to pay attention to the indicators on the HUD and the voice telling you what's happening to your towers/reactor (in Battle Arena mode), and learn to watch the enemy spawn timers and avoid being around when a bunch of them respawn at once.
Learn not to tunnel-vision.  This means don't focus on killing one enemy bot to the exclusion of everything else around you.  That behavior loses games.
Learn to de-pin towers and the reactor.  There are crystals attached to teh inner pins of the fusion towers and protonium reactor.  Once you destroy all of these, the rest will fall off.  This is MUCH faster than destroying each individual crystal, and will greatly increase your win rate.
Welp, that's all for now.  :)  See you in the Battle Arena!

While singleplayer is challenging, I'll admit that co-op is slightly more challenging in a fun way. I've beat this game multiple times, and hasn't gotten any easier. It might be my crappy memory, and it might be my inability to actually be good at video games; either way, it's still fun in that makes-you-wanna-rip-all-your-hair-out way when you can't complete a chamber. The first time I played this game, it felt like I was falling in a dark pit, surrounded by pitch black nothingness. Second time, it got unnoticably brigther, but brighter still.
Then there's co-op. After my brother beat the game about 5 hours before me, he suggested we play co-op. Then he went to our grandparents house, and my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ self couldn't figure out how to wave so that stalled us from playing. But when I finally did figure out how to, we were then caught in other problems. Couldn't get out of the chamber. Thankfully, my idea came to the rescue! I felt so intelligent when I was able to get us out of that infuriating chamber with that one little dumb idea I had.
Really, the most infuriating part of this game is when your hands are starting to sweat or your fingers accidentally slip and you go whoosh! into the water, to your death. I can hear GLaDOS and her monotone voice as I type, mocking each little thing I do, or her arrogant voice during her little chats in the elevator ride or while you're sprinting down a hallway or something.
I rate this game an overall 8/10. HIGHLY recommended, completely worth every cent. Well, like 5 cents less, but still. It's a freakin' good game!

1.0 Review
Came back to Robocraft after several months absence.  Holy Cow a lot has changed!  I left a strong Tier 9 at level 80.  I came back to find the tech tree completely gone, all my blocks reshuffled and some refunded into "robits".
"Where is the pilot seat?  Is that not a thing anymore?"  Nope, it apparently isn't.
"Where did Mega battles go?  That was my favorite mode!"  Gone without a trace.
"WAIT, we AUTOHEAL now?!  What is the point of healers?" There is none.  Sell all the nano weapons as they have absolutely no purpose.
"I can have multiple weapon systems?!  What is this heresy?!"  Yup, why specialize when you can do everything...
"There is a bunch of new stuff.  I'll just reformat my old designs... WAIT, why can I not match the color!?"  Most colors are now "premium".  I'm stuck either going light blue and grey or not changing anything.  Lame.
"Wow, some of these new support items are really OP.  Deployable shield, teleporter, and energy battery feel really cheap to play against.  Holy Cow they are expensive!"
"Sprinting shotguns... F'ing sprinting shotguns..."
So yeah, came back already at high level.  Game is still fun but not as much so as it was when I left.  Loot crates are crap no one asked for.  Matchmaking balance is a sick joke.  Can still compete but it's a little less fun.  Don't know what I would say if I was just starting out.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EA Review
At first I thought, "Wow! Lego tanks!"
Other thoughts:
"Only three maps.  Not much variety in battles"
"Sure is Open Hunting Season on noobs in the lower tiers!"  The game heavily incentizes you to drop a few tiers and grief lower level players with gear they don't yet have access to.  Due to the robot ranking system, it's limited to basically the two tiers below your rank, but it's still frustrating when you can't win because almost everyone in your tier is picking on lower level players with gear they don't have access to."
"Aimbots seem to be a big problem with this game!  SMGs with single block accuracy from medium range over 20 shots... right.  The sniper rifle doesn't shoot where I point it half the time while other players seem to have instant pin-point accuracy without their laser pointer even getting near me.  At least plasma just looks like a hard weapon to master."
"Oh, my bad.  It's not all aimbots.  Some of it is server weirdness and lag glitches being coded stupid, letting players ghost around the map killing you while their body stays safely parked in the background"
"Small tanks (and their low profile) are nearly worthless due to the way the game handles damage, oddly.  Instead of it being a linear damage line, it's more like electricity in that it flows into all adjacent blocks.  Makes optimum building paterns look decidedly strange"
"Double that for jets.  They are so slow that lack of cover means death 99% of the time unless they one-shot you with multiple plasma on the first attack.  Plasma, the only gun type that shoots all the guns at once."
"Weird flying physics!  Makes jets hard to build"
TL:DR Fun when people aren't cheating, the server isn't glitching out and giving people free kills due to strange latency handling issues, and you build a tank by someone else's plans or master the arcane and counterintuitive damage overflow system.  But hey, it's free.  What do you wnat for free?

Definitely a must buy. Portal 2 is a wonderful puzzle game with a funny and heartwarming story.
In Portal 2 you learn more about Aperture Science in the past. And it's not like those mostly dull CW TV shows where you learn more about superheroes when they started. It is actually interesting because you learn more about GlaDOS herself (who she is and why she is insane). It is impossible to play this game without smiling from laughter as GlaDOS and the hilariously stupid Wheatley attempt to kill you. You will want to stop progressing through the game just to hear Wheatley try to "hack" a machine. Most of the time if you wait enough Wheatley will continue attempting to figure out how to get out of a certain situation. For example you will hear his hacking techniques where he makes a list of the objects in a locked room including a computer, the floor, and objects not in the room like pens.
Portal 2 has levels but there are parts of the game where you get out of the test room number i formula and explore the back of the facility in search of a way out. The test rooms themselves are very accessible. To test a hypothesis you don't have to do alot of work, where in other FPSes with puzzle elements you would have to backtrack the whole level to find one stupid cracked wall that looks different from other ones that you have to shoot. They also give you alot of hints in the design of the level. It's kind of hard to describe but the design of the levels (like railings on certain platforms or black spaces on certain places) scratches off some theories with wrong answers on how to solve some of the puzzles.
There is also coop but I have not played it yet. I have looked at the level editor and the great thing about it is that you cannot submit a level unless there is a solution. That definitely means that all the levels in the workshop are genuine.
This is a game that everyone can play and would want to play to the end. I wish Valve would make single player games again. Definitely get it and play it!

I've played robocraft long before i've installed it through steam ( easily have over a thousand hours in it ) starting over a year ago- a good while before robocraft had been added to the steam store.
Positive reviews are plentiful and they're well earned, This review however is about the negatives from the perspective of an old-time player.
So here's a couple words about the "endgame" and the "day-to-day gameplay" as it currently stands before the major 'meta-changing' updates which will come in a week's time from this day.
1 Expect to be frustrated, As any teamwork oriented PvP game goes there's allot that can go wrong.
Either your team picks the worst route to oppose the route enemy team takes / you get focused / become narrow-minded / half your team ends up being composed of people trolling
Or ( due to the phase of the moon & the fact that your neighbours conducted their rituals in the wrong order ) You may end up unable to connect to battles and/or experience an awkward amount of bugs.
Either way- you can easily end up spending over an hour without reaching the point where the game is enjoyable yet again
2 attitude- "Road rage" is very common in this game, people often end up swearing and arguing over nothing even without any ill intent ( we're all good people in bad circumstances ) and moderators aren't an exception
If you see someone manifesting road rage symptoms you'd be wise to simply ignore them, Simply replaying to them without a proper high-brow Dr. who impersonation may lead to you being silenced aswell.
While moderators and admins in robocraft are typically wonderful people and i've got several of them on the ingame friends list some have been laid off and sent to an anger management course, while others await in line.
3 progression- While it may certainly take a fair chunk of time to even get to Tier 10 / Tx1 aka endgame ( which is a good thing ) reaching that point is only the beginning, You'll be experienced with a couple playstyles but that's it, There are plenty ways to play the game which you may have never tried and I strongly recommend becoming familiar with as many playstyles as possible if you're interested in becoming a better pilot or builder, This is the stage where buying garage slots is extremely worth it.
And in the case of those who merely want to play, Many resort to copying mainstream designs for the purpose of a cheap playstyle which seriously hinders enjoyment of everyone else. ( a youtuber named "Smash Wutz" is especially guilty in this )
4 Nerfs / Balance- There are many "builds" which are borderline exploiting the game mechanics, Gone mainstream they have lead to nerfs directed at them which have sometimes crippled other playstyles/builds.
While i am certain FreeJam will eventually work it through, in the meantime many of us are developing a proper victim-syndrome. :P
To sum it up, You need nerves of steel to play this game on a regular basis.
I do recommend this game but this review is marked negative to express these aspects.

Definitely a must buy. Portal 2 is a wonderful puzzle game with a funny and heartwarming story.
In Portal 2 you learn more about Aperture Science in the past. And it's not like those mostly dull CW TV shows where you learn more about superheroes when they started. It is actually interesting because you learn more about GlaDOS herself (who she is and why she is insane). It is impossible to play this game without smiling from laughter as GlaDOS and the hilariously stupid Wheatley attempt to kill you. You will want to stop progressing through the game just to hear Wheatley try to "hack" a machine. Most of the time if you wait enough Wheatley will continue attempting to figure out how to get out of a certain situation. For example you will hear his hacking techniques where he makes a list of the objects in a locked room including a computer, the floor, and objects not in the room like pens.
Portal 2 has levels but there are parts of the game where you get out of the test room number i formula and explore the back of the facility in search of a way out. The test rooms themselves are very accessible. To test a hypothesis you don't have to do alot of work, where in other FPSes with puzzle elements you would have to backtrack the whole level to find one stupid cracked wall that looks different from other ones that you have to shoot. They also give you alot of hints in the design of the level. It's kind of hard to describe but the design of the levels (like railings on certain platforms or black spaces on certain places) scratches off some theories with wrong answers on how to solve some of the puzzles.
There is also coop but I have not played it yet. I have looked at the level editor and the great thing about it is that you cannot submit a level unless there is a solution. That definitely means that all the levels in the workshop are genuine.
This is a game that everyone can play and would want to play to the end. I wish Valve would make single player games again. Definitely get it and play it!

Portal 2 is another game most people have played before, and for good reason. It’s one of the best puzzle games in recent history. If you found the first Portal game a bit too challenging, I personally thought part 2 was easier, but that might just be because I knew what I was doing after having played the first one immediately before. Additionally, Portal 2 has a co-op option where you can go through custom maps with a friend (or stranger) and download new puzzle rooms from the Steam workshop.
Recap of Portal 1 (with spoilers):
In the first game you are a test subject in a testing facility called Aperture Labs, running through puzzle rooms guided by a computer AI named GLaDOS. About halfway through, you discover that GLaDOS has killed the people running the facility and is planning to kill you too after the puzzle tests are complete. After finally destroying GLaDOS, you make it to the surface but are dragged back down by someone/something that you don’t see.
Portal 2 takes place an unspecified amount of time after your failed escape attempt. In fact so much time has passed that the lab is falling apart around you and the world outside is supposed to be some sort of post-apocalyptic waste. Since the game takes place in the same universe as the Half-Life games, the Earth has probably been taken over by the Combine. You and your new pal Wheatley (the artificial intelligence sphere who woke you from suspended animation) try once again to escape the lab while avoiding the resurrected GLaDOS.
Like the first game, Portal 2 is a first person puzzle game where you use orange and blue portals to traverse test rooms and the ruined underground world where Aperture Labs is located. Your special portal gun shoots orange and blue portals onto specific surface types depending on whether your press the right mouse key or left. By passing through a blue portal, you come out the orange one, and vice versa with your momentum unchanged. Just like in Portal 1, quite a few of the puzzles are based on jumping from high places into a portal on the ground to come shooting out of the other one. A couple of new elements have been added, such as laser puzzles (directing beams of light into laser receptacles) and light walls (beams of light you can walk on).  This time around, you spend a lot more of the game outside of the pristine testing chambers and inside the vast underground chambers where Aperture Science Innovators built the facility. The place has a 1950’s feel to it and you can listen to a bunch of pre-recorded messages from Cave Johnson, the owner of Aperture.  The voice work here from J.K Simmons is great, and the humor in Portal 2 is fantastically done.
Pros:
+Portal 2 takes all the great stuff from the original game and adds more. More puzzles, more humor, and more backstory. The puzzles aren’t too difficult, at least in the beginning, which is great for me because if a game is too hard, I go right for the online guides.
+You get to know GLaDOS a lot better in this game than in the previous, and not just because the game is longer. You also hate each other right from the start, so there are a lot more insults being thrown at you.
+The game’s story mode is great, and there is a co-op mode available to play with your friends!
Cons:
-Not much, the game’s awesome!
This is probably nitpicking since there’s not much wrong with the game. The Steam achievements for Portal 2 are about half for multiplayer and I’ve never really liked relying on other people to get achievements. I originally wondered why the game installation was so big compared to Portal 1, and it seems that at one point Valve had ambitions to build an online marketplace for Portal 2, similar to the Team Fortress 2 or Dota 2 economies. Steam has a separate backpack for Portal 2 items and you were supposed to be able to buy cosmetic items for your multiplayer character (hats). Alas, it never really took off, so there’s not much demand online for Portal 2 in-game items. I imagine it’s because the co-op is only 2 players, and most likely it’s going to be a friend that you play with a lot. There’s not much opportunity to show off cool hats, as opposed to TF2 or Dota where you can play with 10 people at a time to show off your awesome swag.
All in all you should definitely give Portal 2 a try if you liked the first one or like puzzle games in general. It’s casual enough that you can play for 10 minutes at a time or you can really dive into the story and finish the game over a weekend. Portal 2 can be found pretty cheap quite often, especially if you go for the Portal 1 + Portal 2 bundle.

Definitely a must buy. Portal 2 is a wonderful puzzle game with a funny and heartwarming story.
In Portal 2 you learn more about Aperture Science in the past. And it's not like those mostly dull CW TV shows where you learn more about superheroes when they started. It is actually interesting because you learn more about GlaDOS herself (who she is and why she is insane). It is impossible to play this game without smiling from laughter as GlaDOS and the hilariously stupid Wheatley attempt to kill you. You will want to stop progressing through the game just to hear Wheatley try to "hack" a machine. Most of the time if you wait enough Wheatley will continue attempting to figure out how to get out of a certain situation. For example you will hear his hacking techniques where he makes a list of the objects in a locked room including a computer, the floor, and objects not in the room like pens.
Portal 2 has levels but there are parts of the game where you get out of the test room number i formula and explore the back of the facility in search of a way out. The test rooms themselves are very accessible. To test a hypothesis you don't have to do alot of work, where in other FPSes with puzzle elements you would have to backtrack the whole level to find one stupid cracked wall that looks different from other ones that you have to shoot. They also give you alot of hints in the design of the level. It's kind of hard to describe but the design of the levels (like railings on certain platforms or black spaces on certain places) scratches off some theories with wrong answers on how to solve some of the puzzles.
There is also coop but I have not played it yet. I have looked at the level editor and the great thing about it is that you cannot submit a level unless there is a solution. That definitely means that all the levels in the workshop are genuine.
This is a game that everyone can play and would want to play to the end. I wish Valve would make single player games again. Definitely get it and play it!

Playing this game can be frustrating at times.  As you get into the higher tiers, you start to see more and more opponents that have intentionally made their machines out of low tier blocks with high tier weapons to troll newer players.  The game also suffers from only having one mode of play for now, though they are at least working on more. While you can earn everything for free, this game does have pay to win elements in the form of being able to turn low tier tech points into uber points with the premium currency, which can then be used to fast track a person's unlocks.  Add that to the fact you can also use the premium currency to buy parts, and even buy whole robots, and you get a noticeable gap in gameplay all around.  All in all, until the devs fix the high tier weapons in low teir problem, and make more than two planet styles for maps, I'd only play if you're prepared to lose a lot in the early tiers. (Made it to tier 4, that's where it really starts getting bad)  May update this guide once the new modes come out, they may change things.

Robocraft is an amazing Arena-FPS-type (and third-person over-the-shoulder shooter), featuring *completely* customizable robots. Helicopters, tanks, wheeled vehicles, helicopters with tank tracks and wheels, winged flying vehicles, walking legs (think bugs) for mobility that can walk up sheer cliffs, vehicles with no obvious mobility (or with only sleds), hovercrafts (with anti-gravity hover devices), all equipped with slow-moving lightly-arching AoE cannons, innacurate machine guns, or highly accurate, high damaging, scoped Rail cannons.
Want to make a bot that sits on base and defends? Sure, no problem. Want to make a bot that is too fast for most people to shoot, good at scouting, but with no firepower? Doable. Everything can be done, with the inherent balance of the bots being that you may only place a certain amount of points (CPUs) on the bots; “blocks” for chassis design cost next to nothing, but weapons, shield-plates, and attachments all require more.
Free and definitely worth trying!

At first this game had some serious problems
like how they used ranks, levels AND tiers and it was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to figure all of that out, plus the amount of cash you were getting after every battle was miniscule.
But all of that is in the past, I came back to it recently to see how this game was doing and I was pleasantly surprised, they got rid of the tier limitations (you could use blocks/weapons/items from only one single tier which meant that you were stuck in one place for ages before you could move onto the next level/tier) they added tons of new blocks/hardware/weapons and most importantly they balanced stuff out so you're not going to get that one OTKfag that has a tiny tier 1 vehicle and a goddamn tier 4 weapon... that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t is gone which makes stuff hard for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and trolls.
This game is free to play, although it does have microtransactions, it doesn't make the game unbalanced or uneven, the extra items you get through microtransactions are purely aesthetic meaning it doesn't affect your gameplay and getting premium only increases the amount of money you gain at the end of each battle... it doesn't even affect the amount of exp you gain to level up.
There is one more thing I feel I need to point out however,  and that is the fact that the devs constantly work on it, improve it and try adding new things, most updates carry big changes with them (for eample recently an entirely new gamemode was added with a new map) so it doesn't feel that you play a game that's just stuck in one place.
There is always something new, and that's great.
But that can also be a bad thing.
Because the devs constantly work on it (even though it is a fully finished product) there are times when they make a bad decision that might ruin the game for some, for example: this review was originally written in 2015 but so much has changed that I needed to come back to this review and update it, for starters they got rid of the whole online cash stuff, now everything relies on drops (yeah they added drops), the devs thought this would be a better idea because instead of having to save up money to buy some blocks or weapons that are expensive, instead you can just get them straight away after each battle.
Cool idea, but the problem here is that most items you need never show up, it's a one in a million chance, all you get is the standard basic building blocks.
So the devs added an option of buying them from a store, no more "tech tree" that required you to have a certain level in order to be able to buy a certain block or weapon, but there's a catch, and that is they cost (no, not pay to play crap, don't worry) How do you get this currency? well you don't get currency after any matches, the only way you can get any currency is by going to the menu and selling the blocks/weapons you have, meaning that if you are saving up for an item after every game, you get the blocks/weapons, then you need to go to the "recycle blocks" menu, remember which blocks you just got and sell them for currency and only then you can use this currency to buy what you actually need.
And then there's the price drop.
Normally, in most games (this was also the case in this game before they changed it) when you sell an item at a store, you sell it for 50% of the price of the item in the store which means that you lose 50% of its value... but for some reason the devs thought it was a good idea for each block to sell at 10% of its value... this means that everytime you sell your blocks or currency you actually lose 90% of the value... and this is the ONLY WAY of obtaining the currency needed to buy the items you want, so basically you're stuck in a russian roulette loop hoping you will get the item you want because saving up now takes forever... literally, I just played approximately over 5 constant hours, got lucky with some good drops and I only saved up 1/6th of the price I need...
This was an example of how constantly improving and trying new things in the game can go wrong, I am sure however that they will change it eventually, because this wasn't the first bad idea I've seen them apply and they always change it back or fix it, overall, despite being currently disappointed with the most recent change I do reccommend this game because I know it's only temporary and the amount of good decisions they make far outweigh their bad decisions.

, a new player I convinced into playing.
This has been something I've said for a very long time: Every game has a curse, whether it be buggy patches, inconsistent player count, inactivity, things of that nature. Robocraft got a bad curse - The worst kind, the kind that every developer whether in a large corp or a basement dweller like myself fears in their worst nightmares: The asshurt, b*tchy playerbase.
Most of the vets I've observed on the forums will barely come short of throwing an entire fit over every update. In fact, people have even screamed to "fix (blank) by doing (blank)", and - I'm not kidding here - after they released the fix, these players went back to FJ and told them it was a bad fix. Even typing that makes me furious - These spoiled brats think they can just b*tch and moan to get their way, and when FJ gave them the benefit of the doubt they spat at them because
(--every spoiled kid ever).
Now, think about it: When FJ pretty much gave those bratty players the finger because of what they did and just moved on with the game, they all ragequit and left their -1. Now, I'd be OK with some of these -1s if these players didn't do what they're doing:
Yes, you read that right. Look on any 3rd party blog or board that FJ linked to from their website and go to the comments - In the vast majority of those articles you get people saying "yeah no this game is sh*t" (or similar).
With that in mind, I truly hope that I have somewhat made you reconsider some of those -1s. Everything I say up there is clearly observable. If you go to the forums on Robocraft's website and go back far enough, you'll see this constant b*tching.
This seems to be a recurring thing in some reviews. I don't know the exact reason they may call it this, but I
that it's not true. Chances are, they are angered because there's a "premium row" to crates that gives you more items, but otherwise has the same rarity modifiers and such. While this does raise the possible concern of "What if I get an Epic / Legendary in the premium row?", I would like to point something out: The small weapons are not only cheaper than the large ones, but can deal the same damage
of a bigger version of the weapon. The way Robocraft works is entirely flat. Should you design a small robot that has many small (cheap) guns, the game will grant you a damage boost because you are a small design with little health. That way, you can deal a lot of damage in a little time at the cost of being killed a bit faster. An excellent team resource, if done properly. Alternatively, you can build big and have a lot of health, but you won't do so hot damage wise. Additionally, big weapons use a lot of energy. The largest plasma cannon can only fire four shots before you're out of energy and delayed. The smallest one can nearly endlessly fire (It still goes down, just really slow) and is really good to use if you've got damage boost on your side.
Robocraft is very very friendly to new players. As I said above, you really can't tell who's premium and who's not via performance (That said, you can tell via paint color on the robot). As a premium user, I feel no more powerful than any other player in the battle. In fact, my newbie friend has been able to best me on the battlefield many times over - just as much as I have bested him. FJ is incredibly talented at creating these power changes and you can't blame them for not being 100% accurate. This game is based on user creativity, and the numbers you give weapons for damage have to somehow fit every scenario. Do you know how hard that is? FJ isn't perfect, but they have certainly done a good job with it. If you fight back against a guy with good guns, you have a good chance of winning.
As I said in the first header, most of those reviews are skewed or made for the purpose of revenge. I've read them all, and each of them seem to be truthful if you change the perspective to the shoes of the salty players. I have been a very friendly and postive player, and I am nice to the developers. The developers have certainly done their best to return the favor to me. By maintaining a positive outlook, being flexible and dynamic, and being patient, I have pushed through the common flow of ragequitting and have instead posted this positive review. I am also doing all in my power to convince people that this game really is worth it. So please, give it a try anyway, see if you get a kick out of it. If you end up liking it, well, there you go.
Despite the negative review-status of the game, I'm telling you that this game is still fun and is a good thing to play. I most certainly hope you enjoy it. So please, give it a try anyway even if the reviews look like crap. I think you'll have fun.

And the microtransactions are by no means mandatory - this game is free to play, not pay to win. RoboCraft is a game about building your own vehicles and fighting other people's vehicles. Vehicles are voxel like while the terrain you fight in isn't. Currently the game modes: team deathmatch, last team standing wins or you can capture the other team’s base; the pit, free or all, first to 20 wins; battle arena, MOBA styled gameplay where you basically take out the other team’s base.
It comes with free premium until 2016 for existing players. Lot’s of major changes. They added a paint gun so you can color your blocks whatever color you want, but now tiered blocks don’t exist like T1-T10. So you can now be creative with color and not suffer a combat disadvantage. Speaking of creativity have 25 garage slots to be creative with. It’ll be infinite garage slots later on so that limitation of 3 is gone. They also added new blocks to be creative with.
Combat wise there isn’t a pilot seat anymore so you die if <25% of your bot is left now. Being stuck crippled somewhere isn’t a thing now since if you don’t participate in combat for 10 seconds you auto heal. There’s alot more so I won’t dive further into the update.
People who like designing vehicles
People who like vehicular combat which includes tanks, airplanes, helis, etc. (You can just buy robots from the robot factory with RP you get from battling if building isn’t your strong suit)
People who like shooters

In a very pleasent surprise, this game didn't turn out to be just a longer version of the original Portal game.  I thought it would be difficult for Valve to create a sequel to the first without making it so similar that it seemed like the extended edition of Portal 1, but they stepped up to the plate and did very well for themselves.  Just from the first few minutes of gameplay you can already tell that the second installment in the Portal franchise has a meatier story with interesting characters and still brings it's signature humour from the orignal title.  GLaDOS is still a very important part of the story and is involved in a very special moment involving a 9 volt battery and a potato.  You also still play as the female protagonist in this installment.  The stunning attention to detail in the level design and the atmosphere is phenomenal and really struts Valve's stuff.
Portal 2 expands on the standard portal gun gameplay from the original while adding these fun new mechanics called gels, but I'll let you find out more about those buggers.  The puzzles this time around aren't easy, but they're all reasonable and don't seem to require Stephen Hawking to decypher.
As great as everyone knows the Portal storyline is, the co-operative feature added to this Portal really makes it stand out.  Grab a friend and take your shot at some co-operative humour-based puzzle fun to see who's the worse at navigating a light bridge!
Overall the only real downside I see is that once you've finished the single player and the co-operative modes, there isn't much replayability here, especially considering I don't know anyone who really delves into the map editor feature and all, but it is certainly worth the 15 or more hours of fun regardless.

Robocraft is a multiplayer sci-fi action game built upon well balanced coding, mechanics, and provides a third party software that prevents users from infiltrating the software to hack the game. It provides a well done system of upgrading your vehicle in the tech tree and allows the player to use their imagination. The art style is neat, the gameplay is well done, and the servers are reliable. However the game does have some major disadvatages and limits that can overall ruin the gaming experience. 1: the game doesnt allow you to use multiple weapons. This may not be a bad thing for some but this is a major letdown that demolishes the chance of having any variety within the robots you create. That doesnt mean there should be no limits to what your ship can withhold but that doesnt mean you should only allow one turret to be used at a time. 2: The premium content. I dont mind having a little premium content in every once in a while but some features that would be excellent within the game are inacessable without any cash... i know its a free title but i just want to mention it. 3: the lack of gamemodes. The game does let you use a HUGE assortment of guns, blades, rotors and other creative stuff but there is basically only two gamemodes, challenge mode and just a normal match. A normal match is when you claim a basic base that is in the same exact location in every map or kill all the players trying to face you. Challenge mode is the same but you are against higher level players whiles you have a army of lower tiers. These cons of this robotic deathmatch of a game are pretty bad, but the pros of it all are overwhelming. Also since this is a totally free to play game i rate this a 9/10: It is an excellent game to play. Try it out for yourself! I know you'll like it!

This game used to be great. Play the game, get RP, buy new stuff, play some more. Now, your success relies entirely on the kindness of an RNG Lootbox system. New weapons are almost impossible to get unless you are extremely lucky OR you pay real-world money for both Premium status AND a bunch of loot crates, and even then you have a chance of blowing over $100 and STILL not getting what you want. Recycling system is extremely limiting, as it only gives you 1/10 of the value of your items, meaning that you either have to be lucky enough to get what you want, or save up enough from weeks and weeks of playing to buy ONE good weapon.
EDIT: It now gives ~1/5 value, 3/5 if you have premium. Still takes forever since you won't be recycling the majority of rare and legendary items you find. They have also added Robits directly to lootcrates, but in rather low amounts.
In short, this game is no longer free to play OR new-player friendly. Many people have been complaining about the state of the game and FreeJam has yet to do anything to fix the major flaws in their business model.
Allow me to quote a part of the FreeJam mission statement, so that you can compare it to what I just stated above:
“Freejam (the developer of Robocraft) has community in its blood. The word Freejam is a combination of 'free' and 'jam', where 'free' shows our dedication to keeping Robocraft always free, and 'jam' stands for jamming with our community to determine how our game continues to evolve. We like to think of Robocraft as a game that has been built from the ground up in collaboration with the community.”
Congratulations FreeJam, you have failed on both parts.

I've always been a fan of procedural destruction, and blowing custom built bots apart (and getting your own bot torn to pieces) or healing them up really scratches that itch. Just the core mechanic of trying to shoot off important bits of your opponent and design your own bot in a way that makes that hard hasn't stopped being fun yet, half of what makes healing so fun for me is watching bots regrow piece by piece.
Something else I'm a huge fan of is asymmetric warfare. Anyone play Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy? The 2v1 mode was really cool there, and I think more games should have alternate modes with uneven teams evened out by a difference in power that favours the smaller side. Robocraft’s Challenge Mode does this very nicely in my opinion, pitting a team of 4 against a team of 12 in a Boss Battle. Totally my favourite thing, whether it’s being a desperate medic as part of the 12 or dispensing death as part of the 4.
You can only queue as a Boss once every 10 hours, which is a shame. From the wiki: “Due to technical difficulties and unexpected server problems, Boss Battles have been rationed to 1 battle every 10 hours. This is not the intended time slot for boss battles and will be reduced down once the current issues being experienced with boss mode are fixed. The original intended wait time between boss battles was meant to be 20 minutes, and fluctuate depending on server population, this goal has not been changed.”
250 hours in I still feel like I've got loads of the game left to explore, like I've not quite got a Megabot yet (an extra tier for gargantuan bots with a 5 times higher block limit - in the top tier of regular play each team is joined by a single megabot). The game is about to get a massive overhaul too, which sounds like it's going to make the game much better in terms of how matches work. There'll be respawning, objectives to capture and defend that power defensive structures, quasiMOBA levelling up your bot in matches (with a choice of what set of abilities you have as part of building a bot), all sorts.

There's creative Fun to be had in building weapons of mass destruction.
Requires a lot of time in design phases to stay competitive, and has myriad netcode and balance issues.
7.4/10 Great fun, but requires too much effort in some areas.

I am by no means an expert, I am just an unbiased consumer. I read the reviews and was so excited about trying this game, and I am absolutely floored by what I've found. Yet another absolutely delightful idea for a game, so well put together, so customizeable and replayable, and then they ABSOLUTELY destroy it with pay to win. You really don't need to read further if you don't want to, that should have been enough there. To explain a bit further, this game pretty much allows people who have either spent countless hours farming to unlock certain items, and farm the money to purchase the upgrades, to go into the lower level games with a very small tank, with a gun that can 1 shot anybody. This already being a huge problem, is just exacerbated by the fact that people who want to spend real money can do the same thing, unlock the best upgrades, and then smoke through the lower ranks, 1 shotting every player and reaping the benefits. I'll put this into perspective. you just spent 10 minutes making the perfect tank, it's well balanced, has all the weapons you want, you're so excited to get into a game with people who are close to you in rank. queue up, 20 seconds, you get into a game. another 30 seconds goes by for the start of the game, you go RACING off down the track. You're totally going to find someone, kill them, and get to the enemy base and win the game right? Wrong. red beam appears and you get shot once, dead. What the hell? I have to requeue now?   fast forward, you've gone through the queue again. you're racing off down the track. a green tank rolls out in front of you, you start throwing EVERYTHING you got at it. just, a barrage of laser firepower, you are OWNING this g...   one hit kill again?  this time to a barrage of 6 giant red cannons. fine... I'll just be more careful, and not get close enough for them to do that again. fastforward a couple minutes, in another game, you're creeping up toward the base, hoping to get the jump on a defender. you make it to a ravine, across the way you see a teenie tiny spec. red laser again? oh♥♥♥♥♥♥you gun it and... oh awesome not a one shot kill, but he has somehow knocked all of the wheels off your left side, you're a sitting duck for one of the other players to come over and kill you.
TL;DR  Great idea, the fact that higher levels can come in and smoke you in one shot all day, forcing you into endless queues ruins it, along with the pay to win players doing the same.
P.S. There is no report system for the trolls either, your own teammates can come over and basically shove you around into a corner until someone comes to kill you. This happens. A LOT. pretty much if you're getting creative and your ship doesn't look like it's balanced out enough to survive a hurricane, someone is going to troll you, roll you, stick you against a cliff and leave you for dead.
It would be more nice if the technical difficulties problem finished ASAP

Oh god, this game is amazing.
First, I'll go over the graphics. The stylized graphics set in a futuristic world make for a great experience, the only thing to complain about is how SMGs have no S-Types (The orange circle icon) and nothing matches it.
The gameplay in Robocraft is very unique, gaining depth as tiers go up. At first there's a SHOOT IT IF IT MOVES mentality, but as of tier 2 electroplates, hovers, and thrusters are introduced, and these will level as they go. Low tiering (Bringing high tier items into lower tiers, often called seal clubbing) is an obvious problem, and can screw up new players, but ultimately doesn't affect play as much as other tiered games.
Megabots at Tier 10 are a great addition.  Like a giant meat shield of a team leader, when your mega isn't serious or is a WIP, your team is ultimately screwed. Being able to use mega parts on non-megabots is a bit of a problem but like low-tiering, isn't too much of a problem.
The 5 weapon types in the games have their own problems in and of themselves. SMGs, the typical subatomic machine gun, or as I like to call them, the scrub machine gun, are drive-forward-make-it-die kind of guns. Little skill is required ad despite being "nerfed into the ground, these weapons are dominant at high tiers, and any other poorly prepared bot is not going to make it out looking very well. Also, the mega is huge as heck and shoots twice as fast. Go figure.
Plasma is the second unlock at Tier 3. A kind of artillery type, these are usually adapted by people traumatized by low tierers. The only non hitscan tank of a weapon has a slow recharge and heavy damage, with the mega shooting 2 volleys doing 20k damage from 1 shot. The only problem I have with these is that THEY HAVE NO FREAKING WAY TO COUNTER SMG 1V1S. So yeah, that needs to be nerfed/buffed.
Rail guns are for the sniper in us all. Charging over 12 seconds, and firing individually over a long range to do massive damage if aimed right. Building a sniper is hard as getting the crosshair to match the gun's positioning is a difficult task. The scoping mechanic needs to be changed according to gun placement, in my opinion. It would make rails an easier to pick up weapon for new players. Rail spam is another issue. My suggestion to fix this is rails doing less damage the closer to the target.
Nanotech disruptors are for team players and point farmers. Essentially healing targets and rebuilding a vehicle. With 2 targeting modes, auto and manual, these guns are the perfect killsteal guns and late-game tide turners. I have no problems with these weapons at all. These guns need more love.
Like blowing things up with giant bolts of electricity? Tesla blades are for you. A not-so-subtle homage to Nikola Tesla, the high power coils will produce an explosion on impact with T8 having 1 use, T9 having 2 and T10 having 3. These can be healed back on from medics. The thing about these is they make great mega destroyers. Maybe increasing CPU on teslas will stop walls of blades from being the robotic equivalent of David VS Goliath. Tesla are mostly balanced and I reccomend them to any nano user or high-speed-charger alike.
Robocraft has many unique ways to move, and I'll start to go over them here. Wheels are first up on our rolling roster. Being very basic and the first to start out with, wheels are really wheels. You unlock these first and get bigger as you go. They hit max size at TX-1 megabot size where you question your sanity they're so huge. Overall speedy but not the beefiest.
Enter Hover Blades, the hovering force of the game. Dominant at higher tiers, especially with SMGs. You hover above the ground at a not-too-high place with a decent speed, increased by thrusters. Overall balanced and nice to use.
Thrusters can be used as a stand-alone, in notoriously evil thruster sticks. Sink a fortune into some thrusters and build a metal sandwich of death. Constantly annoying and begging to be nerfed, thruster sticks need a change, and more than just a rudder adjustment, *cough cough DotM Hotfix #5 cough cough*
Next comes the aerial attackers, the flyers. Flying high, powered by thrusters, wings and their counterpart, rudders, flyers are most commonly plasma, attacking craft with aerial bombardment. Interceptors are less common, but still exist. Medic flyers will swoop down to heal friendlies and tesla kamikazes will make you pee your pants with laughter or poop them in suprise. SMG and Rail Guns are prime AA weapons and I crai every taim an SMG is oblivious to aircraft.
Lo and behold, I descend upon the tank treads to caress them with my highly judgmental nose. Tanks are beefiness' answer to wheels, much like how the jackalope is Texas' answer to the minotaur. Beefy and unable to be lifted, tank treads are slower than a snail made of molasses. They are extremely durable and well balanced.
Walker legs are next on the list. Basically a giant upgrade to bionic legs, these decently slow legs can climb upside-freaking-down. Great for rails and hybrids, the walker legs have no real setbacks besides there slowness.
Finally, copters boil down to hover blades and wings having a 20 pound baby. Flying high in the sky, the helicopter class is basically a giant hover with more height. A balanced way to move. Onto technology!
The technology part of the tech tree is a bunch of gimmicks you never knew you loved until you bought them and used them. Radar allows you to see enemies on the minimap, jammers allow you to stay hidden (FreeJam, how have you not made free T1 jammers? FREE JAMMERS? Eh? Eh?) and radar receivers can pick up friendly radar signals to create a large web of radar. No problem with these, except that receivers cancel out any reason to have a radar dish. Maybe require a dish to make them work.
Overall, great game, made even greater by the fact that it is in Early Access. Can't wait for what the future holds, FJ!

I seriously want to like this game. SO much. The idea behind it is VERY unique, the building mechanics are quite good, the customization between all the different vehichles are AMAZING, the fanbase is fairly nice (compared to things like the hyper-devoted fans of things like COD) the controls are.. pretty good I guess, and so on.

But the focus on the P2W aspect destroys it. unless you spend about 25 years playing constently, you HAVE to spend an insane amount of money on the blocks, the weapons, the movement parts, and everything else in the game in order to make something at least semi-decent. And even if you make it to that point, their are always people that spent more money than you did, and procceding to get even better items, making balance get thrown out the window.
And though I didn't start playing it when this was supposedly implemented, I have heard news recently about a supposed "EasyAntiCheat" system that they have put in place to help against the cheating issue that was very prevalent. Sound kinda iffy, but whatever. The cheater thing was VERY bad when I played, so this could have helped.
But then I start reading steam forums and reveiws talking about how EAC is a malware that sends things like keypresses, chat messages, screenshots, and even PASSWORDS into PUBLIC ACCESS, as in for ALL to see.
This... is a STUPID idea by the developers, because this will make players fear even installing the game because they will think "oh god, i might get hacked by EVERYONE." I would rather deal with hackers making playing the game harder than have my privacy COMPLEATLY removed for "safety reasons" Discusting. THIS is why you should just use VAC
So, in the end, the game in itself is great, but the P2W aspect, as well as this "EasyAntiCheat" malware ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, makes this almost compleatly unplayable.

The amount of hours I have invested into this game should be proof alone.
A fantastic FTP that inspires creativity, one could argue that you could pay to win however that assumption is not acccurate. Not only do you need to log some battles, you have to win them as well in order to achieve "tech Tokens" to unlock other components for your bot. You can convert these tokens into Uber Points via "galaxy Cash" aka $$$ to unlock higher tier goodies but only if you unlocked the adjecent items on the tech tree. I would also like to point out that the Mega Seat cannot be bought with Galaxy Cash (at the time of writeing this review) and costs 1,000,000 Robo Points (achived by playing).
You can biuld many various platforms: hovers, cruisers, tracks, walkers, drones, flyers sporting a balanced variety of weapons: plasma, rail, SMG, nano tech, and tesla blades.
My only complaint would be people bringing in uber tiered weapons in a low tier battle, essentially the "one shot wonder".
However the Devs keep adding new and interesting updates, different game modes are coming soon and it looks promising.

But even after that, the game still feels good after 2 (soon to be 3) years of gameplay.
Pros:
- Cool looking robots
- Robot art
- Frequently updated
Cons:
- Some people are clueless (no offense) and don't care about cspture points
- Some robot types are superior over others most of the time.
Conclusion: It's still one of the best games I've played after 2 years.

This is literally my favorite game of all time. I was first introduced to the Portal series at my friend SomeMaddness's house but never thought much of it. Then again, I feel like i might have been a bit to dreamy to realize the beauty of this game. Portal 2 takes place some 20,000 to 50,000 years ahead of Portal 1. As you probably already know, Aperture Science has fallen apart and we don't know much more. You play as Chell, the daughter of an unknown Aperture Science Employee (i think it might be Ratman) and she has to "Test her way throught he game!" as I put it... Well anyways not to blab on about it (i could talk about it for hours, no seriously ask my friends, and I strongly reccomend it. If you have not played Portal, then...(shame) but if you have not you can still enjoy this game for countless hours. Ive Played for 44 hours when i wrote this review, and if you are reading this, then i probably have played more by then. There are TONS of hidden little easter eggs EVERYWHERE (if you know where to look) and I really think that there are some even I don't know. Now don't get me wrong, this game is confusing! You might spend as long as 10 minutes on some of the test chambers, but if you are doing bad you are probably over-thinking it. (no seriously, I spent 20 minutes on a chamber where all I had to do was not pay attention to the extra bits) and i have played, and replayed the game multiple times. The Co-Op is a joy to play, unless your friend won't listen to you, (tornadofighter3 you know who you are.........) but if you have a good friend who will listen to you, its easy. Unless you have a bad internet connection, because it that case, you end up with a monitor with the screen punched in. Buy this game but i reccomned getting the Portal-Portal 2 bundle because its cheap and worth the money. First game I ever bought on Steam, best game I ever bought on Steam. If you stuck with this Heck of a long review this long you better give yourself a pat on the back because this is a LONG review. I will warn you, when you finish you will be grasping for more, so I reccomend the "Thinking with Time Machine" community made mod. I personally haven't finished it and it is WAY harder than Portal 1-2 combined. Once you play this and Portal 1, you will realize that Valve needs to go back to preschool and figure out how to count to three... Well I reccomend this game and really want you all to get it and enjoy the counless hours of rage induc...happiness. =P

Old review from 2015-09, not recommending the game:
The (alpha-version) game changed really much within the last month. Some changes were good, many were bad in my opinion. Therefore I change this review to be non-recommending so it does not give a wrong advice about the game.
What I don't like at the moment about the game are the buggy HUD during fights, many many disconnect I get just after a match starts (despite a very stable internet connection), that there is only one match type left and the new system of the tech-tree.
Old review from 2015-04, recommending the game:
This game is great. And I cannot even compare it to another great game because I think the developers created the first of it's kind: A mixture if level 'em up, collect 'em all (heavy meta-gaming  included), Cubes (so it is MineCraft-like) and a 3rd Person Shooter. Great (-:
I have played 50 hours so far and have not reached the highest level so I cannot say anything about replayabiliy on the very long term.
I found RoboCraft by coincidence and really like it. It is still in development and although some nice features have been removed (to make it easier understandable i guess) even more good features have been implemented. Go ahead developers (-:
What I like the most about this game - especially in comparison to many other games these days - is that it feels technically mature: Steering and controling the robots feels natural, the robot editor is good, shooting and hitting works without glitches, even the HUD is good.
The only draw-backs so far are:
1) that there are only a few different maps to play. But since this game is still in development at the moment ("early access"), for sure more will come.
And 2) that Premium-mode expires after e.g. 48 hours real-time. I'd prefer something like 16 hours game-time instead.

1) If you are a healer, you are not a Tank. Don't going rushing into combat first...on your own.
2) Going by yourself will lead to your death and possibly your whole teams death.
3) If you are facing a group of higher Tier characters, stay together as a group. You will and can make it out alive. if you go alone, see complaint A2.
4) Healers, don't ditch your f****** non-healers in the middle of combat, they will die, and you will die too shortly afterward.
5) In regular combat, make small groups that go together, they gave us 30 seconds before a match for a reason.
Why the game is awesome.
A) Game Praise
1) It's legos on cocaine.
2) Non-stop Deathmatch
3) Hardly any DM wait times unless (see A1)
4) The Tier system is pretty cool. Flops are tough but fair. (Your points for how much stuff you can put are your bot)
5) Lets you do almost whatever you want build-wise.
B) People Praise
1) Most of the players are funny, fair and good sports.
2) When a team works well, its the best thing in the world.
3) When the healers do their jobs and do them well, they are the most loved and respected players.

All in all, the game is really well made, and really well done. If they fixed the issues with the games, I would give it a 10/10. But since these issues are still present....Final Score (for now)
7/10

there are 11 tiers from tier 1-10 and tx-1

Robocraft is a creative game allowing you, the player to build tanks, planes and anything you wish.The game is a multiplayer online experience on the line of "World of Tanks". :Negative: The game is fairly entertaining, however there is not really a good matchmaking system thus you might get paired up against a very powerful team. The seperation of tiers helps this, but the game still is not very well balanced. The game is free to play so if are willing to put in some time, you will not lose any money. The biggest problem however is that it takes a long time to get anywhere. You can not build a plane until halfway through the game, and this put a damper on my spirits when I first booted up the game. When you get to the fourth tier, you will start noticing a big problem. The railgun( ie sniper rifle. The rail gun puts a very big handicap on people trying to get through the game as you will notice yourself getting repeatedly picked off multiple times. Now, for most fps players you're probably thinking "Well that doesn't seem like a bad problem as most shooters have very big sniper problems". Well the sniper problem tends to be a bit bigger in Robocraft due to the fact that the maps are very open, meaning there is less cover to hide behind. There is also a shortage of maps, as there are only 5 different maps to play on. The servers are also very buggy as you will most likely have to resolve crashes and restart your computer frequently.:Positive: The game allows much more freedom than most games as you are actually able to build your own tank rather than choose from a preexisting one. The game is great for creative people who also want some action out of their creations (for those of you that have played Minecraft and wanted to build a giant siege engine you know what I mean). The game is of course still free to play so if you are unsure you can easily download it,and create an online acount. For those of you that might not have internet I am afraid there is no way for you to experience this. Robocraft is a fun and enjoyable experience with a lot of big problems that may or may not be fixed.

This has got to be one of the most fun, most rewarding and entertaining experiences I have had in a game.
First I simply played the single-player and enjoyed it a lot, felt I received my moneys worth. But after playing a bit of coop with my sister I just felt inspired to get around and write a review.
So where to begin? Perhaps gameplay. It takes a gimmick, shooting portals to travel, manipulate stuff and ultimately solve puzzles. Portal 2 runs with the gimmick and, in true Valve-style, creates puzzles which feel more rewarding and organic than typical videogame puzzles, where it usually feels like you are trying to mind-read a cryptic all-powerful creature, a creature which tries its best to mask what it wants from you, which punishes every experimentation and failure harshly and without even giving you a clue of where you went wrong.
Instead, Portal does things like Half-Life 2 did (I touched upon it in my
), there´s more of a sense of observing, putting things together without too much arbitrary design choices and rules which never seem to stay consistent and trustworthy. Portal 1 and 2 has some arbitrary things like portals firing upon white surfaces, but it makes this clear and stick with this rule, it creates an environment where learning the rules is not useless, but you keep adding them up lawfully, like a scientist exploring how the game universe operates.

I got into Robocraft on a whim, expecting to try the free to play game, check it off the list, and be done with it.  Hours later I realized that it had me.  It's good.  Real good.  It carries the torch of Chromehounds from way back in the day.  It has more options for creative freedom though, and it only takes around 15 seconds to find a match.
You build a vehicle from Minecraft like blocks and add prefab pieces like weapons and wheels.  Each block has its own armor while each prefab piece is specific to its function.  Then you take the vehicle into team pvp battle.  Every block and prefab can be destroyed when it gets hit so you need to put thought into vehicles or you may find yourself without propulsion or weapons.
The types of vehicles that can be made are pretty extensive.  Wheels for rolling, wings and thrusters for flying, hoverpads for floating, spider legs for crawling up mountains, tank treads for steamrolling, and even sleds for rocketing along.  Or combine a couple to make flying spider tanks or a rocket racecar.
The devs add things to this game on a regular basis.  It's pretty cool to see the game grow as fast as it has been.    The only knock I have is that gameplay tweaks for balance take awhile to be addressed.  They've done a good job so far on that point, but it's taken awhile to get the balance to where it is now.

Welcome to the Portal 2 store page. You are about to purchase one of the most the best games that has, and probably will be made. Yes, the game is that good. Why, you ask? Well;
The story is well written and feels solid.  The pacing is perfect and manages to balance that fine line between delivering a consistently pleasing experience to you as the player but without leaving you feeling pressured or overloaded. The puzzles are challenging, but not mind-numbingly so; you will likely not be destroying your expensive hardware out of frustration at least.  The graphics are quite good and even though the game will be turning four years a few month's from now, Portal 2 is testament that Valve's source engine (which itself is growing quite long in the tooth) is still a force to be reckoned with. The sound design in this game, from the AI's comments to the  environmental sounds manage to create an atmosphere that feels truly amazing.
And Finally, what makes Portal 2... 'PORTAL 2!'  the enigma known  as GLaDOS. There really is nothing that could be said about this entity that hasn't been already; except for the simple fact that GLaDOS is a lot more human than AI. It's uncanny. And also, depending on how much you've heard/read about the game, creepy. And sad. Damn.
The only real downside to Portal 2 is that given Valve's history with the number 3, another masterpiece like this is unlikely to happen in the near future. It's a shame really.
Would I recommend this game to anyone? No. I would recommend it to everyone.

Robocraft is a Freemium, multiplayer-only, arena robot combat game.
This is a simple game that is easy to play, but hard to master.
It has very basic system requirements, so gamers running econo PCs with onboard graphics or older PCs can still enjoy decent framerates/gameplay.
Pros:
1. Simple to get started - use the preset vehicle or build your own quickly
2. Controls are very intuitive - only aircraft present control challenges
3. Matchmaking is usually fast, allowing 10-15 games in an hour!
4. Tech tier system prevents over and under matching in normal games
5. Laugh at your team mates' silly designs!
6. You can build complex machines that are devastatingly effective
7. You can also build simple but brutal machines that work just as well
8. Few cheaters. Played several hundred games and only noted 2 possible cheaters/hackers/glitchers
9. This game has "low violence", i.e., the graphical violence is at a fairly low level, and in my opinion, is ok for children 9+. Of course, parents shold exercise their OWN discretion. View the gameplay and decide for youself.
Cons:
1. Weapons need to be balanced better. Lower damage all round, and no one-shotting - this gets more apparent the higher level battles you fight. Currently, THERE IS NO WAY TO PREVENT ONE-SHOTTING IN THIS GAME.
2. The design garage could have "default craft" you could load up using default start equipment so u get involved faster - this is not for people who want to spend 2 hours getting a hovercraft right, its for people who want to spend 10 mins and get playing in sooner.
3. Needs more maps.
4. Needs more terain types. Example: water bodies can really allow hover machines to shine.
5. No falling or collision damage. In sandbox mode, sure. In ranked gameplay? Fighter planes crashing into the ground, tanks rolling off cliffs, all to avoid enemy fire. Seriously?
Overall: 7/10

Robocraft is definitely one of my favorite games on Steam. This game doesn't feel like it should be free, even with microtransactions. Robocraft will keep you playing for hours and hours. Reason being, is that this isn't the kind of game you get far into really quick and then it gets boring. It takes time to make progress into the game and even when you get far, it doesn't get boring. There is a microtransaction system with "Galaxy Cash" in which you could skip most of the  game, but it still doesn't feel like a pay to win game. Robocraft is still going to be updated a lot in the future, so when you get to the end-game point, there will still be features that will keep you playing.
Now I personally love this game because of it's endless possibilities. You start at tier 1 and make your way up to higher tiers. You create a robot (which can vary from a small harmless robot to an ultimate death machine), and by winning games with your robot you will earn robopoints and tech tokens. The better you do in a battle, the more tech tokens and robopoints you will achieve. With tech tokens, you unlock different parts for your robot such as guns, different forms of mobility, defense plates, chassis cubes, etc. With robopoints you can buy the robot parts that you unlock. Each part you put on your robot has a "robot ranking" and with a higher robot ranking you can unlock the next tier, where you will be put into battles with other robots of that tier. With each tier you can unlock new robot parts with that tier's tech tokens. Different parts have different amounts of CPU. If you use up too much CPU you will run out and have to take off certain parts for more CPU. When you do good in a battles you will level up (and I don't mean that each time you do good in a battle you will instantly level up). When you level up you will earn more maximum CPU, so you wont really get stuck at part in the game. So as you do this, you reach higher and higher tiers, making your way up in the game.
My only cons are that there need to be more gamemodes (which they already plan to add), more maps, and some game balancing changes, which they have been doing lately, so most of that will be fixed/added. Also, from time to time servers will go down, and you'll have to wait a while to get in a game sometimes, but they've done things to fix this too.
Now remember, this game is FREE, so I suggest just getting Robocraft now if you haven't already. Robocraft is a great game for people who like Team Fortress 2.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Welcome to the Portal 2 store page. You are about to purchase one of the most the best games that has, and probably will be made. Yes, the game is that good. Why, you ask? Well;
The story is well written and feels solid.  The pacing is perfect and manages to balance that fine line between delivering a consistently pleasing experience to you as the player but without leaving you feeling pressured or overloaded. The puzzles are challenging, but not mind-numbingly so; you will likely not be destroying your expensive hardware out of frustration at least.  The graphics are quite good and even though the game will be turning four years a few month's from now, Portal 2 is testament that Valve's source engine (which itself is growing quite long in the tooth) is still a force to be reckoned with. The sound design in this game, from the AI's comments to the  environmental sounds manage to create an atmosphere that feels truly amazing.
And Finally, what makes Portal 2... 'PORTAL 2!'  the enigma known  as GLaDOS. There really is nothing that could be said about this entity that hasn't been already; except for the simple fact that GLaDOS is a lot more human than AI. It's uncanny. And also, depending on how much you've heard/read about the game, creepy. And sad. Damn.
The only real downside to Portal 2 is that given Valve's history with the number 3, another masterpiece like this is unlikely to happen in the near future. It's a shame really.

First off I would say Portal was not a bad game.  But Steam only has recommend and not recommend and I can't honestly say I would tell anyone who hasn't played it that they should.
Single Player Gameplay - Puzzles were fun, if not really challenging.  A couple of achievements like Overclocker and Smash TV were good at adding additional challenges.  And of course there are many mods (which I look forward to trying some of).  The gels and gravity-tube things blended in well with the puzzles without overwhelming the fact that portals were core of each puzzle.
Story - I was pretty unimpressed with the story to be honest.  What I liked about Portal was the creeping dread, the growing sense of unease.  And when I watched it played again I saw lovely foreshadowing I had missed.  Portal 2 had none of that, there was all the subtlety of a Michael Bay film.  Without spoilers I'll say there is a part where a character is supposed to parodying the foreshadowed threats of the first game, but the whole game had been so heavy handed that it just highlighted how short it fell of it's predecessor.  Each 'twist' was so obvious my cat got it beforehand.   Each 'joke' was hammered in relentlessly... hahaha she's an orphan. hahaha...she's fat (a joke they just would not let go of), it got real old, real fast.  The stark minimalism of the first game was lost in a rash of babbling voices, there was too many voices, talking at you too often so you never got the clinical isolation of the first.  Also, I found Wheatley very unfunny, perhaps it's because a 'British accent' (whatever that is) doesn't automatically make me laugh.  It was the tiny touches I cherished, the weird turret that talked about Prometheus (creepy), the hideous brownish-orange colour that so taints the legacy of the 1970's (also creepy).  But too much was lost in noisy set-pieces and ham-fisted narration.
Co-op - Haven't played co-op yet on this account but did some on a friends console and had a lot of fun.  It is the aspect which coupled with mods (modding in general is the greatest thing ever in my opinion and why many RPGs are best played on PC) that I expect to get most pleasure from playing Portal 2.
So overall, it was fine, just fine.  If there was a 'meh' button with thumb neither up nor down I'd go for that but there is not.  6.5/10

contributing to your win in the matches are also the configuration of your machines. you must understand what kinds of objectives that youd want to achieve with them. you must know what works best on your style of play. some like to stay behind the lines, some like to bring the fight to their enemies, some would not even like to fight at all and support their teammates. so, before you build something, ask yourself; what are you building for?
to those who think this is another pay2win game, this game is definitely NOT one of them. the only reason you should buy in-game cash is if you want accessories or custom guns on your machines, supporting the awesome devs, or to buy premium time for those who dont like grinding(unless you know how, its kinda grindy). there is no possibility that the players who pay is more powerful than the players who didn't, so really, there is no force in buying the game credits.

Robocraft has had a very uneven experience during it's time on Steam. The developers have no clear direction for where they want to go, meaning the experience is both inconsistent and unintuitive. Systems change quarterly, with major features being announced then scrapped, or implemented and then removed within six to eight months. Massive balance changes are forced on the community for the sake of player retention, then are often rolled back after the results prove disastrous. Matchmaking and competitive play are almost nonexistent, and the skill level of the average playerbase ranges from mediocre to downright appalling, much of which is due to the total lack of documentation and tutorial material from the developers, as well as the ignorance and arrogance of the mostly clueless players. If you're looking for a game with consistency and intuitive design supported by a friendly and proactive community, keep looking. Robocraft clearly is not it.
Toxic community and inconsistent development direction aside, the game is built around one of the most intriguing concepts available in the competitive gaming community, that being the ability to design, engineer, and iterate on the design of a combat robot. Despite the often frustrating circumstances in which it's delivered, the core of Robocraft is an immensely satisfying one. Components are varied and offer an unexpected degree of complexity, creating a deep building experience for those looking for it. By nature such a system lends itself to a few optimal designs, but given Robocraft's changeable nature, the designs that end up being optimized often fall out of favor, forcing players to search for new, more viable designs. For those looking for a solid engineering challenge that is in a constant state of change, this is an excellent opportunity to engage in creative design and problem solving.
