Robocraft has had a very uneven experience during it's time on Steam. The developers have no clear direction for where they want to go, meaning the experience is both inconsistent and unintuitive. Systems change quarterly, with major features being announced then scrapped, or implemented and then removed within six to eight months. Massive balance changes are forced on the community for the sake of player retention, then are often rolled back after the results prove disastrous. Matchmaking and competitive play are almost nonexistent, and the skill level of the average playerbase ranges from mediocre to downright appalling, much of which is due to the total lack of documentation and tutorial material from the developers, as well as the ignorance and arrogance of the mostly clueless players. If you're looking for a game with consistency and intuitive design supported by a friendly and proactive community, keep looking. Robocraft clearly is not it.
Toxic community and inconsistent development direction aside, the game is built around one of the most intriguing concepts available in the competitive gaming community, that being the ability to design, engineer, and iterate on the design of a combat robot. Despite the often frustrating circumstances in which it's delivered, the core of Robocraft is an immensely satisfying one. Components are varied and offer an unexpected degree of complexity, creating a deep building experience for those looking for it. By nature such a system lends itself to a few optimal designs, but given Robocraft's changeable nature, the designs that end up being optimized often fall out of favor, forcing players to search for new, more viable designs. For those looking for a solid engineering challenge that is in a constant state of change, this is an excellent opportunity to engage in creative design and problem solving.

Portal 2 is everything the original was, just more of it. The game mechanics and graphics haven't noticeably changed (nor did they need to) and the storyline picks up more or less from where it left off. But with more ways to solve new puzzles, more AIs to contend with, and more areas to explore, the very simple goal of the game - getting to the exit with portals - doesn't get stale. The game goes about tying up loose ends while providing new tidbits to speculate over, none of which feel like cliffhangers. Co-op has been added both gracefully and quite cleverly. The co-op courses expand the storyline and the partners are given an effective shorthand to communicate with, meaning the chat function is only used in extreme cases. Put simply, Portal 2 really is everything the first was, a solidly great, immersive puzzle platformer, with a bit more of everything.

Right off the bat I'm going to say this- I did not enjoy this game, but I can see why some people might, My reasons will come later.
In short, Portal as a whole is a fun physics puzzle game that will never have anther sequel so long as Valve owns the IP because Valve doesn't believe in the existence of 3, but for what it's worth, it's a nice installment.
In Portal 2; Wheatly, a new robot, tries to get you out of aperture labs as everythings gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥since Chell (you) was (were) in stasis. This accidently revives GLaDOS from the last game and you then are forced to do tests and what not same as the first. Nothing wrong with these tests, my major gripe comes from when wheatly takes over GLaDOS' body and sends you deep underground to the old aperture labs. One can quickly notice a distinct lack of portalable surfaces, which only become more and more scarce. It quickly becomes ridiculously difficult to find the one portal-able surface in an otherwise empty room in order to progress. This not only killed all game flow but made the game tedious.
I'd normally have more to say, but I quit this game very early on because it was so boring that not even the briliant writing could salvage the game.
But- the actual tests are fun, introducing the new goo element to the gameplay, which give you abilities such as running faster or bouncing up in the air. This opens up an entire world of possibilities that I unfortunately can't be bothered to explore further. There is also co-op which cuts out the parts I disliked in the story and instead connects lab tests in a hub-world. These tests are fun and challenging because they utilize the 4-porta mechnic introduced with the addition of your co-op portal gun which can shoot purple and red (IIRC) portals.
Disliked the story, loved the co-op puzzles, although they also suffered a bit from "Where the hell is the one surface I can put a portal on" -itis at times, nowhere near t the extend of the single player and it never really made the expirience unenjoyable.
Play for the co-op, not the story.
7 /10

Wow, where do I begin with this game? Valve took the simple game of Portal, and created an ENORMOUS universe full of fun, secrets, lore, amazing characters, great gameplay, and of course puzzle perplexing portal action. The art design is remeniscient of the first game, and still manages to add both a 50's esque design, and an even late future layout. With the edition of our lovable friend Wheatley, and the return of our all time greatest enemy the "Genetic Life and Disk Operating System" or GLaDOS, you know this can't go wrong. Portal 2 completely redefines the genre of puzzle game by adding a memorable plot as well as an even more memorable array of tests and puzzles littered throughout "Aperture Science". I give this game all five stars for its ingenuity and creativity in both level design, playthrough, and final execution. I reccomend this game for all people, first person shooter fans, puzzle gamers, and even people who just want a good laugh. Portal 2 has really changed the way I think about Valve and their abilities and I look forward to viewing their other games soon.

Right off the bat I'm going to say this- I did not enjoy this game, but I can see why some people might, My reasons will come later.
In short, Portal as a whole is a fun physics puzzle game that will never have anther sequel so long as Valve owns the IP because Valve doesn't believe in the existence of 3, but for what it's worth, it's a nice installment.
In Portal 2; Wheatly, a new robot, tries to get you out of aperture labs as everythings gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥since Chell (you) was (were) in stasis. This accidently revives GLaDOS from the last game and you then are forced to do tests and what not same as the first. Nothing wrong with these tests, my major gripe comes from when wheatly takes over GLaDOS' body and sends you deep underground to the old aperture labs. One can quickly notice a distinct lack of portalable surfaces, which only become more and more scarce. It quickly becomes ridiculously difficult to find the one portal-able surface in an otherwise empty room in order to progress. This not only killed all game flow but made the game tedious.
I'd normally have more to say, but I quit this game very early on because it was so boring that not even the briliant writing could salvage the game.
But- the actual tests are fun, introducing the new goo element to the gameplay, which give you abilities such as running faster or bouncing up in the air. This opens up an entire world of possibilities that I unfortunately can't be bothered to explore further. There is also co-op which cuts out the parts I disliked in the story and instead connects lab tests in a hub-world. These tests are fun and challenging because they utilize the 4-porta mechnic introduced with the addition of your co-op portal gun which can shoot purple and red (IIRC) portals.
Disliked the story, loved the co-op puzzles, although they also suffered a bit from "Where the hell is the one surface I can put a portal on" -itis at times, nowhere near t the extend of the single player and it never really made the expirience unenjoyable.
Play for the co-op, not the story.

Hello there,
for my first review I decided talk more about Portal 2. Original intention was to play it with my friend, but after completing a few rooms I began to love this game and went to explore it alone during my free time.
Now, this game has a tag of "puzzle" on itself, but it wasn't really hard for me. Actually, almost every challenge is completed under the same pattern or, let us say, a way of thinking. Thus sometimes it can get monotonical. Nevertheless, the puzzles are really original, interesting to play in and sometimes even surprising. The other content is unique, the atmosphere is fascinating, great job with the soundtrack.
Basically, you'll get an approximately 7 hour journey in a huge factory/laboratory that is filled with good/interesting/funny stuff that can be found all around. The only drawback I found was the lack of a choice in this game. For example there could me more ways to complete levels (though I admit that this could make the game even more easy). Or, what would be more interesting, there could a few alternative endings to the game. Or paths leading to the same ending. But this does not make the experience any worse.
Verdict: interesting/unique/intrigueging/easy/a bit too short for it's price tag.
Buy this game of you like linear (but interesting) games with funny/sarcastical plot features.

What do you get when you combine the Building aspects of Minecraft and the Arena and Fun of World of Tanks?
Robocraft.
Build a bot, go into the arena and have fun destroying your enemies. Best part of this game is the simplicity of the roles you can play (at least the ones I've seen):
Bomber: Flying bot with plasma cannons that rain down hell on enemies
Medic: Heal your allies AND damage your enemies
Interceptor: Bombers worst nightmares
Snipers: You know how they work
There are probably more but thats the most common I've seen. Anyway, there are even different types of transport/movement in the game:
Walkers: Jump, Climb walls and even hang from ceilings.
Wheels
Hovers: Able to adjust a certain amount of height to fit their needs. They can even climb some walls if you build it right.
Tank Treads: For those of us who like making tanks
Rotar Blades: Helicopters!
Wings: Fly like an eagle!
This game also has the best devs! At random times you will either be awarded Premium time or be given codes to get premium time! For those who are going, "Great, its got a Premium option, must be some kind of pay 2 win system." NOPE! It all comes down to skill and building talent!
You losing too much HP? Add more shields! Not enough damage? MOAR GUNS! Flying awkward? Reposition the flying parts or move some stuff around!
If you like building and fighting and having a good time, come play Robocraft!

Hello there,
for my first review I decided talk more about Portal 2. Original intention was to play it with my friend, but after completing a few rooms I began to love this game and went to explore it alone during my free time.
Now, this game has a tag of "puzzle" on itself, but it wasn't really hard for me. Actually, almost every challenge is completed under the same pattern or, let us say, a way of thinking. Thus sometimes it can get monotonical. Nevertheless, the puzzles are really original, interesting to play in and sometimes even surprising. The other content is unique, the atmosphere is fascinating, great job with the soundtrack.
Basically, you'll get an approximately 7 hour journey in a huge factory/laboratory that is filled with good/interesting/funny stuff that can be found all around. The only drawback I found was the lack of a choice in this game. For example there could me more ways to complete levels (though I admit that this could make the game even more easy). Or, what would be more interesting, there could a few alternative endings to the game. Or paths leading to the same ending. But this does not make the experience any worse.
Verdict: interesting/unique/intrigueging/easy/a bit too short for it's price tag.
Buy this game of you like linear (but interesting) games with funny/sarcastical plot features.

I find so hard to believe how *well made* this game is. I passed Portal three times (but I've got a total of 9hrs, not much at all)  and thoroughly enjoyed it; mostly because it's inside the Half-Life universe. I had been wanting to play Portal 2 for a very long time because of it, since the first game was so original and well thought-out. I actually memorised most of the Portal levels and tricks, so I thought Portal 2 wouldn't be a huge challenge, and that it'd be easier. I thought it wouldn't make me think as much as the first game, I was sure of it. And I was wrong.
Valve has crafted something astounding with Portal 2. There were about four chambers in which I was so frustrated I just wanted to rip the hair off my skull. The game forced me to think and puzzled me a great deal. When I wasn't stressing myself, shooting portals all over the map and jumping to my death in exasperation every ten seconds, I was astounded and unable to believe how incredibly well made the maps are and how well executed the chambers are. Portal isn't my favourite Valve game, subjectively to me it isn't the best. But objectively, I have to say Portal is Valve's best creation. They have crafted something special in this game, three influential factors (two which I'll count as one): Humour, tragedy/darkness and originality.
The first factor is evident. Cave Johnson and his speeches are hilarious. GlaDOS is a ♥♥♥♥♥, and yet her intended-to-be-hurtful comments are hilarious and found a way to make me gasp in both surprise and humour. The long-fall boots, turret trailer and the Portal Valentine's Day video are hilarious to say the very least (and freaking original!).
The second factor is well covered up by the first factor, but it is still there nevertheless. Portal has a tragic story: that is undeniable. Aperture Laboratories has a tragic, screwed-up background. Test subjects were treated like dirt, the scientists didn't care an iota about their welfare and Cave Johnson didn't even try to hide his contempt towards them. That's why it's screwed-up, but it's tragic because it's an abandoned facility which used to be one of the greatest science companies of all time (even though they had their fair share of controversies) and it wasn't abandoned because of its bankrupcy, or because they ran out of ideas/products. It's because everyone was murdered, dammit! Every single scientist we know of, except Rattman, is dead and just when Aperture had its most promising project under its sleeve. Not a single soul is seen in Aperture; death is such a strong essence in Portal but the tragedy is well masqueraded by the undeniable humour.
The third and last factor is the most astonishing one: ORIGINALITY. The test chambers, the idea of the game, the execution of physics in the game to make a realistic notion out of the puzzle-solving with the Handheld Portal Device; as bizarre as the idea of a gun which shoots portals in plain surfaces sounds, Valve found a way to make it seem both believable and realistic. Both with the execution of physics in the game and with the explanation of the gun itself. It's incredible.
These three factors, but the last one specially, is why I consider Portal is the best game Valve has ever made, and why I consider it to be one of the most amazing games to *ever* be created. I recommend it to *everyone*.

I have almost absolutely nothing but high praise for this title and the developers.
First of all, the Early Access tag is certainly warranted - there's some serious bugs but nothing exploitable.  For example, if you don't have the best internet connection, a sudden spike in your latency basically kicks you out of the game and forces you to manually quit the application, which is annoying.  Luckily you will still get money and tech points when you log back in if your team won, so that's almost okay.
This game is Free To Play in the best way possible.  Microtransactions might allow you to play higher tiers faster, but they don't give you an edge - there's no "gold equipment" or anything of the sort.  You can buy Premium to double (yes, double) your rate of experience, money and tech point gain at the price of about $5.50 a month, which is a bargain compared to most F2P titles.  Tiers play against their own and sometimes in "Challenge" matches in which four players of a high tier fight ten of a lower tier.  At first, these are frustrating, but they become fun and rewarding by the time you reach T5 or 6.
As for the gameplay mechanics, the tier system is phenomenal.  You'll spend your first week or two grinding up through tiers, upgrading your tank/flyer/car/whatever and gradually getting into more complex fights.  But the best part is that Tier 10 and TX (Megabot) are not the "end game" by any means, because at that point you'll probably engineer a high performance craft for a low tier, and this is where the design portion becomes truly rewarding.  You'll spend hours in the lab squeezing every Ranking point possible to stay in Tier 5, right on the edge of Tier 6.
The design choices you'll make are extremely varied and promote the replay value.  Right now there's five different weapons, seven or eight movement systems, electronics upgrades, shielding plates and armor blocks that can be arranged together in a myriad of ways.  Walker/copters are as common as the straight-up artillery tank.  Rain death from a flying fortress or zip around in a rocket sled.  Balance your armor/shield, weapons and speed to suit your tastes.  There isn't a "meta" that makes or breaks games - everything can conceivably be countered in a variety of ways, which makes Robocraft less about how much time you pour into your design and more about how much practice you have in using it.
Aside from the previously mentioned bugs that will occasionally force me to quit in frustration, I've very much enjoyed my first 38 hours playing this game and will definitely enjoy the next 38 hours.  Give it a shot - it's free!

As I have previously stated, I recently received a new desktop computer. This computer, the ASUS ROG G20, is optimized for computer gaming. Naturally, I took this as an invitation to play every game I can find, and I am. I have discovered an interesting game called Robocraft. This game is free to play, and available on Steam, thanks Valve, we love you. I have put almost 48 hours of gameplay into it for the first two weeks I've had it, and I must say, it's pretty fun. In Robocraft, you get to design and build a robot, complete with guns and other neat items, and then take it to the battlefield. Here you get to fight real people, playing with robots they built themselves. You can use your ship in one of three ways: on a practice field, where you get to see how well if moves and fires; in a normal battle, where its pits you and eleven other random people against a group of twelve; or a challenge battle, in which you and eleven others fight a group of four from a higher tier.
The point of every battle is the same each time; you have to either kill all of the enemy ships or take over the enemy base. You can take their base by resting on it without conflict, as they can to you. The best strategy, I have discovered, is to have six players rest on your base, while six other players head to the enemies' base. By doing this, you can keep a well powered guard at base to defend it, and a small group to attempt theft of the enemy base. The only problem with this is that many players will often branch off and do their own thing without even consulting the group.
The coolest part about this game, and the reason I keep playing it, is the variety. In Robocraft, a player can build several types of vehicles ranging from Rail Tanks-which is practically a tank with a sniper rifle attached- to SMG Flyers-airplanes with machine guns. You can mix any weapon with any vehicle as long as you have the money to build it, and the possible designs are endless! I am currently trying to master the construction of a Plasma Flyer. This airplane is equipped with five T4 plasma cannons that all fire at once, dealing massive amounts of damage. This doesn't make me unstoppable though.
The game is balanced by tier level. For example, a Tier 5 ship will never fight a Tier one ship because his vehicle will be way too overpowered (OP). Even when I enter a battle with other Tier 4 ships, I cannot dominate because, even though I have amazing guns, my armor level is really weak. This means that I can deal incredible amounts of damage to any vehicle, but any other vehicle can kill me in just a couple shots. A tank vehicle is very common for stealing a base, as they can't deal very much damage, but they can’t take many hits without receiving it either. This system helps it so that no one player can destroy the competition and be unchallenged. Even the best players have a loss every now and again, because they are not the only player fighting for their team. If their entire team was destroyed and they were left alive, then the enemy team could gang him and destroy him, claiming victory.
So, I give Robocraft a 10/10 for all around amazing game. This game is fun, creative, fair, and affordable. This is definitely one of my favorite games and I cannot wait to get back to it tonight! На мой, может и любительский взгляд, Portal - одна из наиболее интересных игр от Valve. Очень редко от вышеназванных разработчиков можно встретить подобного жанра игру. Вы же понимаете, что я имею ввиду, что классика Valve, такая как Left 4 Dead, Counter-Strike, Half-Life вплотную приближена к оружию, убийству и монстрам. Но не Portal. За всю игру, теоретически, от ваших рук не погибнет ни одно живое существо. Даже не разу не промелькнет и капелька крови (если не учитывать вылетающие из вас брызги при попадании из турели). Правда необычно?
Пусть в нашем арсенале лишь одно оружие (и то оно делает дырки в пространстве, а не во врагах), но это не мешает в полной мере наслаждаться красивым и захватывающим геймплеем. Ведь все дело в том, что игра опирается не на бессмысленную резню "один против тысячи", а на то, насколько хорошо работает ваша логика.
А так же отдельная похвала за возможность прохождения совместных миссий с другом. Сложные задачи удобнее решать с напарником, но возникает дух конкуренции...
В целом остается сказать, что игра не заслуживает никакой другой оценки, кроме как 10 из 10. Идеальная возможность потренировать мозг. Спасибо большое.

This game is a huge amount of fun.  Building yourself a vehicle is way more intersting than it should be and disassembling the enemy as you damage them adds a surprising amount of visceral reward for getting in a good hit.
This is a free game, so there is a premium currency, but there are no "premium-only" weapons or armor and it is completely unnecessary to easily unlock all available items.  The first couple of tech levels have limited mobility/weapon selections (wheels and smgs) to encourage you to familiarize yourself with the game, but it is very possible (from experience) to get past this within an hour or two of unpaid gameplay.  You may even find that you enjoy the setup and keep using upgraded versions in later tiers!
Matchmaking is divided into tiers based on "value" of the blocks used, so while it is possible to build a twink lower-tier robot, the exponentially higher values of higher tier weapons and armor keep any round from becoming unbalanced.
There is a physics engine, so airplanes have to actually be balanced and heavy ground bots will trundle along slowly under the weight of their weapons and armor.  If you ever decide you're not enjoying your current playstyle, changing to a different setup is as easy as building a different robot.
I would really encourage anyone to give this game a try.

The game is supposedly to build and fight with a robot.  However, game design decisions (limited electroplate shapes, an upcoming change to armored chassis cubes granting certain shapes higher durability than others) push players towards building cookie cutter designs.  Balance nerfing (increasing weight of electroplates and destabilizing thrusters among others) make player choice less meaningful.  Although some balance nerfing is to be expected, it has been in my opinion too much.
What players are left with is the tedium of grinding for RP to purchase parts for cookie cutter designs, without creative or artistic freedom.  Even future planned features disclosed by the designers and programmers do not address this fundamental issue.
Robocraft doesn't match other shooters that have superior graphics, better communication, and most importantly, significantly added tactical options.  Robocraft doesn't match other building games, as other building games typically do not have construction rules that effectively strangle creative and artistic freedoms.
Though this game is still in alpha, I do not see these trends changing, and must give the game a negative review at this time.

This is my Review for the game, Portal 2. This may be a long one so enjoy.
Portal 2 is a Portal Puzzle Game, Taken place in the Mysterious Aperture Science Laboratories.
You play as a Character called 'Chell'. This game is taken place after the events of 'Portal' Which I seriously recommend playing before this. This game features a very lengthy Single Player which Personally took me about 3 days to complete. The game also features a Co-Op Mode where you play as two Experimental Robots named as: P-Body and Atlas.
The game does have Steam Workshop Integration also and an In-Game Editor. Hours of Fun!
!Spoiler Warning!
You wake up in a little room and the Announcer tells you some 'Important' Information and teaches you how to play the game. You then go back to sleep and is woken up later by someone 'knocking on the door'. You walk to the door and a little Personality Core enters on a Management Rail.
Pros and Cons.
Pros
•Very Lengthy Story.
•Very Enjoyable for all ages.
•Very Easy to Learn.
•Very Nice Control System.
•Co-Op Mode.
•Steam Workshop Integration.
•Runs Really Smooth
•You get attached to the Characters
Cons
•A few gamebreaking bugs I personally have come across.
•Texture Glitches from time to time.
•Very Laggy Movement sometimes.
•Very Short Co-Op Mode I could complete in under a day.
At the end of all of this, I recommend this game if you've played the Original Game, If you havn't. Buy them both!

Robocraft is basically a build-your-own vehicle combat game. Overall, it's simple, fun, and surprisingly satisfying. Combat is usually thrilling, and there's a feeling of satisfaction when destroying an enemy.
Mechanically, the game is solid - vehicles handle well, whether they're ground, hover, or flying. Guns feel fairly balanced as well. Progression is a bit slow (if you're f2p) and grindy, however the combat is fun, matches go quickly, and queue times are fast - you probably won't find yourself bored.
The micro-transaction system for the game is, quite honestly, the best I think I've encountered. Nothing you can buy with actual cash can't be earned in the game, unless it's simply cosmetic. Cash only seems to effect your rate of progression through the game. Not Pay2Win by any means. Also, and more importantly, the prices are very, very fair. And truthfully, it's a good enough game that it's worth dropping a few bucks on just to help support it.
The only downside to the game is a mild lack of variety. Some more weapon types and especially game modes would be nice, but, as it currently stands, there's enough that it doesn't feel stale. Maybe just a little lacking.
Overall, a fun, simple, and fair f2p game. Worth checking out.

So I wandered across Robocraft at about midnight last night, read a whole bunch of great reviews and figured hey, its free right so if it sucks, no loss.
The sun has risen now, birds are chirping in the trees and I keep telling myself I'll get to bed soon, just one more battle.

The free to play element is exactly that, no need to shell out cash to buy gear, you earn enough and earn it quickly, to keep up to speed and even though battles are pretty short lived in the beginning (very much a case of "hey, why am I upside down? is that a chopper in the sky? oh, I'm dead!") you still get some in-game currency even if you get obliterated, which happens often to me (but maybe I'm just rubbish).
I highly recoomend this to anyone, but be warned, it will suck hours off your life!
In summary
Pros
- free to play (and win)
- easy controls
- build robots
- destroy other robots
- unlock massive amounts of tech
- build better robots
- get revenge!
Cons
- sleep deprivation

Robocraft does what it does very well.
Build:
Player's robots are all different (apart from a very few bought robots piloted by new players), no matter how common certain categories of design are. There's much enjoyment to be had in trying to create something different and/or optimising for battle. Trying to balance fliers and in particular rocket and helium drones is particularly interesting.
Fight:
At the moment the game is pretty well balanced*..except for being able to fly with far too much mass and rotor blades being far too tough. Compared to team shooters in general, combat is a sluggish and awkward affair. I do wish the fastest useful bots one could design were much faster. The effective skill ceiling is relatively low. Teamwork and tactics are above all else what win and lose games in this title.
*The relative strength of various weapons and items varies from tier to tier, however. I think this is both a positive and a negative. While certain weapons are obnoxious in certain tier brackets, it's nice to see a change of meta in both weapon selection and behavior as you change tiers.
Free to Play:
Robocraft does break one cardinal F2P rule as far as I'm concerned: one cannot aquire everything in the game without paying. However, it is only cosmetic items, garages, and speedometers and altimeters that require fun bucks. It's reasonable. The grind to get from tier to tier is rather insufferable in my opinion, but with the game itself being enjoyable, that burden is lessened somewhat.

Robocraft is an amazing mix of Minecraft, World of Tanks, and Batlebots. Play against (and with!) thousands of other players worldwide in an friendly online MMO enviroment with great visuals and even better phyisics! Go up against limitless amounts of different designs and many different strategies on all kinds of terrain! Build a robot out of your own imagination! Equip it with Electroplates, Plazma Launchers, Railguns, WIngs, Tesla Blades, Walker Legs, Thrusters, and more! Grab some frends in a platoon! All of these features AND MANY MANY MANY MORE await you in this Free-to-Play and Free-to-Win Game!
Overall, a nice game that has many features and constant updates, Robocraft stands out as an amazing expirience with many weeks of play to offer and barely any complaints from it all. It doesnt suffer from the "Best Robot Design" problem nearly at all and you can get every funtional component with a Free-to-Play account! Some cubes can only be bought with real money, but those components are merely cosmetic and give you no advantage in battle, only a bit of flair! :D One of the cons to this game are its servers, which clog up sometimes, but the devs fix these issues very quickly and often give away free preimium to conpensate for lost time. Another one of the cons are that you are fairly restrained by your CPU (how big your robot can get) and geting more is a task only accomlished with time, which can get somewhat grindy. This is already mostly not a problem though, as every game is vastly different and thus repetivity is almost non-existant. The last con is that higher teir and higher level players often build robots that "count" as a lower tier robot but have much higher teir weapons and/or have insane ammounts of armor. These robots can often instakill enemies and are a general pain. This problem is also somewhat null though, as the robots with overtiered guns are usualy small and die in 3 or 4 hits from normal weponry. Compared to other, simmilar titles like Gear Up and Guns and Robots, Robocraft Features a Free-to Win model with very balanced gamplay and very generous and community- minded developers, as well as a safe and fun enviroment all around.
In Summary, A GREAT game with GREAT balance and a GREAT community with GREAT devs.

Edit: most of this review still holds true, but now that I've gotten over my first impression, I need to change my recommendation to a negative. Building bots is fun and rewarding. Playing with the brainless twits who infest this game and seem to have no understanding of the most basic forms of tactics or strategy whatsoever is not. It's a frustrating experience that turns 90% of the games you'll play into a rage-inducing nightmare. It will depress you that so much of humanity is so stupid that complicated ideas like "take cover behind that rock so you don't get instantly murdered" is beyond their limited brain capacity. The game is still free, and you won't lose much by playing it, but do so at your own risk of becoming depressed.
I look at Early Access with nothing but suspicion and disdain, after getting burned by so SO many of them turning out to be, essentially, scams to take in the impatient.
But Robocraft's free to play, and it follows the Warframe philosophy of F2P. There's no pay to win, just pay-for-cosmetics and 2x exp/money booster pack types of things. You can also buy a very limited selection of prefabricated bots, which unlocks the tech tree in the spots you'd be using with those advanced bots, but that gives you no advantage at all.
It feels exactly like World of Tanks. I wouldn't be surprised if the same people worked on that game. Except, unlike World of Tank, you build your bots yourself from the ground up using a large variety of blocks. Stronger and stronger armor, lighter-than-air blocks to make you float or right yourself if you go off a cliff, sled skis, wheels, hover blades, helicopter blades, thrusters, rudders, wins, tank treads, spider legs... and that's just for movement. There's also about 5 weapon types, shield configurations, and radar equipment like jammers or receivers, and you're limited only by what you want to make:
Spider legs on an airplane so you can climb up a mountain and fly off? Sure!
Sled skis under a hovercraft so you can get really low to the ground and glide directly on the ground? Why not?
Wheels on your helicopter, thruster jets on your tank, immobile gunboxes that sit there and hopefully shoot first, you get to make your own vehicle.
There are still cheaters around; it's not rare to see a railgun user aim at you through cover from impossibly far across the map when he couldn't see you if you were lit up like a disco ball. Some of them even shoot you through mountains. Hopefully they get banned, or murdered in their sleep, whichever comes first.
There's literally no reason not to try this game, except if you pay for your downloads by the byte, in which case why are you even reading this? Every letter is costing you money stop.
It's early access, and no-one should ever buy anything that is early access, ever, under any circumstance, for any reason. But this one's free. Just download it and try it, already. It's fun, and if it isn't your thing, you've lost nothing.

Robocraft, Well the name is pretty self explanitory, you build robots, Tanks, Flyers, walkers, combinations of all the above, your imagination is the limit.
I've played over 217 hours before writing this review, and honestly I can find no fault with the game, yes there are some cons, and I'll list those in a bit, but for the most part this game is definitely top notch especially for an alpha.
With that said:
Pros:
~ Build your own comabt mechs (Even Healers).
~ Balance is good, their are no unfair combinations, the CPU requires you to sacrifice tank for damage and vice versa is different amounts depending on your desires. You can basically tweak your bot to do whatever you want.
~ Balanced Leveling system - Levels are aquired through kills, Heals, and Damage, The tech path determs which rank your bot fights in, the higher the rank of your bot the better gear you can get. You get higher ranks by equiping better gear you can unlock from the tech tree with token you earn from combat.
~ Balanced Matchmaking - Tech Tiers are seperated by your robots ranking, So you'll never face a robot that completely dominates you because of gear or parts (Unless you do a challenge battle which reward a TON of money and tech points).
~ Plenty of different game Modes, (With more to be added from what I hear).
1. Chalenge Mode - A mode where 4 Higher tier bots face off against 10 Lower tier bots, the tiers are usually 2-4 apart. A Challenge, but not impossible to win on either side.
2. Mega Bot - 1 Huge, High damage Player Bot vs 10 Other Players.
3. Normal and Ranked - Normal matches with Occasional high reward ranked matches.
4. More on the way.
~ The tech tree - Plenty of Options,
1. Weapons - Plasma Cannons (Artillary), SMGs (Pulse Lasers), Rails (Snipers), Disrupters (Dammage Over Time and Heal Over Time).
2. Armor - Too many to list, Lets just say you have  tons of options in armor types, including plateing which can give your bot cool looks as well as shields.
3. Miscilanious stuff, like thrusters, wings, radars, jammers, all kinds of stuff.
There are literally 100's of items, and infinite combinations for Bots.
~ F2P - The only thing you can buy are premade Bots (Nothing over Rank 7), and Premium (Which basically is like a sub that gives you 100% bonus to earned RP (Money) and Tech points, which in Moeny is less then 10$ a moth (It's actually like 6.45$ or something for 30 days of premium).
Con's:
Honestly I had to rack my brain to figure out what to put here. But I would say perhaps some PVE could be added, maybe a story line, Open world, and some other stuff.
I can't honestly think of anything negative to say about the game. and haveing played it for over 200 Hours I have encounted 0 issues (even though it's in alpha) I mean yea theres the occasional (And I mean only like once or twice a day occasional) DC, Bug, and Server instability, but I don't really count that as a "Con", with it being an Alpha, I count it as "Expected".
I would 100% recomend this game to anyone who loves creating their own stuff from nothing,a nd useing it to fight other people in matches. So if your creative, Intelligent, and enjoy the ability to mold your fighting machine to your standards, and your designs (Entirely with very little limitations). This is the game for you.

Edit: most of this review still holds true, but now that I've gotten over my first impression, I need to change my recommendation to a negative. Building bots is fun and rewarding. Playing with the brainless twits who infest this game and seem to have no understanding of the most basic forms of tactics or strategy whatsoever is not. It's a frustrating experience that turns 90% of the games you'll play into a rage-inducing nightmare. It will depress you that so much of humanity is so stupid that complicated ideas like "take cover behind that rock so you don't get instantly murdered" is beyond their limited brain capacity. The game is still free, and you won't lose much by playing it, but do so at your own risk of becoming depressed.
I look at Early Access with nothing but suspicion and disdain, after getting burned by so SO many of them turning out to be, essentially, scams to take in the impatient.
But Robocraft's free to play, and it follows the Warframe philosophy of F2P. There's no pay to win, just pay-for-cosmetics and 2x exp/money booster pack types of things. You can also buy a very limited selection of prefabricated bots, which unlocks the tech tree in the spots you'd be using with those advanced bots, but that gives you no advantage at all.
It feels exactly like World of Tanks. I wouldn't be surprised if the same people worked on that game. Except, unlike World of Tank, you build your bots yourself from the ground up using a large variety of blocks. Stronger and stronger armor, lighter-than-air blocks to make you float or right yourself if you go off a cliff, sled skis, wheels, hover blades, helicopter blades, thrusters, rudders, wins, tank treads, spider legs... and that's just for movement. There's also about 5 weapon types, shield configurations, and radar equipment like jammers or receivers, and you're limited only by what you want to make:
Spider legs on an airplane so you can climb up a mountain and fly off? Sure!
Sled skis under a hovercraft so you can get really low to the ground and glide directly on the ground? Why not?
Wheels on your helicopter, thruster jets on your tank, immobile gunboxes that sit there and hopefully shoot first, you get to make your own vehicle.
There are still cheaters around; it's not rare to see a railgun user aim at you through cover from impossibly far across the map when he couldn't see you if you were lit up like a disco ball. Some of them even shoot you through mountains. Hopefully they get banned, or murdered in their sleep, whichever comes first.
There's literally no reason not to try this game, except if you pay for your downloads by the byte, in which case why are you even reading this? Every letter is costing you money stop.
It's early access, and no-one should ever buy anything that is early access, ever, under any circumstance, for any reason. But this one's free. Just download it and try it, already. It's fun, and if it isn't your thing, you've lost nothing.

Robocraft, Well the name is pretty self explanitory, you build robots, Tanks, Flyers, walkers, combinations of all the above, your imagination is the limit.
I've played over 217 hours before writing this review, and honestly I can find no fault with the game, yes there are some cons, and I'll list those in a bit, but for the most part this game is definitely top notch especially for an alpha.
With that said:
Pros:
~ Build your own comabt mechs (Even Healers).
~ Balance is good, their are no unfair combinations, the CPU requires you to sacrifice tank for damage and vice versa is different amounts depending on your desires. You can basically tweak your bot to do whatever you want.
~ Balanced Leveling system - Levels are aquired through kills, Heals, and Damage, The tech path determs which rank your bot fights in, the higher the rank of your bot the better gear you can get. You get higher ranks by equiping better gear you can unlock from the tech tree with token you earn from combat.
~ Balanced Matchmaking - Tech Tiers are seperated by your robots ranking, So you'll never face a robot that completely dominates you because of gear or parts (Unless you do a challenge battle which reward a TON of money and tech points).
~ Plenty of different game Modes, (With more to be added from what I hear).
1. Chalenge Mode - A mode where 4 Higher tier bots face off against 10 Lower tier bots, the tiers are usually 2-4 apart. A Challenge, but not impossible to win on either side.
2. Mega Bot - 1 Huge, High damage Player Bot vs 10 Other Players.
3. Normal and Ranked - Normal matches with Occasional high reward ranked matches.
4. More on the way.
~ The tech tree - Plenty of Options,
1. Weapons - Plasma Cannons (Artillary), SMGs (Pulse Lasers), Rails (Snipers), Disrupters (Dammage Over Time and Heal Over Time).
2. Armor - Too many to list, Lets just say you have  tons of options in armor types, including plateing which can give your bot cool looks as well as shields.
3. Miscilanious stuff, like thrusters, wings, radars, jammers, all kinds of stuff.
There are literally 100's of items, and infinite combinations for Bots.
~ F2P - The only thing you can buy are premade Bots (Nothing over Rank 7), and Premium (Which basically is like a sub that gives you 100% bonus to earned RP (Money) and Tech points, which in Moeny is less then 10$ a moth (It's actually like 6.45$ or something for 30 days of premium).
Con's:
Honestly I had to rack my brain to figure out what to put here. But I would say perhaps some PVE could be added, maybe a story line, Open world, and some other stuff.
I can't honestly think of anything negative to say about the game. and haveing played it for over 200 Hours I have encounted 0 issues (even though it's in alpha) I mean yea theres the occasional (And I mean only like once or twice a day occasional) DC, Bug, and Server instability, but I don't really count that as a "Con", with it being an Alpha, I count it as "Expected".
I would 100% recomend this game to anyone who loves creating their own stuff from nothing,a nd useing it to fight other people in matches. So if your creative, Intelligent, and enjoy the ability to mold your fighting machine to your standards, and your designs (Entirely with very little limitations). This is the game for you.

This game is not currently for you if you are looking for a non hostile and fair environment to learn the game in. For some, to me inexplicable reason the designers decided it would be a wonderful idea to have a very freeform construction system without any real limits apart from total "build points" invested. Which means that it is incredibly commonplace to see veteran players with Tier 5 railguns or plasma cannons to strap them unto 4 blocks and a driver's seat and be admitted into tier 1 where they proceed to one shot whatever contraption newbies come up with with their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tier 1 blocks. In turn killing them is difficult because they are such small targets and all you have is horrendously inaccurate SMGs which have practically no chance of actually destroying these seal clubbers before you get obliterated in one shot.
This issue has been raised multiple times on their forums since forever and it's pretty clear at this point that it's not going to change. So if you're not interested in getting stomped over and over and over while you try to grind out your crappy modules for gods know how many hours then I'd avoid it.
Think World of Tanks levels of newbie hate... but about 10 times as bad.
The building aspect is really interesting and fun and apparently gets really good at the higher tiers with decent balancing between bot types and such.
So if you have the stomach to grind a few dozen hours to get there, you'll enjoy yourself but until then you'll just suffer in seal clubbing hell.
Recommendation:
Try it out... it's free after all but be prepared for lots of bugs, net code related issues, a third party anti cheat program and of course the above mentioned overtiering problems.

Before I start I wanna say that I found this game fun for about 2 hours after that It got tedious and boring to me.But I still recommend you try it out for yourself.
Alright , lets talk about one of the main aspects...
Building.
There are things I like ,but for the most part building in this game is a pain between the butt crack.
You can access building parts fast , but placing the blocks , one by one is just soooo boring.
I like the choice of go heavy and slow or go fast but less defensive.
There are alot of blocks to work with , but if you are a newbie and you want the most badass machine ever, sorry to crush your dreams but that ain't gonna happen because the amount of weapons , blocks and other movement and special things are limited to a certain amount. The more you play or pay the more you can place . Also with that in mind most of the blocks in the start of the game are very ...plain. You have to play alot to make the game interesting.
Alright let's talk about another thing.
Battleing.
There are a good amount of weapon choices , but like I said its gonna take alot of time to get them.
Basiclly if you are a sniper , you aim , you shoot and when someone comes you run. Do that till' you die.
If you just going ham and sham and going tank then press W and shoot and the general direction that the enemy is at.
If you are flying , well then just ....fly (and shoot in the general direction).
Most of the things I have said have been negative, but in general the game is not as bad as you think . I mean seriously thought It was gonna be as bad as Rambo : The video game. But It was suprisingly good.
Try it out for yourself , it doesn't take long to install and its probably worth the 2 hours.

Finally an early access game that i can fully reccomend.
the only part of early access you feel is that the servers have problems once in a while and sometimes you freeze or crash. but at least to me those things happen only rarely, however if they happen its usually in phases of the devs trying to get the server back up for 2 days. otherwise it already plays like a full game. though sometimes when they bring out a big patch there are a couple of glitches and general issues with the new stuff. but never for long.
what do you do?
well you unlock parts for your robots with experience that you gain through battles and buy them with money that you also gain in battles. at higher levels you get more and more different parts and get more and more creative. what I really love about this is, that its really up to you how effective the bot you build will perfom in battle. I for example cant build flying robots for♥♥♥♥♥♥but wreck things greatly in my land based robots.
so is it pay to win?
aw hell no. the things you can only buy with the real money currency are all cosmetic and have absolutely no effect on the outcome of the battle, unless I dont know, you disctract your opponent with your shinyness or something. all robots avaivable for cash are just pre-built and can be built all by yourself with in-game money.
And now most importantly: the updates.
this is really the main reason why I reccomend this game
every other month or so they bring out another huge update that adds even more parts to your selection and at the rate at which this is going I cant wait to see the huge selection you will have once this is released. And they actually listen to their players.
They removed repair costs! I cant stress enough how important this is. repair costs are a major reason people buy premium accounts in other games, meaning a reliable source of income without being to much pay to win to attract free players. but the players didnt like the repair costs so they just removed them. I mean that really is an honorable attitude. speaking of premium, there was also an update where they didnt just double the reward for preimum users, but also give 5% extra cash and Xp to EVERY player in the battle for EVERY premium user. so if there is a lot of those you might actually get a bonus as big as a premium user without ever paying anything. they also give away free premium days rather frequently.
to sum it up:
great fun, great devs, great game

The 99% positive reviews are probably enough to convince you to get this game, but if you still have your doubts then maybe this review will help you.
Portal 2 is a great experience, however, not everyone may enjoy it, or feel it was worth buying.
The game, like Portal, is entirely puzzles. You get your portal device, make portals, and find a way to get past to the next area. I liked that the game had a very smooth and nice introduction to the concept of the game. All the mechanics were taught in a challenging, meaningful and consequently, entertaining way.
The gameplay was very enjoyable. Portal 2 offers much more levels, and therefore, hours of gameplay. This said, the level of challenge Portal 2 offers is much greater. The game introduces several new mechanics, which make the gameplay evermore interesting. Aside from these, you get a smooth soundtrack that enhances the atmosphere of the game. Another great aspect of the game was the co-op mode. The multiplayer in this game, I must praise. Brilliant. It is a legit idea to buy a 2-pack, simply for the sake of playing the co-op with a friend. The co-op feature alone is a good enough reason to get the game. It feels very rewarding to complete series of levels with a friend.
Now with a highly praised gameplay by critics, and 99% positive review rating from the steam community, you would assume the game has no bad points right? No? Well, I personally feel it does have a minor one.
Story. Some people may not even care about this, but I do. I really enjoyed Portal, and enjoyed narrative of the game. Portal 2 obviously continues from where you left off, but sadly, the actual story wasn't so engrossing. I liked the characters, GLaDOS and Wheatley (great voice acting!) but for the most part of the single player mode, I did not care for what you were supposed to do. There is no clear direction or purpose, and it felt like just random story elements were added for the heck of it. I couldn't fully appreciate this aspect of the game.
Conclusion
With the vast amount of content available from community contributions, along with the map creation feature, you cannot get enough of this game. Though I personally enjoyed the singleplayer mode of Portal better, due to it being shorter and a more constructive narrative, it really is just my preference. Portal 2 is a great game to play first, and there is a great amount of content you can find around the Steam community. Puzzles are much more challenging, but overall feel quite rewarding when solved.
As to why I stated that you may not think it's worth buying, here is why: some people just don't enjoy puzzle games. I have quite a few friends that only have a few hours into this game, and they felt it was boring. I can understand this, and if you felt bored, it may not have been worth paying for. I feel that if you pay the full price just to play for a few hours, just to know you would get bored, then it's not worth it. This said, I would highly recommend waiting for the discount, or purchasing it in a bundle.

To end on a positive note, game is solid. Try to get it the moment it's on sale

Robocraft seems like a very interesting concept with tons of potential. However, right now, the game doesn't seem worth playing. It is in alpha, so that very well could change. Don't take this review as me saying that you shouldn't be interested in this game.
Right now, the game has 2 major problems.
First, balance. As you enter your first few games, you will feel very out-classed. Right now, the matchmaking doesn't seem to distinguish between new players and older players. As a result, older players with their much more powerful weapons will completely decimate you and your hopes of getting far at all in the match. It's not that you suck at building or anything: higher tiered robos are simply too powerful to get past as a lower tiered robo.
There are two solutions to this problem. One is to balance the tiers out, as to make lower tiered robos more competitive against higher tiers. If they did this, matchmaking would be perfectly fine, as long as they keep it reasonable. The other option is to change matchmaking so that lower tiered mechs can't go against too-higher tiered ones.  For either case, they would probably need to implement some sort of averaging system to rate robos based on the various tiers of the parts used on them, as you can mix and match as you please.
The second problem is gameplay. The building part of the game is nice and all, but that means nothing if the game itself is realitively boring. What's the point in building bots if you don't enjoy using them? This isn't to say that driving them around and shooting isn't fun, as it kinda is. It means that the pvp mode is boring. Ignoring the mechs, it boils down to running over to the enemy spawn, hoping you don't die in the process, and hoping that you capture the spawn before the enemy does. That is pretty boring if you ask me. The game needs more and better modes. Scrap capture the spawn and replace it with capture the flag, or maybe have points open up around the map for you to capture. As long as it isn't the 1-cap-to-win thing that the game has currently, it will be a welcome addition.
But at the moment, again, it is an interesting concept that isn't worth getting into yet. Would I suggest it now? No. Would I suggest it later? Possibly. I would suggest to keep an eye out for the game and see if it gets better than it is now. It simply isn't fun yet.

These loot crates give you 4 parts or 8 with premium. depending on how well you did in the match is supposed to affect what comes in the crates. For those not aware of the game : It is a free to play (non-pay-to-win) vehicular warfare game.
You build your tanks, hovers, cars, walkers or planes with 'lego' and fight either in team last man standing (classic mode) or team node capture mode (battle mode). Fights are dynamic based on player availability, and there is Curse voice support adding optional voice chat.
It supports Steam but can run as stand-alone on most Windows systems even without it.

Once logged in you can enter the following code to get a days premium bonus: ROBOMOBA-151204

EDIT: Wow. I didn't think it would happen, but it did. I just don't understand how the game went bad in just a year after my original review. This game used to be fun to play with friends. Or even by yourself. ( I logged 300+ hours on it) Then, the devs turned. They started to slowly push out veteran players for newer players, by forcing updates that just ruined the game. We used to have amazing blocks, which were light, but strong. We used to have great gameplay, which was at some points flawed, but it made it all the much better. We used to be able to build in any color we wanted, WITHOUT PAYING FOR COLORS (seriously? That's the dumbest thing I've ever heard of being implemented into a game). When this game came out, it went from good, to better, to best, and was compared to getting a puppy on christmas day. Now?  Well. I compare it to watching that puppy get hit by a car the first time you take it outside on the same day. To build so many cool creations, just to see the dev's strip them of their creativity by removing armoured blocks, and their color. its just saddening. And now we can't even play with friends if they arent the same rank? Thats just pushing it over the damn line. At this point, I think it's time for all the vets to uninstall the game. Because as far as I know, we're never getting the good old robocraft back.
Think of a game. Where Minecraft, Robots, and a sandbox game are all put together to make one game: Robocraft.
Unlike my expectations, Robocraft has given me 148 hours of playtime AND COUNTING. Robocraft has a friendly user family, and is VERY productive in the delvelopment department, correcting any glitches found by users as quickly as possible, Patching cracks, and ruling hackers out ENTIRELY! They buff/debuff weapons accordingly, making sure everything is equal between each team and class. This game shows Minecraft and Team Fortress mixed together, to create a wide variety of classes to pick from. From the healing medic, all the way to the SMG (an example of heavy), To a Plasma Bomber (Demoman) etc.
I think you get the point. But in case you don't, Imagine Team Fortress. where you can customize your class. I'm not saying robocraft copies Team Fortress. But it is a great example of Robocraft.

Put in a decent amount of time, this game never gets old. If you enjoyed the concept of building, then this is the game to in the very least blow a weekend too. Lots of love goes to Freejam for keeping this game free, as I've paid plenty of money for games with a fraction of it's potential.
The first major thing this game has going for it is it's not pay to win. Yes, you have the option to buy a pre-constructed robot, and can even disassymble for parts, but the only real advantage this gives you is your pFlop being boosted. at level 57 I'm over 1k. I've found that it's a better investment to become "premium" which in turns doubles your resources gained at the end of each fight. This just cuts your unlocking and arming time in half. To me, I've payed the standard $15 per month for many subs to games, and always want to show a bit of appreciation for the designers.
Second is the queues. How many games put you into combat in an average of 8 seconds? The games can be very quick, taking a win from either the enemies base being taken over, or complete annilation of the opposing force. Once your in the third tier, there is even boss battles, and the bosses themselves are us, in higher tier levels! The action can be nonstop, or games of cat and mouse depending on the compostitions of teams.
They did really well staying away from the One Size Fits All builds, in the effect that it's really up to what you wanna make. I've seen some really cool concepts (Mobility Hybrids) and stuff that has made me laugh and cheer. My personal goof-off lately was a floating Creeper head from minecraft that shot twin rockets out it's mouth. More looks then function for sure, but you have 3 bays to make different builds in and can purchase more. The choices you make as you build are really based on two factors: Mobility and Weaponization. Despite all the tears in the chat, the guns are balanced. Don't cry cause you drove your SMG tank full speed into the open and a Railgun (sniper) tickled you. Likewise don't get mad cause while trying to snipe on your Railgun Walker you let a SMG or Plasma (Artillery explosive) get close enough to snuggle you while your gun recharges (Feels like it takes forever, doesn't it? :P ) In the end it's all about what you have fun with.
Bottem line is this game is free, you lose nothing playing it. I personally can't wait to see what FJ comes out with next, and hope they keep the free to play concept balanced like they did here

I like it. Bought 30-day premium (it's like US$4.95) because of how much fun I was having.
- Build your own thing then use it to destroy the things that other players built.
- When you destroy parts of the enemy vehicles, the parts come off. There's sort of a sadistic pleasure in blowing the wings off a plane or shooting the guns off a tank. Nobody actually dies (since it's robots) so you never feel bad about it.
- Easy to get into. Freedom to build a variety of things right from the start.
- Matchmaking is one of the best I've ever seen. You typically get a fair balance of different roles in each match.
- Community is generally friendly, especially considering it's a purely competitive PVP game.
It's a little unfair to write a cons section since the game is still in its very early stages, but I'll list them anyway for the benefit of people who are thinking of trying this game. As of the time of this writing, these are the things I dislike:
- Servers somewhat unstable especially during the weekends. You sometimes get booted off, or maintenance suddenly happens during a match. Also you might not get any credit for some wins.
- You can't have more than one weapon type on your vehicle. This is intentional and is designed so that each robot will have a specific role rather than hybrids, so it isn't something they're going to "fix" or anything. Just thought people should know, which is why I list it as a "con."
- Due to how the blocks fit together, some of the most effective vehicle builds are very ugly. If you wanna make an aesthetically good-looking vehicle (such as modeling it against a real world vehicle), you're usually going to sacrifice a lot of firepower and/or armor to do it.
I'll update as I play and as updates come out.

Portal was a clever little game that managed to surprise with brilliantly innovative gameplay, a memorable villain, and quite a bit of humor. Having always enjoyed the "mysterious organization doing apparently pointless testing on humans"-angle, from the Vault-Tech vaults in Fallout and the Dharma Initiative in LOST, Aperture Science and its apparent custodian, GLaDOS, tickled a nerve with me from the very beginning.
And like all popular games, we got a sequel.
Fans of Valve's games have often made a point of discussion that the company is notorious for NOT making sequels to their games (beyond the 2. installment anyways). Half Life 3, Left for Dead 3 and Portal 3 are all games fans have been requesting for years now, with no announcements that they're even being worked on.
The reason I mention this, is because I think it's a testement to Valves integrity that they refuse to take the easy cash-grab route with their beloved franchises. Portal 2 is most definately a game that both builds upon the first game, keeping what was great about it, and adds enough new content to distinguish itself as something great all on its own.
The prototype of Portal 1 started life as a student-made Half-Life mod, and from those humble beginnings, Portal 2 retains that crazy indie-game feel and ambition whilst also shining with all the polish and production value of a AAA-game. The basic schtick of opening portals to play with 3D-space is complimented by the addition of three different gels that show up mid-game and add new layers to the puzzles. The puzzles range from the easy, introductory ones, to the "what kind of mad genious DESIGNED this sh**?"-variety. Some of the levels had me stumped for quite some time - but they never felt unfair or misleading, and because of that, progress brought with it a wonderful sense of accomplishment.
As I've already said, the story - though somewhat sparse - in Portal 1 was one of my favorite aspects of that game, and Portal 2 expands the mythology tenfolds. The new characters introduced are all engaging, interesting and funny - and GLaDOS remains a wonderfully entertaining, brilliantly executed and perfectly acted character. The graphics look great on my rig, the music is perfect, and the gameplay is brilliant.
With the stupendous backlog of games I have bought but yet to finish (or even "play"), there are only a small handful of games I play again after I've completed them. Portal 2 is one of those games. Maybe because I enjoy the gameplay, maybe because I enjoy the story, or just maybe because I am truly stuck in GLaDOS' compulsion to keep testing.
And I have yet to try my hand at the very promising multiplayer-mode, or look into Steams workshop of player-made content.
So if you haven't already, I wholeheartedly reccommend you try Portal 1 and Portal 2.

This is a game like no other. With its unique blend of building and tps this game tops the rest. Oh, did I mention that its free?
Robocraft is a game about building robots from scratch, adding a range of weapons (from the long range rail cannon to the short but incredibly effective medic gun), and choosing your prefered methord of transport. The game uses a tier based system, each tier being unlocked by adding more and more valuable pieces to your vehicle. "Tiering up" offers you the opportunity to use tier-exclusive tokens to unlock stronger and more powerful weapons, armour and transport.
A range of gamemodes are available for you to compete in with your robot: The standard battle which consists of two sides of robots all of the same tier fighting in a last team standing capture the point gamemode, boss battles which teams low level robots up agaisnt a small amount of high level robots in a battle to the death and a few more added in the most recent update.
That brings me swiftly on to my next point on the extensive amount of work and updates put into this game. The dedication to perfection is clearly evident in robocraft, making it almost impossible to tell that it is in early access. Each update to the game adds brand new things to add to your vehicle and new gamemodes to shape the way you play the game and only further adding to it's extensive replayability.
All in all, this game has a huge amount of advantages from its core gameplay, with the building at heart, to the extremely polished finish. However, like most games there are a few faults. The eventual grinding style that is required to reach the higher levels, though small, can put many off playing this game. Also, the game can be easily played for free, however there is an opportunity to purchase in game credits allowing you to skip tiers and buy superior robots. Because of the overwhelming advantages I am still willing to rate this game an incredibly strong 8.5/10.

It's like your minecraft creations only with wheels and guns. You build your Robo, and then battle on teams and try to capture the enemy base or kill the team. ( Sorry for it being so long.)
---Pros---
-Great game. Can run on most computers. I have a somewhat low grade laptop and it runs fine on 2nd to lowest graphics option.
-Graphics. The graphics are good even on low settings.
-No Lag. The servers have apsolutly no lag.
-Destroying other peoples Robos. It is awesome to watch somones Robo being shot to death block by block.
-Posibilities. Their are so many posibilities for this game. And I hope it becomes a better game with more game modes.
-Money system. To get RP (Robo Points) you need to win a game and get kills. I recamend you dont buy the premium in the lower tiers. It is easy to get an upgraded gun if you play 2-3 games. Things are cheap at low teirs compared to other games. Games take 2-3 minutes to start and finsih so getting 200-300 RP at T2 is pretty easy. Same goses for tech points.,
---Cons---
-WARNING: Do Not Flip. If you flip, you dead. If your not at spawn and you flip over, you will destroyed untill or before you flip over. Fliping back over (by hitting F) takes 10 seconds and you can not shoot or move. And you can get shot by the enemy team. Not fair. And its very easy to flip when going down or up a hill. I really hope this gets fixed because it is annoying and I have died several times to this problem.
-Higher tier players have an advantage. If you die in 2 seconds, it is probibly a higher tier weapon. Very Noticiable.
-Not much else to do besides build your Robo, do ranked every once in a while, and fight untill you reach higher tiers. The good thing, it does not feel like a grind.
Other then that, it is a great and well developed game and I hope it gets even more developed. I know this game is in Early Access and some of the cons may or all of them may change. I look forward for this game to change and develope for it's community and I hope it will not be a disapointment like some other games. This game is simple and easy to run on my "low grade pc." Other then that, It is a great game and i rate it a 9/10. Happy Gaming to all!!!

Okay, this is gonna be a long one.
Robocraft is a captivating game. It combines the best aspects of Minecraft-likes, allowing you to create a vehicle sculpted to your very own specifications, looking, feeling and behaving exactly like you want, and games like Mechwarrior, which feature... Not necessarily slow, but very deliberate vehicular combat, where every move you make counts.
By far the best part of the game is playing with the different parts. If the idea of playing as a dive-bombing rocket plane, a spider-medic that can walk on walls, or playing as a thruster-powered spider tank that can jump 2km at a time sounds appealing to you, you owe it to yourself to at least try the game. My personal favorite was my Helitank, which could use its aerofoils to "switch forms" between a low-flying gunship good against grounded targets and firing down from cliffs, a hovertank that could fly low to the ground for cover-to-cover skirmishing, or a slow, but heavily armored airplane for emergency takedowns of annoying enemy bombers.
I had a lot of fun with it, and I encourage you to play it. However, if you do, I ask you to be wary. The game has 10 'Tiers,' similar to levels in RPGs, and as you Tier up, you get access to more and more tech. You only unlock all the tech (movement parts, weapons, armours, etc.) until you reach Level 7, and even then, only all the variety is available once you reach Level 10, at which point Megabots are available. The problem is, as you Tier up, matches get more and more serious... But players don't. I found at Tier 7, often, the match would be an utter stomp, in one direction or the other. It was usually over in under 3 minutes, with one of the two teams having 10 kills and 0 deaths.
And this wasn't just my team or the other team, this was about a 50/50 split. Because you are reliant on your team - you need your Snipers to take down enemy bombers and countersnipe, you need your bomberes to take down enemy plasma cruisers so your snipers don't get smashed, you need your tanks to take down enemy SMG cruisers and snipers so your bomberse don't get shot down, all the while medics are trying to keep your team able to walk and roll - if even one team member isn't taking things seriously, and decides to roll off on his own and get sniped, or dive-bomb the enemy in the hopes of scoring a single kill (which they often don't),♥♥♥♥♥♥just hits the fan and your team falls apart. Often it isn't even a single player that does this, it's 3 or 4. At this point, neither victory or defeat are fulfilling because you feel like every match is the same. Spawn, move with the largest group of teammates, either destroy or be destroyed, usually in an overwhelming charge on either part of your team or theirs.
Because of this, it comes down to luck-of-the-draw. Who has the best, or not even the best, but the most serious players. And, that may sound great and all to you more hardcore gamers... But the closest you can come to deciding your team composition is playing in a 3 (4 if you're Premium)-man platoon. In 10-player matches. There are no custom games. So, as a result, I left after I felt that the game was no longer fun for me. Before I left, I actually dropped down from Tier 7 to Tier 3, just to see if my suspicions about the game becoming "too serious" were right, and they were - Tier 3 matches were far longer, had more variety (despite less tech being available), and usually were less predictable overall.
So gamer be warned, this game is fun... At first... But it quickly becomes weighed down by poor balance and heavy teamplay in the face of a blind matchmaking system.

Just any other Free to Play game, you should pick this up for an hour and give it an open-minded go.
In this game you build a tiny vehicle (I say vehicle, because robots do not require a pilot, because it is esstentially it's own pilot, but vehiclecraft doesn't sound as good, so I'll call it a robo) and then fight using it against other players who have built their own robot.
You can build whatever you want. If you have the parts, it can be made. I've seen people make literal spider walkers (are usually seen in challenge mode or late into the game, like 80% into it), an smg car shaped like a person, a heavily armored box car, a car only describable as a quad from dune 2000, even a flying♥♥♥♥♥♥♥that one time.
You can make jets, hovercrafts, "drones", actual drones, helicopters, tanks, cars, and you can get to the end of the game's current progression to make gigantic versions of these where you can either pit it against tons of smaller, weaker enemies, or fight in a battle filled with giant robos!
I have only gotten 27% into the game, Tier 3, but already I can make hovercraft, cars, tanks, hybrids of either of those and stuff.
There are indeed weapons, and they all have their own uses and strengths and ways of using them. Indeed, this isn't call of Duty where tons of weapons exist, but all of them in a category all work basically the same.
You've got 4 weapons. SMGs, Plasma Cannons, Railguns, and Nanotech Disruptor which heal allies and deals damage to enemies in a straight beam.
The game abides by physics most of the time, so if your robo is not properly made, then you can expect to find problems, luckily there IS a practice mode that has no penalty or reward, filled with enemies you can test your robo against, some of them potentially player-made (THAT NEEDS TO BE A THING IF NOT! <3)
This game is fun, just... don't get discouraged if some turd with a railgun goes into Tiers 1, 2 or 3. It happens a decent amount even though Tier 5 really should be a cut-off point for tech being below the tier it was meant for (Aka railguns below Tier 4 battles, or Helicopters below Tier 5. Walkers below Tier 7 isn't much of a big deal honestly because they're cool to the point I wished there was a Tier 4 version of them).
you won't be able to make the robo you want to from the get-go (I personally have an obsession for walkers, sometimes bordering on fetish-territory if you throw on some missile launchers and beam cannons onto it xD).
The only real downside to the game is the inability to mix and match weapon types. I suppose it helps for balance reasons, but it'd be cool if you could have two weapons at a time. Though then you could have medic guns on railgun planes, which would be a tad unfair.
Each different item has its purpose and use, th only thing that is really much of an exception are the blocks, but they are instrumental in being tough to destroy as without them... well you're not tough to destroy as the original blocks are free for a reason.
Spoiler: They're garbage above Tier 1.
There's also Electro plates, which are indeed shield technology, but the precursor to it.
Feel free to download this game and give it a try, it's really quite fun! Personally building the robo is my favorite part, let alone actually using it, which is even better.
It's really fun.
I also give this game a 6/10, which says alot for it's current state. There's not alot of bugs left and the devs have taken time and actually tried in their endeavor to make a great game which has probably very little content in comparison to the finished result, and 0 bugs or glitches pretty much.
PS: This game has support for us OCD buggers who have to symmetry everything in the mirror mode. Press X or map the key in the controls menu under "Build"
Happy Building, and Merry Killing!

The cheating that was rampant in the early stages is now basically non-existant, and as with any other shooter, teams that work together are much more effective than people going it alone.

If someone were to ask me what my favourite game was, I'd say Portal 2. I have a handful of games that I hold dear to my heart, but Portal 2 is a gem. It basically took the BRILLIANT concept of Portal and expanded on it. They added quite a few new gameplay mechanics that interact with the portals (that will leave you scratching your head while having a blast messing around with everything), giving it that much more depth.
The characters are perfect. It's a wonderful balance of humour, banter between characters, intellect, sass..without it being too much. It never got annoying or felt like they were pushing a character too hard in an attempt to be funny. I honestly have a soft spot for all the characters and they just make me so
. I get so immersed when playing, getting lost in the puzzles (that aren't too easy, aren't too hard), fantastic dialogue and atmosphere (the scenery is incredible, the littlest details add to the overall dreary tone).
I have beaten this game 7 times I believe, between xbox and an old steam account, and it was always as enjoyable as the time before. It has replay value if you give it 6 months inbetween playing sessions, you forget a lot of the solutions. I wouldn't get stuck often, but it wasn't an instant-robotic-motion of "ok I have to go here, then here, and now this", I still had to think. I found myself laughing at the  jokes and blunt ridicules towards one another,
